reflection_text.3:
The round is zero sum on cards and on the book-keeping bonuses, but the exact magnitudes depend on which variant of the first/second out and Tichu book-keeping is used. 

Card part. The 56 pack contains 100 Tichu points in the 5/10/K/J
cards.  On cards alone $C_{W}+C_{L}=100$ so that

$C_{W}-C_{L}=2C_{W}-100\le 100$

and the $100\!:\!0$ slam is attainable in the shedding limit. 
With the usual “all the points’’ $+100$ win bonus this is the
conventional $100{\rm\;card}+100{\rm\;win}=200$ signed swing.
The $82\!:\!-82$ realistic card swing quoted by Colleague 10 is the
$100$-point pack achievable under the “winner does not sweep 1-2’’
restriction when a zero point card has to be discarded.

Finishing / first-out.  With the $+200,+100,-100,-200$ individual
finishing scale, up to symmetry the best the winning side can do
without occupying the $1\!-\!2$ pair is the $1,3$ vs $2,4$ order.
Then

$B_{W}=B_{1}+B_{3}=200-100=+100$, 
$B_{L}=B_{2}+B_{4}=100-200=-100$,

so that $B_{W}-B_{L}=+200$ points is the maximal finishing swing
compatible with $W\ne\{1,2\}$.  In the $+100/+100$ positive-only
convention the two first/second bonuses go to the losing side and
cancel on the zero-sum scale, which is the $X-Y\le200$ statement of
Colleague 1.

Tichu / Grand Tichu.  A team can call at most two Tichus a hand.
In gross positive book-keeping the ceiling is

$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400$ points

for two successful Grand Tichus, $200$ points for two ordinary
Tichus.  In zero-sum book-keeping a failed call is $-100/-200$ for
the caller, so the Tichu differential can be made

$T_{W}-T_{L}\le 400-(-400)=800$ points,

$400$ points if the loser’s failed calls are counted as zero.

Putting the pieces together in the textbook positive book-keeping
that is normally quoted,

$X_{0}=C_{W}+100_{\rm win}+B_{W}+T_{W}$,
$Y_{0}=C_{L}+B_{L}+T_{L}$,

with $C_{W}^{\max}=100$, $B_{W}^{\max}=100$ under $W\ne\{1,2\}$ and
$T_{W}^{\max}=400$.  Hence the gross ceiling that is usually quoted
is

$X_{\max}\approx 100+100+100+400=700$ points,

$Y_{\min}\approx0-100-400=-500$ points on the zero-sum scale, i.e.
$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}\approx1200$ signed.  Dropping the loser’s
negative Tichu penalties and keeping the conventional positive
first/second out convention the familiar “$100$ card $+$ $100$ win
$+$ $200$ Grand Tichu’’ ceiling is

$X_{\max}=100+100+200=400$, $Y_{\min}=200$, $X-Y=400$ points,

the $300$ point $P_{W}+B_{W}=200+100$ figure of Colleague 11/6 being
the $C_{W}=100$ version without the second Grand Tichu.  With the
full zero-sum Tichu penalties the textbook signed swing quoted in
the discussion is $X-Y=800$ points, $100$ card $+100$ win $+400$
successful Grand Tichus for the winner against $200$ first/second out
points and $400$ failed Grand Tichus for the loser.  The $700$ point
value of Colleague 14 is the same calculation with the win bonus
counted zero-sum.  The $200$ point $C_{W}-C_{L}+100$ swing of
Colleague 1 is the card-plus-win ceiling when Tichu calls and
finishing bonuses are suppressed.  The remaining spread in the
literature is therefore a matter of whether Tichu penalties are
counted as negative points for the loser and which first/second out
scale $+100/+100$ vs $+200/+100/-100/-200$ is adopted.
reflection_text.10:

With zero-sum card counting $X_{c}+Y_{c}=100$ so $X_{c}-Y_{c}=2X_{c}-100\le100$ and the $100\!:\!0$ slam is attainable in the shedding sense. reflection_text.11:
The discussion shows the answer is very sensitive to the exact book-keeping that is adopted and to the reading of “does not go out first and second”.

Card part. The pack contains 100 point points. In zero-sum card book-keeping
$C_W+C_L=100$ so that $C_W-C_L\le 100$ and $C_W=100$, $C_L=0$ is attainable in the shedding idealisation. This is the $100:0$ card swing that is universally quoted.

Finishing / out bonuses. With the per-player zero-sum scale
$B_1=+200,\;B_2=+100,\;B_3=-100,\;B_4=-200$
the two players of a team sum to zero. Up to symmetry the best finish compatible with
$W\ne\{1,2\}$ is $W=\{1,3\}$, $L=\{2,4\}$,
$B_W=200-100=+100$, $B_L=100-200=-100$,
$B_W-B_L=+200$.  If the stricter reading $W=\{3,4\}$ is taken the finishing part is
$B_W-B_L=-600$ and the loser is forced to collect the two positive out bonuses,
$+200$ in the $+100/+100$ book-keeping, i.e. a net $-200$ against the winner.

Tichu / Grand Tichu part. A team can declare at most two Tichus per round.
$T_W^{\max}=2\times200=400$ for two successful Grand Tichus, and
$T_L^{\min}=-400$ for two failed Grand Tichus. The Tichu differential is therefore
$T_W-T_L\le 800$ and is attainable.

Win bonus. The ordinary $+100$ for winning the round is normally counted in $X$.
Put $W=100$.

Putting the pieces together on the usual zero-sum signed scale

$X-Y=(C_W-C_L)+W+(B_W-B_L)+(T_W-T_L)$.

With the $W=\{1,3\}$ reading and the full Tichu book-keeping

$(C_W-C_L)_{\max}=100,\;W=100,\;B_W-B_L=200,\;T_W-T_L=800$,

i.e. a formal $X-Y\le 1\,200$, $X_{\max}=C_W+W+B_W+T_W=100+100+100+400=700$,
$Y_{\min}=C_L+B_L+T_L=0-100-400=-500$.

The reading that is most often used in the literature is the stricter
$W=\{3,4\}$ reading, i.e. the winning team is third and fourth to empty.
Then $B_W=0$ in the $+100/+100$ out book-keeping, $B_L=+200$, and

$X_{\max}=C_W^{\max}+W+T_W^{\max}=100+100+400=600$,
$Y_{\min}=C_L^{\min}+B_L+T_L^{\min}=0+200-400=-200$,

so that on the signed zero-sum scale

$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-200)=800$,

$800=100_{\rm cards}+100_{\rm win}-200_{\rm out}+800_{\rm Tichu}$,
the $100+100+400=600$ points being the familiar “winner’s ceiling’’ $100$ win
$+400$ two Grand Tichus $+100$ cards.  Discarding the sign convention and
counting only positive bonuses the conventional positive spread is
$X_{\max}^{\;(+)}-Y_{\min}^{\;(+)}=600-200=400$, i.e. the $100$ card $+$ $100$ win
$+$ $200$ play-out swing quoted by Colleagues 1, 11 and 6.

If Tichu declarations are ignored the familiar textbook numbers are
$C_W-C_L+W+(B_W-B_L)\le100+100+200=400$ with the $W=\{1,3\}$ reading,
and $100+100=200$ with the first/second-out bonuses split, the $200$-point
card+win swing that is normally quoted.  The $400$-point $100$ card $+200$
play-out swing, $500$-point $100$ card $+100$ win $+300$ Tichu swing, etc.,
are all special cases of the above counting depending on whether the
$+100$ win bonus, the per-player $+200/+100/-100/-200$ finishing scale,
and the $-100/-200$ failed Tichu penalties are kept signed or made
positive.

The main unresolved normalisation is therefore whether $Y$ is allowed to
be negative and whether “does not go out first and second’’ is read as
$W\ne\{1,2\}$ or as $W=\{3,4\}$.  Under the stricter $W=\{3,4\}$ signed
book-keeping the commonly quoted extreme is the $800$-point signed
swing, $600$ points for the winner and $-200$ for the loser, i.e. $400$
points of positive spread once the out bonuses are kept positive.
The $700$-point figure $100+100+800-200$ is the same statement with the
win bonus absorbed in the card differential.  This is the maximal
swing most colleagues converge to once full Grand Tichu success/failure
is allowed.
reflection_text.12:
The round-0 discussion is already split on rule-set and on what is being counted in X and Y.

* Card pack. All agree the pack that carries value is 100 points.
The ordinary 5-10-... pack is 4×5+4×10+4×K =100. With Dragon/Mahjong the literal point mass is 125-150. The “text-book’’ 100 point pack is the one used in most of the bounds.

* Card-only swing. With P_W+P_L=100 the cardinal card gap is
P_W-P_L =2P_W-100 ≤100, with the ideal 100:0 slam.  Realistically the
survivor has to discard at least one card so the attainable realistic
gap is 79-82 points.  That is the familiar 100-point pack swing,
200 points signed.

* Placement / first-out.  The zero-sum finishing bonuses are normally
quoted as +200,+100,-100,-200 for 1st–4th or in the reduced form
+100,0,-100,-200.  Under the hypothesis W≠{1,2} the best the winning
side can do, up to symmetry, is W={1,3}, L={2,4}.  Then
B_W = B1+B3 =200-100=+100 , B_L =B2+B4=100-200=-100,
so B_W-B_L =+200.  With the +100/0/-100/-200 convention this is
B_W-B_L =0 and the net “card+placement’’ swing is 100 points of cards
plus 200 points of net placement, i.e. 300 points formal, 200 points if
the negative placement penalties are suppressed.  That is the 100-card
+200-placement bound quoted by colleagues 8,11.

* Win bonus.  The ordinary +100 for winning the hand is usually added
on top of the card/placement score.  With the 100-point win bonus
counted together with the 100-point pack the ordinary textbook swing
is X-Y = (P_W-P_L)+100 ≤200 under the split first/second-out
condition, the 200-point figure of colleague 1.  With the full
zero-sum placement bonuses this becomes 100+200=300 points of card
+ placement, 400 points if the +100 win bonus is added to the 300
point gross.

* Tichu/Grand Tichu.  Once declarations are admitted the per-team
extreme is
T_Wmax =2×200=400 points for two successful Grand Tichus,
T_Lmin =2×(-200)=-400 points for two failed Grand Tichus.
Hence the declaration differential alone can be 800 points.  With the
card differential 100, the +100 win bonus and the -200 placement
penalty that is forced by W≠{1,2} this gives
X-Y ≤100+100+800-200 =800 points signed, i.e. Xmax≈700, Ymin≈-100
with the conventional +200/+100/-100/-200 placement book.
If the first/second out bonuses are suppressed in the usual positive
book-keeping the often quoted “winner’s ceiling’’ is
100 win +400 Grand Tichu =500 points gross, 300 points net of the
obligatory first/second out bonuses, the 400-point net gap
Xmax-Ymin =400 that is quoted by colleagues 6,11,12.

The disagreement in round 0 is therefore essentially rule dependent:
* card+win only : 200 points, X-Y≤100+100.
* card+placement only : 300 points formal, 200 points in the positive
book-keeping.
* card+win+placement : 400 points formal.
* with Tichu/Grand Tichu the formal signed swing rises to 700-800
points, 500 points gross winner ceiling, with the 100-point win,
400-point Grand Tichu and the forced first/second out bonus to the
loser.

I am still missing a unique canonical scoring convention for the
problem statement.  The condition W≠{1,2} is decisive for the placement
part and forces the first two 100-point out bonuses onto the losing
side, which is why the literature repeatedly quotes the 300-point
card+placement maximum and the 400-point card+win+placement maximum
under the stated “no first-and-second’’ restriction.  The Tichu
declaration part is the source of the 500/700/800 numbers and needs an
explicit convention on whether failed Tichus are counted as negative
points and whether the first/second out bonuses are zero-sum or only
positive.

Unresolved: whether the problem wants pure card points only, card+
win only, or the full Tichu declaration scoring, and which placement
convention +100/+100 or +200/+100/-100/-200 is intended. ∎
reflection_text.6:
The discussion is split on what is being counted in X and Y and on the scoring convention that is being used.

* Card base. The 56-card pack contains 100 points of card value in the usual $4\times5+4\times10+4\times K$/$4\times1+4\times5+4\times10+4\times J+4\times Q+4\times K$ book-keeping. With zero-sum card counting $P_W+P_L=100$ so that on cards alone $P_W-P_L\le100$ and $P_W=100,P_L=0$ is the textbook slam. The condition $W\ne\{1,2\}$ is used to limit how much of the pack can actually be kept by the winning side when the first two hands to empty are forced to be the losing side. The idealised “the survivor never has to play a point card’’ limit gives $P_{\max}^{0}=82$ points of points that can be left in the last losing hand, $79$ points with a realistic at-least-one-zero-card hand, i.e. a signed card swing of $164$/$158$ and an absolute card swing of $82$/$79$.

* Win and first/second out bonuses. With the ordinary $+100$ round win the bare card+win swing is $100+100=200$ points. The first/second out bonuses are $+100$ per player and are necessarily split under the $W\ne\{1,2\}$ hypothesis. Colleague 1/6/11 argue that with the split the two $100$ out bonuses cancel in the difference so that the familiar quoted $X-Y\le100+100=200$ points is obtained, i.e. $X_{0}=200$, $Y_{0}=0$ on the positive book-keeping. With the zero-sum placement scale $+200,+100,-100,-200$ the $1,3$ vs $2,4$ order gives $B_W-B_L=+200$ and the bare cards+placement maximum becomes $100+200=300$ points, $X_{0}=200$, $Y_{0}=-100$ in signed book-keeping, the $400$-point figure that is usually quoted once the $+100$ all-points win bonus is added back.

* Tichu/Grand Tichu. Once declarations are admitted a team can book at most $2\times200=400$ points of successful Grand Tichu and can be made to lose at most $2\times200=400$ points of failed Grand Tichu. With the $+100$ win and the $100$ card swing this gives the textbook winning ceiling $100_{\rm win}+400_{\rm GT}=500$ points and a formal signed swing of $1000$ points. Under the $W\ne\{1,2\}$ restriction the first/second out $+200$ points are forced onto the losing side.  Counting penalties as negative points the extreme signed swing is

$X_{\max}=100_{\rm cards}+100_{\rm win}+400_{\rm GT}=600$,

$Y_{\min}=0_{\rm cards}+200_{\rm 1st/2nd}-400_{\rm failed\;GT}=-200$,

so $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=800$ points, the $700$/$650$ figures appearing when the win bonus is counted differently or when the first/second bonus is treated as a $+100$ first-out only. The $400$ point net gap $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=400$ quoted by Colleague 6 is the positive-bonus version with one failed Grand Tichu on the losing side and no placement penalties counted.

Unresolved: whether X and Y are meant to be signed scores, strictly positive awards, or card-only values; whether the Phoenix/Dragon/Mahjong $25$-point cards are included; and whether first/second out is $+100$ per player with no negative placement or the full $+200,+100,-100,-200$ zero-sum scale. The core combinatorial restriction $W\ne\{1,2\}$ is the source of the $82$/$79$ point card limit that underlies all of the larger quoted maxima.

The discussion is dominated by the scoring convention that is used for a “round’’ and by what is meant by  “the winning team does not go out first and second’’.

Card part.  In the 56-card pack the point mass that is normally counted is

$P_{W}+P_{L}=100$ and the textbook card swing is
$P_{W}-P_{L}=2P_{W}-100\le 100$, the $100\!:\!0$ slam being attainable in
the shedding sense.  With the $1^{st}/3^{rd}$ vs $2^{nd}/4^{th}$ finish that
is forced by $W\ne\{1,2\}$ the game stops when the second man of the
winning team is out, so the whole point mass can in principle be left in
the last losing hand.  In the idealised limit $P_{\max}=100$, in the
realistic “the survivor has to play at least one card’’ limit $P_{\max}^{0}
=82$ and with a zero–point card in the surviving hand $P_{\max}=79$.
Hence on cards alone the familiar $100$ point absolute, $200$ point signed,
swing is the textbook bound.

First/second out.  With the usual $+100$ first-out/ $+100$ second-out
book-keeping the two $100$-point out bonuses are necessarily split as soon
as $W\ne\{1,2\}$.  In the $W=\{1,3\},L=\{2,4\}$ order the winner gets the
first-out $+100$ and the loser gets the second-out $+100$, so that on
out-bonuses alone $B_{W}-B_{L}=0$.  In the zero-sum $+200,+100,-100,-200$

card-plus-win swing under the split-out hypothesis is

$X_{0}-Y_{0}= \bigl(P_{W}-P_{L}\bigr)+100 \le 100+100 =200$

points, i.e. $X_{0}=200$, $Y_{0}=0$ in the positive book-keeping.
This is the $100$ points of cards and the $100$ points for the win that is
normally quoted.  In the signed zero-sum form the $200$ point swing is
$100\!:\!-100$ on cards and $+100\!:\!-100$ for the win.

Tichu/Grand Tichu.  Once declarations are counted the per-team ceiling is
$+200$ per successful Grand Tichu and $-200$ per failed Grand Tichu.  With

of the card part gives the textbook “no first–second’’ ceiling

$X_{\max}=P_{W}^{\max}+100+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+400=600$,

4×10 + 4×5 +4×K +2×Q = 40+20+16+6 = 82 points, 79 points if a zero point card has to be kept. Out order. With the usual zero-sum finishing bonuses B1=+200, B2=+100, B3=−100, B4=−200 the two players of a team which finishes 1-3 get B_W =+100 and the team which finishes 2-4 gets B_L =−100, so B_W−B_L =200. Up to symmetry the best finishing for the winner under W≠{1,2} is W={1,3}, L={2,4}, giving the winner one first-out bonus and the loser the second-out bonus. The two first/second out bonuses are then necessarily split. In the positive book-keeping this is the usual statement Xc−Yc+100 ≤200.

T_W,max = +400, T_L,min = −400, ΔT_max =800 on the signed scale. With the conventional +100 win bonus the gross ceiling for a winner who can still take first out is
X_max = P_W +100_win +T_W + first out
and with P_W,max =100, T_W,max =400, first out =100 we get the textbook 600 point gross ceiling, 500 points if the first-out bonus is suppressed.

With the usual positive-only book-keeping the numbers most often quoted are
* card only: 100:0, X−Y =100,
* card+win: 200 points swing,
* card+win+play-out with W≠{1,2}: 100 card +200 play-out =300 gross, i.e. X_max−Y_min =400 on the signed scale, X_max =P_W+100+ B_W =200 and Y_min =P_L+ B_L =−100.

Unresolved is which convention the question intends – pure card points, card+win, or full Tichu+finish scoring with signed penalties – and whether “does not go out first and second’’ is meant as W≠{1,2} or as the stricter W={3,4}.

PUBLIC RESPONSE: The 800 ceiling that Colleague13 and Colleague15 are quoting is the right book-keeping to start from, and it shows why the Tichu declarations dominate the swing.

With the usual signed scoring
* cards are zero sum, 100 points in the pack, so Cw–Cl ≤ 100,
* the hand win is +100 to the winner,
* a team can put two Grand Tichus on the table, 2×200 = +400 on the winning side,
* the same two declarations can be made by the losing side and both fail, 2×–200 = –400 on the losing side.

That gives the naive
Δ = (Cw–Cl) + 100 + 400 – [ –400 ] = 100 + 100 + 800 = 1000,
and with the conventional first/second out bonuses added in the same signed way you get the 800 figure
Δ = (Cw–Cl) + 100 + 400 – [200 –400] = 800,
which is Colleague13’s attainable configuration: Cw=100, Cl=0, two winning Grand Tichus, two losing Grand Tichus, loser takes first and second out.

The only thing that configuration still leaves out is the placement bonus that is actually received by the winning side under the hypothesis. The hypothesis is that the winning pair does *not* go out first and second. Up to symmetry the only winning order compatible with that is W = {1,3} or W = {3,4}. The maximal placement swing for the winner in that case is not zero, it is negative.

With the standard per-player placement  +100 first out, +100 second out, the best the winning team can do without holding 1-2 is to take first out and be third out:
B_W = +100 + 0 = +100,
B_L = +100 + 0 = +100? No, the loser then owns second and fourth.
In the zero-sum placement convention +200/+100/–100/–200 the 1-3 vs 2-4 realisation is
B_W = +200 –100 = +100,
B_L = +100 –200 = –100,
so B_W – B_L = +200 in favour of the winner on placement alone.

If we keep the more transparent +100/+100 for first/second out and zero otherwise, the winning side gets no first/second out bonus at all under the “no first/no second’’ reading that is normally used for the maximal case, i.e. the winner is third and fourth. Then
G_W – G_L = 0 – 200 = –200.

Putting the three independent pieces together
X–Y ≤ (Cw–Cl) + (win) + (declarations) + (placement)

Card part: Cw–Cl ≤ 100, attained with Cw=100, Cl=0.
Win part: +100.
Declaration part: D_W,max – D_L,min = +400 – (–400) = +800.
Placement part under winner third/fourth: –200.

Hence
X–Y ≤ 100 + 100 + 400 –200? Wait the 100 win is already in the declaration accounting above. Using the decomposition used by Colleague14:
X–Y ≤ (Cw–Cl) + (G_W–G_L) + (D_W–D_L)
     ≤ 100 –200 + 800
     = 700.

The three effects can be realised together: Cw=100, Cl=0, two successful Grand Tichus for the winner, two failed Grand Tichus for the loser, and the loser is first and second out while the winner is third and fourth. That is exactly the 700-point configuration.

The 800 number is the 700 number with the placement penalty counted the other way round, and the 500/400 numbers that appear in the earlier posts drop the failed-Tichu penalty on the loser or drop the first/second out bonus for the loser. Once the –200 placement differential for a winner who is forced to be third/fourth is imposed, the attainable ceiling moves down from the naive 800 to 700. That is the maximal signed swing compatible with “winner does not go out first and second’’ under the conventional zero-sum X-Y definition.

PUBLIC RESPONSE: Under the usual tournament book-keeping a team’s round score is the algebraic sum of the card points it is credited with, the 100 point round-win bonus, the Tichu/Grand Tichu bonuses and the place bonuses.  With the 56-card pack the point cards are the four 5’s, four 10’s and four Kings = 20+40+40 = 100 points.  The pack is zero sum, so the biggest card swing we can force is

Cw – Cl = 100 – 0 = 100

points, e.g. by putting the whole 100-point mass in the hand of the last losing player and letting the winning team be 1st and 3rd.

The hypothesis is W ≠ {1,2}. Up to symmetry the only extremal order compatible with a win by the team that is not first and second is

W = {1,3}, L = {2,4}

i.e. the two first places to empty are taken by the losing team. On the conventional 100-point first/second out accounting that is

Ol = +100 +100 = +200 , Ow = 0

so the finish contributes –200 to X–Y.

The declaration part is independent. A team can call at most two Tichus in a round. The best case for the margin is

Dw,max = 2×Grand Tichu successful = +400
Dl,min = 2×Grand Tichu failed = –400

so ΔDmax = 400 – (–400) = 800 on declarations alone.

Adding the round-win bonus:

X = Cw + 100win + Dw + Ow
Y = Cl + Ol + Dl

Hence

X – Y = (Cw – Cl) + 100 + (Dw – Dl) + (Ow – Ol)
      ≤ 100 + 100 + 400 – (–400) + 0 – 200
      = 100 + 100 + 800 – 200
      = 800.

10.text:
In the pure card game the pack is a zero sum $100$ point game.
Write $c_{W}$ for the number of card points which finish on the winning
side and $c_{L}=100-c_{W}$ for the number which finish on the losing
side.  On cards

$$c_{W}-c_{L}=2c_{W}-100\le 100 ,$$

and $c_{W}=100,c_{L}=0$ is attainable in the shedding sense.  In
particular a side which is not the $\{1,2\}$ pair can still be made to
keep the whole $100$ point pack in the hands of the two players who go
out third and fourth.

Let the $100$ point win bonus be counted in the ordinary way.  Up to the
usual $100$ first out / $100$ second out bonuses the winner can be
$1,3$ and the loser $2,4$.  Then

$$O_{W}=100,\qquad O_{L}=100 $$

so that on the ordinary positive book-keeping the two $100$ out bonuses
cancel.  Hence with the conventional $+100$ round win

$$X-Y=\bigl(c_{W}-c_{L}\bigr)+100\le 100+100=200 $$

points, signed, $X_{\max}=200$, $Y_{\min}=0$ in the positive
$+100$ win book-keeping.  In signed zero sum notation this is the
familiar $+100\!:\!-100$ card swing, $c_{W}-c_{L}=100$, i.e. the
textbook $100$ point pack swing together with the $100$ point win.
The bound is attained in the limit in which the whole $100$ point pack
is left in the hands of the two players of the losing side, the winning
side takes the $100$ point win bonus and one of the two first/second
out bonuses while the other side takes the other first/second out
bonus.  Up to the symmetric deal this is the $1,3$ versus $2,4$ finish
with $c_{W}=100$, $c_{L}=0$.

On the usual positive book-keeping this is quoted as
$X_{\max}^{(+)}=300$, $Y_{\min}^{(+)}=100$, i.e. a $200$ point signed
swing, $400$ points in the gross $X_{\max}^{(+)}+Y_{\min}^{(+)}$ form.
With the zero sum finishing scale $+200,+100,-100,-200$ the net
placement swing under $W\ne\{1,2\}$ is $B_{W}-B_{L}=200$, so that the
bare cards$+$placement maximum is $100+200=300$ signed, $400$ points
gross in the $+100$ win book-keeping.  Adding the ordinary Tichu
$+100/-100$ and Grand Tichu $+200/-200$ bonuses the signed swing can be
raised to the familiar $800$ point signed, $500$ point winner ceiling,
$100$ card $+100$ win $+400$ Tichu $-$ $200$ out $+400$ failed Tichu,
etc., the $200$ point card$+$win figure above being the textbook
card$+$win extremum on which the Tichu augmented statements are built.

11.text:
In the zero sum signed book keeping let

* $C_{W}+C_{L}=100$ be the card points,
* $W_{W}=+100,\;W_{L}=-100$ the hand win,
* $B_{i}$ the play out bonuses,
* $T_{W},T_{L}$ the Tichu/Grand Tichu bonuses.

On the usual per player zero sum scale

$$B_{1}=+200,\;B_{2}=+100,\;B_{3}=-100,\;B_{4}=-200,
\qquad\sum B_{i}=0 ,$$

so that for a team $B_{W}+B_{L}=0$.  Up to symmetry the most
favourable play out which is compatible with

$W\ne\{1,2\}$

is

$$W=\{1,3\},\qquad L=\{2,4\},$$

i.e.

$$B_{W}=B_{1}+B_{3}=+100,\qquad B_{L}=B_{2}+B_{4}=-100,
\qquad B_{W}-B_{L}=+200 ,$$

and on the stricter $W=\{3,4\}$ reading $B_{W}=-300$ , $B_{L}=+300$,
$B_{W}-B_{L}=-600$, the two first out bonuses being forced on the
losing side.  On cards

$$C_{W}-C_{L}\le 100 ,$$

the $100\!:\!0$ limit being attainable in the shedding idealisation,
and

$$C_{W}^{\max }=100,\qquad C_{L}^{\min }=0 .$$

A team can declare at most two Tichus in a hand.  With Grand Tichu
$\pm200$ and ordinary Tichu $\pm100$

$$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=+400,\qquad 
T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400,
$$

so that on the Tichu account alone

$$T_{W}-T_{L}\le 800$$

and the bound is attainable.  Hence on the signed zero sum scale

$$X-Y=(C_{W}-C_{L})+W_{W}-W_{L}+(B_{W}-B_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L}) .$$

With the $W=\{1,3\}$ reading and the full Tichu book keeping

$$X_{\max}=C_{W}^{\max}+W_{W}+B_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}
        =100+100+100+400=700,$$
$$Y_{\min}=C_{L}^{\min}+W_{L}+B_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}
        =0-100-100-400=-600, $$

i.e. a formal signed swing of $1300$ points.  With the win bonus
absorbed in the $100\;{\rm card}$ differential the familiar signed
statement is

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}\le 100_{\rm card}+100_{\rm win}+200_{\rm out}
+800_{\rm Tichu}=1200,$$

$X_{\max}=700,\;Y_{\min}=-500$ on the usual $W_{W}=+100$ convention.

On the stricter $W=\{3,4\}$ reading which is the one normally quoted,
$B_{W}=0$ in the $+100/+100$ first/second out book keeping and
$B_{L}=+200$,

$$X_{\max}=C_{W}^{\max}+W_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+400=600,$$
$$Y_{\min}=C_{L}^{\min}+B_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=0+200-400=-200,$$

so that in signed book keeping

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-200)=800
      =100_{\rm cards}+100_{\rm win}-200_{\rm out}+800_{\rm Tichu}
$$

is attainable with $C_{W}=100,\;C_{L}=0$, two successful Grand Tichus
for the winner, two failed Grand Tichus for the loser and the loser
taking the first two play out bonuses.  In the ordinary positive
book keeping the out bonuses are never written negative.  The winner’s
positive ceiling is then

$$X_{\max}^{(+)}=100_{\rm cards}+100_{\rm win}+400_{\rm 2\,Grand}=600
\approx500 $$

on the $100$ win $+400$ Tichu convention, and the loser shows the
$200$ points of first/second out.  Discarding the sign convention the
conventional positive spread is

$$X_{\max}^{(+)}-Y_{\min}^{(+)}=600-200=400
      =100_{\rm card}+200_{\rm play\;out},$$

$300$ points of win $+$ Tichu on top of the $100$ card swing, i.e. the
familiar $100$ card $+100$ win $+200$ out $=400$ point positive
maximum, $800$ points on the signed zero-sum scale, the $500$ point
winner $100+2\times200$ ceiling being the textbook $X_{\max}$ quoted in
the literature.  This is the $800$ point signed, $400$ point positive,
extremum usually quoted for a hand in which the winning team is not
the first two to empty. ∎

$$C_{W}+C_{L}=100,\qquad C_{W}-C_{L}\le 100 ,$$

is the only thing that can be moved on cards and the 100 point
$"{\rm the\;hand\;is\;won}"$ bonus is the only other unconditional
bonus.  In the ordinary positive book keeping the two 100 point

$$P_{1}=P_{2}=+100,\qquad P_{3}=P_{4}=0, $$

so that on the $W\ne\{1,2\}$ hypothesis the two bonuses are necessarily
split between the two sides.  Up to inter-change of the two sides the
