so that the placement part cancels in the difference.  With the
customary $+100$ all- points bonus the score which can be shown on the
board is

$$X =C_{W}+100_{{\rm win}}+P_{W}+T_{W},\qquad 
Y =C_{L}+P_{L}+T_{L}, $$

where $T_{W},T_{L}\ge 0$ are the Tichu bonuses which are actually made.
In particular

$$X_{c}=C_{W}+100_{{\rm win}}\le 200,\qquad
X_{c}-Y_{c}=C_{W}-C_{L}+100\le200, $$

the $200$ point $100$ card $+$ $100$ win swing, and the $100$ point
card swing $C_{W}-C_{L}\le100$ being attained for $C_{W}=100$, $C_{L}=0$.
This is the $X_{c}=200$, $Y_{c}=0$ $200$ point pure card $+$ win
statement, $X_{c}-Y_{c}=200$, i.e. $100\!:\!-100$ in signed zero sum
notation, and it is the $100$ point pack swing which is normally quoted
once the $100\!-\!100$ first/second out split is removed.

If the Tichu declarations are counted in the ordinary positive
book-keeping the largest bonus which can be booked on a winning hand is

$$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200_{{\rm Grand}}=400\;{\rm pts},$$

and it can be booked together with $C_{W}=100$ and the $100$ point win
bonus.  With the $1,3\;{\rm vs}\;2,4$ finishing order which is the best
possible under $W\ne\{1,2\}$

$$P_{W}=100,\qquad P_{L}=100, $$

so that in the usual $+100$ first/second out book-keeping

$$X_{\max}=C_{W}^{\max}+100_{{\rm win}}+P_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}
        =100+100+100+400=700,$$
$$Y_{\min }^{(+)}=C_{L}^{\min}+P_{L}=0+100=100,$$

and the net positive spread which can be shown on the board is

$$X_{\max }^{(+)}-Y_{\min }^{(+)}
      =C_{W}^{\max}-C_{L}^{\min}+100_{{\rm win}}+T_{W}^{\max}
      =100+100+400=600, $$

$100$ points of which is the compulsory first out bonus which the loser
is forced to pick up.  Removing the compulsory $100$ first/second out
money the familiar textbook figure is

$$X_{0}=C_{W}^{\max}+100_{{\rm win}}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+400=600
\;\;\Longleftrightarrow\;\;
X_{0}^{\rm net}=300,$$

i.e. $100$ points of cards, $100$ points for the win and $200$ points
for one successful Grand Tichu, the second Grand Tichu being the
second player of the team.  In the $+100$ all-points book keeping the
conventional clean statement is

$$X_{\max}=300,\qquad Y_{\min}=0,\qquad X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=300, $$

and with the first/second out bonuses counted in the zero sum
$+200,+100,-100,-200$ convention

$$B_{W}=B_{1}+B_{3}=+100,\qquad B_{L}=B_{2}+B_{4}=-100,
\qquad B_{W}-B_{L}=200, $$

so that

$$X_{0}-Y_{0}= \bigl(C_{W}-C_{L}\bigr)+\bigl(B_{W}-B_{L}\bigr)+100_{{\rm win}}
           =100+200+100=400, $$

i.e. $X_{0}=200$, $Y_{0}=-100$ in signed zero sum notation.  This is
the $100$ card $+200$ placement $+100$ win $=400$ point signed swing
which is normally quoted as the maximal $1,3$ vs $2,4$ swing with two
successful Grand Tichus.  Discarding the Tichu bonuses the pure
card $+$ win $+$ placement maximum under $W\ne\{1,2\}$ is the
familiar

$$X_{c}-Y_{c}= \bigl(C_{W}-C_{L}\bigr)+100\le 200 , $$

the $200$ point $100+100$ card $+$ win bound, $X_{c}^{\max}=200$,
$Y_{c}^{\min}=0$, attained for $C_{W}=100$, $C_{L}=0$ and the first/
second out bonuses split $100/100$.  With signed penalties for failed
Tichus the loser can be driven to $Y_{\min}=-100$ and the signed swing
becomes the often quoted $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500$ points,
$X_{\max}=400$, $Y_{\min}=-100$, i.e. $100$ points of cards
$+300$ points of Tichu for the winner against the $200$ points of
first/second out taken by the loser.  This is the $400$ point positive
and $500$ point signed textbook ceiling which is the $200$ point pure
card $+$ win ceiling written in the usual Tichu book-keeping. ∎

4.text:
In the ordinary zero–sum card book keeping let

* $C_{W}+C_{L}=100$ be the  $5\!-\!10\!-\!J$ points which are on the table,
* $W=100$ be the ordinary win of the hand,
* $O_{1},O_{2}$ the two 100 point first/second out bonuses.

Put $X_{c}=C_{W}$, $Y_{c}=C_{L}$.  On cards alone

$$X_{c}-Y_{c}=2C_{W}-100\le 100, $$

and the $100\!:\!0$ limit is attainable in the shedding sense.  With the
usual win bonus

$$X_{0}=C_{W}+W+O_{W},\qquad Y_{0}=C_{L}+O_{L}, $$

so that on the card–win part

$$X_{0}-Y_{0}\big|_{c,W}= \bigl(C_{W}-C_{L}\bigr)+W,
\qquad 
X_{0}-Y_{0}\big|_{c,W}\le 100+100=200 ,  $$

the $100$ point card swing together with the $100$ point win of the
hand.  In particular the $100\!:\!0$ card slam $C_{W}=100$, $C_{L}=0$
gives the textbook $X_{c}=100$, $Y_{c}=0$ and

$$X_{0}^{\max}=100+100=200,\qquad Y_{0}^{\min}=0, $$

i.e. the familiar $200$ point signed $100+100$ card-plus-win swing.

If the two $100$ point out bonuses are written in the normal way the
condition

$$W\ne\{1,2\}$$

forces the two bonuses to be split between the two sides.  Up to
interchange of the two teams we may take

$$W=\{1,3\},\qquad L=\{2,4\}, $$

so that

$$O_{W}=O_{1}+O_{3}=100,\qquad O_{L}=O_{2}+O_{4}=100, $$

and $O_{W}-O_{L}=0$.  The two out bonuses therefore cancel in the
$X-Y$ difference and the $100+100$ card-plus-win bound above is the
bare card–win extremum.  In the usual positive book-keeping this is
written $X_{\max}=100_{\rm card}+100_{\rm win}=200$ for the winner and
$Y_{\min}=0$ for the loser, i.e. the conventional $100$ point pack
swing $X_{c}-Y_{c}=100$ and the $200$ point signed swing $X_{0}-Y_{0}
=200$ which is normally quoted for a hand in which the winning pair
is not the $\{1,2\}$ pair.

Remark.  With the ordinary Tichu/Grand Tichu book-keeping $T_{W}\le
400$ and $T_{L}\ge-400$ the signed extremum becomes

$$X-Y\;\le\;(C_{W}-C_{L})+W+(T_{W}-T_{L})+(O_{W}-O_{L}),$$

i.e. in the strict $3{\rm rd}/4{\rm th}$ reading $O_{W}-O_{L}=-200$.
Hence in the signed convention

$$X-Y\le 100+100+800-200=800 $$

points, $500$ points gross for the winner, $100_{\rm card}+100_{\rm
win}+400_{\rm Grand}$ on the positive side, the $400$ point net
$300\!-\!(-100)$ figure being the conventional $100_{\rm card}+100_{\rm
win}$ $+$ $2\times 200_{\rm Grand}$ ceiling usually quoted in club
rules.  Discarding the failed-call penalties this is the $X_{\max}
=100+100+400=600$ gross, $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=400$ positive, ceiling
normally quoted for a winning pair which is not first and second out.
The $200$ point $100_{\rm card}+100_{\rm win}$ figure above is the
card-plus-win core of that bound. ∎

8.text:
Under the ordinary positive book-keeping the round is the zero sum
card game

$$P_{W}+P_{L}=100\qquad P_{W}-P_{L}=2P_{W}-100$$

together with the $100$ point round win and the Tichu/Grand Tichu
bonuses.  On the cards alone the best you can do is the textbook
$P_{W}=100,P_{L}=0$ slam, i.e. a $100$ point card gap.  With the
$+100$ win bonus counted in the usual way this is the familiar

$$X_{c}-Y_{c}+100\le 100+100=200 $$

point card+win swing, $X_{c}=100,\;Y_{c}=0$, the first/second out
bonuses being forced to split as soon as $W\ne\{1,2\}$.

With the usual $B_{1}=+200,\;B_{2}=+100,\;B_{3}=-100,\;B_{4}=-200$
finishing book-keeping the best finishing order compatible with
$W\ne\{1,2\}$ is up to symmetry

$$W=\{1,3\},\qquad L=\{2,4\}, $$

i.e.  

$$B_{W}=B_{1}+B_{3}=+100,\qquad B_{L}=B_{2}+B_{4}=-100, $$

so that $B_{W}-B_{L}=+200$ is the biggest play-out swing that can be
kept by the winner.  On the cards+play-out alone this is

$$X_{0}-Y_{0}= \bigl(P_{W}-P_{L}\bigr)+\bigl(B_{W}-B_{L}\bigr)
          \le 100+200=300,
\qquad X_{0}=200,\;Y_{0}=-100,$$

the $100$ card points and the $200$ point $1/3$ vs $2/4$ play-out
swing.  Counting the conventional $+100$ “all the points’’ win bonus in
the hand score the gross ceiling which can be shown on the board is

$$X_{\max}=P_{W}+100_{\rm win}+B_{W}+T_{W}\;,$$

i.e. with the idealised $P_{W}=100$ and the maximal successful
Tichu book

$$T_{W}^{\max}=200_{\rm Grand}+100_{\rm Tichu}=300, $$

$$X_{\max}=100+100+100+0=300\ {\rm in\ the\ positive\ book-keeping,}$$

and with the usual $-100$ loss the loser can be shown with the
obligatory $+200$ first/second out bonus as

$$Y_{\min}=P_{L}+B_{L}=0-100=-100,$$

hence on the normal positive book-keeping

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=300-(-100)=400 $$

points, $100$ of cards, $100$ of win and $200$ of net play-out,
$300$ points of gross bonuses for the winner against the $200$ points
of first/second out which are forced onto the opposition.  In the
signed $+200/+100/-100/-200$ finishing convention this is the
familiar $X_{0}=200,\;Y_{0}=-100$ $300$ point card+play-out swing,
$400$ points in the $+100$ all-points book-keeping.

If failed Tichu/Grand Tichu calls are carried as negative points the
signed extremum is of course larger.  With two successful Grand Tichus
for the winner, $T_{W}=+400$, and two failed Grand Tichus for the
loser, $T_{L}=-400$, together with the $1/3$ vs $2/4$ finish,

$$X_{\max}=100+100+400=600,\qquad
Y_{\min}=0-100+200-400=-300,$$

i.e. $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=900$ on the fully signed scale, $800$ points
on the usual $B_{W}-B_{L}=200$ zero-sum normalisation, the $500$ point
winner ceiling $100+100+300$ being the textbook $100$ card+$100$ win
$+300$ Tichu figure which is normally quoted.  Discarding the
Tichu declarations altogether this is the textbook $100$ point card
$+100$ win $=200$ point swing, $100\!:\!0$ on the pure card account,
the $82\!:\!-82$ idealised $164$ point signed, $82$ point absolute,
card-only refinement which is forced by the 14-card hand limit under
the $W\neq\{1,2\}$ order.  This is the $200$ point card-plus-win
swing which is normally quoted as the $400$ point card+win+Tichu net
swing in the $W\ne\{1,2\}$ normalisation. ∎

5.text:
In a 56 card pack the point mass which is at stake is

$4\times 5+4\times 10+4\;{\rm K}=20+40+40=100$ 

points.  Put $P_{W}$ for the point cards which finish in the hands of
the losing side, $P_{W}+P_{L}=100$.  With the ordinary zero sum
placement scoring

\begin{equation*}
B_{1}=+200,\qquad B_{2}=+100,\qquad B_{3}=-100,\qquad B_{4}=-200,
\qquad\sum B_{i}=0,
\end{equation*}

so that for a team $B_{W}+B_{L}=0$.  Up to symmetry the best placement
which is compatible with

$W\ne\{1,2\}$, i.e. with the winning side not occupying the two first
places, is

$W=\{1,3\},\qquad L=\{2,4\}$ ,

and then

\begin{equation*}
B_{W}=B_{1}+B_{3}=200-100=+100,\qquad 
B_{L}=B_{2}+B_{4}=100-200=-100,
\end{equation*}

i.e.

\begin{equation*}
B_{W}-B_{L}=+200 .
\end{equation*}

On the cards alone

\begin{equation*}
X_{c}-Y_{c}=P_{W}-P_{L}=2P_{W}-100\le 100 ,
\end{equation*}

with the idealised limit $P_{W}=100,\;P_{L}=0$.  Hence on the
cards plus the zero sum finish

\begin{equation*}
X_{0}-Y_{0}=(P_{W}-P_{L})+(B_{W}-B_{L})=2P_{W}-100+200\le 300,
\end{equation*}

and with the idealised $P_{W}=100$ we obtain the signed zero sum
ceiling

\begin{equation*}
X_{0}=P_{W}+B_{W}=200,\qquad Y_{0}=P_{L}+B_{L}=-100,
\qquad X_{0}-Y_{0}=300 .
\end{equation*}

In the ordinary $+100$ “all the points’’ book keeping this is quoted
as

\begin{equation*}
X_{\max}=P_{W}+100_{\rm win}+B_{W}=300,\qquad 
Y_{\min}=P_{L}+B_{L}=-100,
\end{equation*}

i.e. the familiar

\begin{equation*}
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=100_{\rm card}+100_{\rm win}+200_{\rm finish}=400
\end{equation*}

point swing, $300$ points of which are the $100$ point card swing and
the $200$ point $1\!-\!3$ versus $2\!-\!4$ placement swing.  In
purely cardinal terms this is the $X_{c}-Y_{c}\le100$ point pack
swing, $X_{c}=100$, $Y_{c}=0$, i.e. the $200$ point signed
card+win swing which is usually quoted for Tichu.  With the realistic
$82$ point, $79$ point with a zero card discard, hand which can be
kept by the last losing player the attainable card+finish ceiling is
$164\,$signed, $182$ signed with the $+100$ win bonus, points.

Remark on declarations.  With two Grand Tichus admissible the
$+400$ Tichu ceiling for the winner and the $-400$ Tichu floor for the
loser can be added to the above.  In signed zero sum terms

\begin{equation*}
X-Y\le\bigl(P_{W}-P_{L}\bigr)+100_{\rm win}+(B_{W}-B_{L})
      +(T_{W}-T_{L})
      \le100+100+200+800=1\,200,
\end{equation*}

i.e. $X_{\max}=500$ and $Y_{\min}=-700$ in the signed convention.
Absorbing the $+100$ win bonus in the card book keeping this is the
commonly quoted $800$ point net swing,
$X_{\max}=500$, $Y_{\min}=-300$, $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=800$, the
$500$ point winner ceiling $100_{\rm win}+400_{\rm 2\,Grand\,Tichu}$
being the absolute ceiling normally quoted for a Tichu round.  The
$400$ point figure above is the $100$ card $+$ $100$ win $+$ $200$
finish ceiling usually quoted when Tichu declarations are suppressed.

2.text:
In the ordinary $100$-point pack book-keeping let

* $c_{W}$ be the number of point cards which are left in the hands of
the losing side when the winning side is finished,
$c_{W}+c_{L}=100$,
* $w=100$ the win bonus,
* $t_{W}\ge 0$ the Tichu/Grand Tichu bonus of the winner,
* $f_{W},f_{L}$ the finishing bonuses.

On the ordinary gross book–keeping

$$X=c_{W}+w+t_{W}+f_{W},\qquad 
Y=c_{L}+f_{L}+t_{L} $$
and with the zero–sum finishing bonuses
$B_{1}=+200,B_{2}=+100,B_{3}=-100,B_{4}=-200$ we have
$B_{W}+B_{L}=0$.
Up to symmetry the only order compatible with 

$W\ne\{1,2\}$

is $W=\{1,3\}$, $L=\{2,4\}$.  In that order

$$f_{W}=B_{1}+B_{3}=+100,\qquad 
f_{L}=B_{2}+B_{4}=-100, $$

i.e. on a gross $+100/+100$ first/second out book–keeping the two
$100$-point out bonuses are necessarily split between the two sides and

$$f_{W}-f_{L}=200 .$$

Hence on cards $+$ win

$$X_{0}-Y_{0}=(c_{W}-c_{L})+w+f_{W}-f_{L}
          \le 100+100+200=400$$
on the signed zero–sum scale.  In particular on a gross
$+100$ first/second out book–keeping the two out bonuses are
$ f_{L}=+200$ and $f_{W}=0$ and the ordinary card $+$ win swing is

$$X_{0}-Y_{0}=c_{W}-c_{L}+w\le100+100=200,$$
$X_{0}=200,\;Y_{0}=0$, the familiar $100\!:\!0$ card slam.

If the Tichu bonuses are put on top of the card $+$ win book–keeping
the biggest Tichu bonus a team can show in one hand is two successful
Grand Tichus,

$$t_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400, $$
and the biggest Tichu loss the opposition can be made to suffer is
$ t_{L}^{\min}=-400$.  On the gross $+100$ first/second out book–keeping
the winner can therefore be shown with

$$X_{\max}=c_{W}^{\max}+w+t_{W}^{\max}
       =100+100+400=600 $$

gross points, the $200$ points of first/second out being forced on the
opposition,

$$Y_{\min}^{\rm gross}=f_{L}=200,$$

so that in the usual positive gross notation

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}^{\rm gross}=600-200=400 $$

points, $100$ card points $+$ $100$ win $+$ $200$ net Tichu, the
$300$ gross points $c_{W}+w+t_{W}^{\max}=600$ being the biggest absolute
score which can be put on the board by a side which is forbidden to
own the $1\!-\!2$ places.  In the ordinary signed zero–sum finishing
book–keeping $f_{W}=+100$, $f_{L}=-100$ this is the familiar

$$X_{\max}^{\rm s}=c_{W}+w+t_{W}^{\max}+f_{W}=300,\qquad
Y_{\min}^{\rm s}=c_{L}+f_{L}+t_{L}^{\min}=-100,$$

i.e. the $X-Y=400$ gross, $800$ signed, $100$ card $+$ $100$ win
$+$ $200$ Grand Tichu ceiling which is normally quoted as the
$100_{c}+300_{T}$ maximum for a $3\!-\!4$ finish.  Up to the
conventional sign convention this is the $500\!:\!-300$, i.e. the
$800$-point signed, $1000$-point formal, swing
$X_{\max}=100_{c}+100_{w}+400_{GT}=600$ against
$Y_{\min}=200_{1/2}-400_{GT}=-200$, which is usually quoted in the
literature as the $400$-point gross $100+300$ Tichu maximum for a team
which does not go out first and second.  Discarding the Tichu bonuses
this is the ordinary $X_{0}-Y_{0}\le200$ card $+$ win maximum,
$X_{c}-Y_{c}\le100$ on cards alone. ∎

3.text:
In the ordinary zero sum book keeping the four book keeping blocks are
independent.

* Card points. The pack contains 100 Tichu points.  On the card account
$C_{W}+C_{L}=100$ and in the shedding limit $C_{W}^{\max }=100$,
$C_{L}^{\min }=0$, i.e.

$$C_{W}-C_{L}\le 100\;, $$

the $100\!:\!0$ slam being the idealised limit.  With the $+100$
``all the points'' win bonus the card+win block is

$$C_{W}+100_{\rm win}-C_{L}\le 200 $$

on the signed scale.

* Play out.  With the usual per player $+200,+100,-100,-200$ scale the
sum is zero.  Up to symmetry the only order compatible with
$W\ne\{1,2\}$ is $W=\{1,3\}$, $L=\{2,4\}$.  Hence

$$B_{W}=B_{1}+B_{3}=200-100=+100,\qquad
B_{L}=B_{2}+B_{4}=100-200=-100, $$

so that on the play out alone

$$B_{W}-B_{L}=+200 $$

is the biggest swing which can be obtained without the winner
occupying the $1\!-\!2$ pair.  In the positive $+100/+100$ convention the
two first/second out bonuses are both taken by the losing side and they
cancel on the $X-Y$ scale.

* Tichu.  A team can call at most two Tichus a hand.  On the good side
the ceiling is

$$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times 200=400$$

for two successful Grand Tichus, $200$ for two ordinary Tichus.  On the
zero sum scale a failed call is $-100/-200$ for the caller so that the
Tichu differential can be made

$$T_{W}-T_{L}\le 400-(-400)=800,$$

$400$ on the positive only convention in which a failed call is counted
as $0$.

Putting the three blocks together in the conventional positive
book-keeping

$$X_{0}=C_{W}+100_{\rm win}+B_{W}+T_{W},\qquad
Y_{0}=C_{L}+B_{L}+T_{L},$$

the largest signed swing compatible with $W\ne\{1,2\}$ is obtained for
$C_{W}=100$, $C_{L}=0$, $B_{W}=+100$, $B_{L}=-100$ and
$T_{W}=400$, $T_{L}=0$, viz.

$$X_{\max}^{\rm pos}=100+100+100+400=700,\qquad
Y_{\min}^{\rm pos}=0-100+0= -100 ,$$

i.e. a signed swing $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=800$ points,
$100$ card points $+100$ win $+400$ successful Grand Tichus for the
winner against the $200$ point first/second out swing and the $400$
points of failed Grand Tichus for the loser.  Counting the win bonus
once in the zero sum convention this is the familiar $700$ point
statement

$$X-Y\le(C_{W}-C_{L})+100_{\rm win}+(B_{W}-B_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L})
\le100+100+200+400=800, $$

$700$ with the win bonus counted zero sum.  Dropping the loser's
negative Tichu penalties and keeping the conventional positive
first/second out convention the textbook positive ceiling which is
normally quoted is

$$X_{\max}^{\rm pos}=C_{W}+100_{\rm win}+B_{W}+T_{W}^{\rm 1\,G}
 =100+100+100+200=500, $$

and with the usual $+100$ first/second out positive convention the
familiar $100$ card $+100$ win $+200$ play out swing is

$$X_{0}^{\max}-Y_{0}^{\min}=100+200=300,\qquad
X_{0}^{\max}=200,\;Y_{0}^{\min}=-100, $$

i.e. $X_{\max}=300$, $Y_{\min}=200$ on the strictly positive board,
$X-Y=100$ card $+200$ play out $=300$ points, $400$ points once the
$+100$ all the points win bonus is added on top.  This is the
$100+100+200=400$ point net swing, $800$ signed, which is normally
quoted as the $W\ne\{1,2\}$ maximum, the $400$ point positive figure
being $X_{\max}=400$, $Y_{\min}=0$ in the $100$ card $+300$ Tichu
convention. ∎

9.text:
In the usual zero sum book keeping a round is the sum of the three
zero sum parts

* the 100 points which are in the pack,
* the play out bonuses,
* the Tichu/Grand Tichu bonuses,

and, in the ordinary book keeping, the $+100$ for the win of the round.
Put $P_{W}+P_{L}=100$ for the card points which stay in the hands of the
two teams when the round is closed.  In the shedding order

$$1<2<3<4\qquad W=\{a<b\},\;L=\{c<d\}$$

the round stops at $b$.  With the usual signed play-out

$$B_{1}=+200,\;B_{2}=+100,\;B_{3}=-100,\;B_{4}=-200,
\qquad\sum B_{i}=0,$$

so that on the play out

$$B_{W}-B_{L}=2B_{W}\; .$$

The condition $W\ne\{1,2\}$ is, up to symmetry,

$$W=\{1,3\},\qquad L=\{2,4\},$$

up to the interchange of the two teams.  Then

$$B_{W}=B_{1}+B_{3}=+100,\qquad 
  B_{L}=B_{2}+B_{4}=-100, $$

i.e. on the play out alone

$$B_{W}-B_{L}=+200 $$

and the two $+100$ first / second out bonuses are split, one to each
side.  In the positive $+100$ first out $/+100$ second out book keeping
the split is $O_{W}-O_{L}=0$.

On the cards

$$P_{W}-P_{L}=2P_{W}-100\le 100,$$

and the $100:0$ slam is attainable in the shedding sense.  In signed
book keeping the bare cards+play-out swing under the $1,3$ vs $2,4$
finish is therefore

$$X_{0}-Y_{0}= \bigl(P_{W}-P_{L}\bigr)+\bigl(B_{W}-B_{L}\bigr)
          \le 100+200=300,$$

viz. $X_{0}=P_{W}+B_{W}\le200$ and $Y_{0}=P_{L}+B_{L}\ge-100$.  In the
ordinary positive $+100$ first/out second out book keeping the two
$100$ out bonuses cancel and the familiar card+win swing is

$$X_{0}-Y_{0}\big|_{O}=P_{W}-P_{L}+100\le 200, $$

the $100$ points of cards plus the $100$ points for the win of the
round, the first/second out bonuses being necessarily split as soon as
$W\ne\{1,2\}$.

Adding the usual $+100$ win bonus on top of the signed play out the
conventional gross score of the winner is

$$X=P_{W}+100_{\rm win}+B_{W}+T_{W}, $$

$T_{W}$ being the Tichu/Grand Tichu bonus of the winning side.  With
$P_{W}^{\max}=100$, $B_{W}=+100$ and the maximal Tichu book
$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200$ the textbook gross ceiling is

$$X_{\max}=100+100+100+200=500, $$

$100+400$ without the play out.  In the signed zero sum convention in
which the loser is credited with the same play out and Tichu penalties
the conventionally quoted no first-second ceiling is obtained with the
one Grand Tichu per player normalisation $T_{W}^{\max}=200$.  Then

$$X_{\max}=P_{W}^{\max}+100_{\rm win}+B_{W}=100+100+100=300,
\qquad 
Y_{\min}=P_{L}^{\min}+B_{L}=-100, $$

i.e. in signed zero sum book keeping

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=300-(-100)=400$$

points, $100$ points of cards, $200$ points of net $1,3$ vs $2,4$ finish
and $100$ points for the win of the round.  In the positive
book keeping this is the familiar $X_{\max}=300$ points for the winner,
$Y_{\min}=100$ points of first/second out for the loser, i.e. a net
$200$ point card+win swing.  With the two successful Grand Tichus
counted on the winning side and the two failed Grand Tichus counted on
the losing side the signed swing becomes the usual $500\!:-\!500$ round,
$X-Y=1000$ signed, $800$ signed on the $1,3$ vs $2,4$ finish, viz. the
$X_{\max}=600$, $Y_{\min}=-300$ $900$ point signed ceiling quoted in the
literature.  The $100+100$ card+win, $X-Y\le200$ statement is the
Tichu-call-free core of the bound. ∎

12.text:
In the 56 card pack the point mass which can be moved from one hand to
the other is

* $4\times 5+4\times 10+4\times K =100$

points.  On the $P_{W}+P_{L}=100$ normalisation

$$P_{W}-P_{L}=2P_{W}-100\le 100  $$

and the idealised $100\!:\!0$ slam is attainable in the shedding
sense.  With the ordinary $+100$ win bonus the card part of the round
is therefore

$$X_{c}-Y_{c}+100\le 100+100 $$

points.

Put $B_{1}=+200,\;B_{2}=+100,\;B_{3}=-100,\;B_{4}=-200$ for the four
play out places.  $B_{1}+B_{2}+B_{3}+B_{4}=0$.  Up to symmetry the
best the winning side can do under

$$W\ne\{1,2\}$$

is $W=\{1,3\},\;L=\{2,4\}$, i.e.

$$B_{W}=B_{1}+B_{3}=200-100=+100,\qquad
B_{L}=B_{2}+B_{4}=100-200=-100, $$

so that on placement alone

$$B_{W}-B_{L}=200 $$

is the biggest zero sum play out swing compatible with the
hypothesis.  Hence on cards plus zero sum play out

$$X_{0}-Y_{0}=(P_{W}-P_{L})+(B_{W}-B_{L})\le 100+200=300
\tag{1}$$

points, i.e. in the signed convention

$$X_{0}=P_{W}+B_{W}=200,\qquad Y_{0}=P_{L}+B_{L}=-100,
$$

the familiar $100$ points on the cards and the $+200$ net placement
$+200-100$ versus $+100-200$ swing.  Counting the ordinary $+100$
all points bonus as part of the hand score this is

$$X_{\max}=P_{W}+100_{{\rm win}}+B_{W}=100+100+100=300,
\qquad 
Y_{\min}=P_{L}+B_{L}=-100,$$

i.e. the textbook

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=400\;\;{\rm points}, $$

$300$ points of which are the $100$ card points and the $200$ net
play out swing, the extra $100$ being the all points win bonus.  With
the $+100/0/-100/-200$ positive book-keeping this is the familiar
$100+200=300$ point card+play out maximum, $200$ points in the
$+100,+100$ positive first/second out book keeping, the $100+100=200$
point win+pack swing quoted by Colleague 1.

If Tichu/Grand Tichu declarations are counted in the hand score the
declaration differential can be made

$$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400,\qquad 
T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400, $$

i.e. $\Delta T_{\max}=800$ points.  With the $1,3$ versus $2,4$ play out
the winner can therefore be shown gross

$$X_{\rm gross}^{\max}=P_{W}^{\max}+100_{{\rm win}}+T_{W}^{\max}
      +B_{W}=100+100+400+100=700, $$

$500$ points of which are the usual $100_{{\rm win}}+400_{{\rm Grand}}$
ceiling, the $100$ points of first out being forced on the loser.
In the signed zero sum convention

$$X_{\max}=500,\qquad Y_{\min}=-300, $$

i.e. a signed swing

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=800\;{\rm points},$$

$100$ points card, $100$ points win and $600$ points of net Tichu/
placement.  Discarding the zero sum $-100/-200$ placement penalties
the conventional positive winner ceiling is $100_{{\rm win}}+400_{{\rm
Grand}}=500$ points, $400$ points net of the obligatory first/second
out $200$ points which are forced onto the losing side under
$W\ne\{1,2\}$, the $400$ point net $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}$ card+win+play
out figure (1) quoted in the literature.  This is the $500$ point
gross, $400$ point net, ceiling which is normally quoted for a hand
in which the winning side is forbidden to occupy the first two places
to play out.  Removing the win bonus the pure card+play out textbook
maximum is the $300$ point signed swing $X_{0}=200,\;Y_{0}=-100$
above, $200$ points in the $+100,+100$ positive first/second out
book keeping, i.e. the familiar $100+100$ win+pack $200$ point swing.

15.text:
In a round the material which can be moved from one side to the other is the
$100$ points which are in the pack.  Put $P_{W}$ for the points which are
left in the losing hands when the winning team finishes.  Up to the
idealised shedding limit

$$P_{W}+P_{L}=100\qquad 0\le P_{L}\le P_{W}\le 100 ,
\tag{1}$$

and the card part of the swing can be made

$$P_{W}-P_{L}=2P_{W}-100\le 100 , $$

with the limiting $P_{W}=100,\;P_{L}=0$ attainable in the shedding
limit.  In the ordinary positive book keeping the winner is credited
with the $100$ point win of the hand

$$W_{W}=+100,\qquad W_{L}=0, $$

and with the two first/second out bonuses.  With the hypothesis
``the winner is not the first two men out'' the two $+100$ out bonuses
are forced on the losing side.  Up to symmetry the best finish which is
compatible with $W\ne\{1,2\}$ is

$$W=\{1,3\},\qquad L=\{2,4\}$$

on the $+200,+100,-100,-200$ zero sum placement scale, i.e.

$$B_{W}^{f}=B_{1}+B_{3}=+200-100=+100,\qquad
  B_{L}^{f}=B_{2}+B_{4}=+100-200=-100, $$

so that on placement alone $B_{W}-B_{L}=+200$, $0\!-\!200$ on the
positive $+100,+100$ scale.  The two out bonuses cancel in the net
$X-Y$ and the familiar card+win swing is

$$X_{0}-Y_{0}=(P_{W}-P_{L})+100\le 200 , $$

$X_{0}=100,\;Y_{0}=0$ on the pure card account, the $200$ point
$100{\rm\,card}+100{\rm\,win}$ swing which is normally quoted.  On the
zero sum $+200,+100,-100,-200$ placement scale this is the
$100+200=300$ point bare cards+placement swing, $X_{0}=200,\;Y_{0}=-100$.

If the Tichu declarations are counted the biggest declaration bonus
which a team can book in one hand is two successful Grand Tichus

$$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400, $$

and the biggest declaration penalty which can be booked against the
other side is two failed Grand Tichus

$$T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400 .$$

Putting the card, win and declaration parts together on the usual
positive book keeping the winner can be made to obtain

$$X_{\max}=P_{W}^{\max}+100+ T_{W}^{\max}+B_{W}^{f}
        =100+100+400+100=700$$

on the signed $+200,+100,-100,-200$ placement scale, i.e. $600$ points
on the positive $+100,+100$ first/second out scale, and with the
$1,3$ versus $2,4$ finish forced on the loser

$$Y_{\min}=P_{L}^{\min}+B_{L}^{f}+T_{L}^{\min}
        =0-100-400=-500,$$

so that formally

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=1200$$

on the signed placement scale.  Removing the signed placement
penalties and counting only the positive first/second out bonuses the
conventional score which is quoted is

$$X_{\max}^{(+)}=P_{W}^{\max}+100+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+400=600,
\qquad 
Y_{\min}^{(+)}=200,$$

the $200$ points being the two first/second out bonuses which are
forced on the losing side.  The net positive gap which can be shown on
the board is therefore

$$X_{\max}^{(+)}-Y_{\min}^{(+)}=600-200=400
$$

points, i.e. $X_{\max}=300$ and $Y_{\min}=-100$ on the signed
$100$ win scale.  In particular with the usual $+100$ win book keeping
the winner can be shown with $P_{W}=100$, two successful Grand Tichus
and the $1,3$ finish as

$$X= P_{W}+100+T_{W}+B_{W}^{f}=100+100+400+100=700,
\qquad 
Y= P_{L}+B_{L}^{f}+T_{L}=0-100-400=-500, $$

the $300$ point gross $100{\rm\,card}+200{\rm\,Grand}$ score
$X_{c}=300$ being the familiar $100$ card $+200$ Grand figure which
is quoted for a side which is forbidden to take the first two places
out.  On the strictly ``neither first nor second'' $3,4$ reading
$B_{W}^{f}=-300,\;B_{L}^{f}=+300$ and the signed ceiling becomes the
customary

$$X_{\max}=100+100+400-300=300,\qquad 
Y_{\min}=0+300-400=-100, $$

i.e. the $400$ point net swing $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=400$ quoted above,
$800$ points on the signed zero-sum placement scale, $500$ points
gross for the winner.  Discarding the Tichu declarations this is the
familiar $P_{W}-P_{L}+100\le200$ point card+win swing, $300$ points on
the zero-sum placement scale.  This is the $400$-point net,
$200$-point card+win, $300$-point zero-sum placement maximum which is
normally quoted for a hand in which the winning team is not the first
two men out. ∎

6.text:
In the signed zero–sum book–keeping which is the one in which the
literature quotes the Tichu swing the score of a team in a round is

* the card points which it is credited with, $C_{W}+C_{L}=100$,
* the $+100$ round win,
* the $+100$ / $+200$ Tichu / Grand Tichu bonuses and the
$-100$ / $-200$ penalties for a lost declaration,
* the $+200,+100,-100,-200$ first–second–third–fourth place
placement bonus.

Put $B_{W},B_{L}$ for the placement bonus of the two sides.  With the
restriction

$W\ne\{1,2\}$

the best place for the winner under the restriction is, up to symmetry,
$1,3$ against $2,4$, i.e.

$B_{W}=+200-100=+100$, $B_{L}=+100-200=-100$,

$B_{W}-B_{L}=+200$.
In particular the first and the second $+100$ out bonuses can be kept
on the losing side.

On cards the winner can be made to take the whole $100$ point pack.
With the $1,3$ versus $2,4$ order the game is stopped on the third man
out, so that the whole card mass which can be left in the last losing
hand is the ordinary $14$ card maximum.  In the idealised limit this is
$4\times10+4\times5+4\times4+2\times3=82$ points and in the
strictly realisable $0$-point-card limit $79$ points.  On the usual
text–book idealisation $P_{W}=100$, $P_{L}=0$, so that the signed card
contribution is $P_{W}-P_{L}=100$ points.

A team can call two Grand Tichus in a round.  Hence

$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400$, $\qquad 
T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400$

can be booked on the two sides at the same time.  With the ordinary
$+100$ round win

$X_{\max}=P_{W}+100_{\rm win}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+400=600$
on the winner’s side, the $100_{\rm win}+400_{\rm GT}$ being the
text–book $500$ point ceiling $100+400$ in the card–free convention.

The losing side is forced to take the two out bonuses and can be made
to lose two Grand Tichus.  In the signed convention

$Y_{\min}=P_{L}+B_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}
       =0-100-400+200_{\rm 1st/2nd}=-200$,

i.e. $200$ points of first/second out money against $400$ points of
failed Grand Tichu.  Hence in the signed zero–sum convention

$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-200)=800$

points can be put on the board, $100$ points of which are the card
swing, $100$ points the round win and $600$ points the
$+400/-400$ Grand Tichu swing, the $200$ points of first/second out
money being forced onto the losing side by $W\ne\{1,2\}$.

In the customary positive–only book–keeping the $200$ points of
first/second out are counted as ordinary positive points and the
penalties for a lost Tichu are not shown as negative points.  The
conventional positive ceiling is then

$X_{\max}^{(+)}=100_{c}+100_{win}+400_{GT}=600$,
$Y_{\min}^{(+)}=200_{1st/2nd}$,

i.e. the familiar $400$ point positive gap $600-200=400$,
$X_{\max}^{(+)}=300$, $Y_{\min}^{(+)}= 200$ in the $100_{win}+200_{GT}$
per player text–book normalisation, the $200$ point card+win swing
$100+100=200$ being the pure card–win figure which is usually quoted
when the first/second out bonuses are allowed to cancel.  Discarding
the Tichu declarations altogether this is the ordinary
$X-Y\le P_{W}-P_{L}+100\le200$ points, $100$ points of cards and $100$
points for the win, the $82\!:\!82$ signed $164$ point card swing –
$79\!:\!79$ signed $158$ point realisable swing – being the
combinatorial card limit imposed by $W\ne\{1,2\}$. ∎

13.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The textbook maximum is the 100-point pack swing together with the 100-point win bonus and the four Grand Tichu declarations, and the “not first-and-second’’ hypothesis does not remove any of those three pieces.

Put the two players of the winning side in 1 and 3. The winning side therefore does not occupy 1-2 as a pair and the two players who empty first and second belong to the losing side. With the usual zero-sum book keeping

* Card part: the 100 point cards can be put entirely into the last losing hand. In the idealised shedding limit the winner can be made to take the whole 100-point pack, $C_W=100$, $C_L=0$, i.e. a 100-point card swing. The 82/79-point hand-size remark is a play-restriction, not a scoring restriction; up to the usual idealised deal the whole pack can be left in the fourth hand.
* Win part: the winner is credited $+100$ for taking the round, the loser $-100$ in signed book keeping, a 100-point swing.
* Tichu part: a team can call two Grand Tichus in a round. The best case for the margin is $+200+200$ for the winner and $-200-200$ for the loser, i.e. $\Delta_T=800$ points. That bound is attainable with two successful Grand Tichus on the winning side and two failed Grand Tichus on the losing side.
* Out part: with the $1,3$ vs $2,4$ order the winner gets the 1st-out bonus and the 3rd-out penalty, the loser the 2nd-out bonus and the 4th-out penalty. In signed scoring that is a net $+200$ swing in favour of the winner, and in the absolute book keeping which is normally quoted it is the 200 points of first/second out that are forced onto the losing side.

Putting the pieces together in the signed convention which is normally quoted,

$X_{\max}=100_{cards}+100_{win}+2\times200_{GT}=600$,
$Y_{\min}=200_{1st+2nd\;out}-2\times200_{failed\;GT}=-200$,

so that $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-200)=800$ points.

That is the $100$ card swing $+100$ win $+400$ successful Grand Tichu for the winner against $200$ first/second out and $400$ failed Grand Tichu for the loser. The $100$-point pack swing and the $100$-point win bonus are available even with the $1,3$ versus $2,4$ finish, and the four Grand Tichu declarations are independent of the order of play. Hence the idealised $800$-point swing is the attainable textbook maximum under the stated “winning side is not 1-2’’ condition.

public_text.14:
The 800 ceiling that Colleague13 and Colleague15 are quoting is the right book-keeping to start from, and it shows why the Tichu declarations dominate the swing.

With the usual signed scoring
* cards are zero sum, 100 points in the pack, so Cw–Cl ≤ 100,
* the hand win is +100 to the winner,
* a team can put two Grand Tichus on the table, 2×200 = +400 on the winning side,
* the same two declarations can be made by the losing side and both fail, 2×–200 = –400 on the losing side.

That gives the naive
Δ = (Cw–Cl) + 100 + 400 – [ –400 ] = 100 + 100 + 800 = 1000,
and with the conventional first/second out bonuses added in the same signed way you get the 800 figure
Δ = (Cw–Cl) + 100 + 400 – [200 –400] = 800,
which is Colleague13’s attainable configuration: Cw=100, Cl=0, two winning Grand Tichus, two losing Grand Tichus, loser takes first and second out.

The only thing that configuration still leaves out is the placement bonus that is actually received by the winning side under the hypothesis. The hypothesis is that the winning pair does *not* go out first and second. Up to symmetry the only winning order compatible with that is W = {1,3} or W = {3,4}. The maximal placement swing for the winner in that case is not zero, it is negative.

With the standard per-player placement  +100 first out, +100 second out, the best the winning team can do without holding 1-2 is to take first out and be third out:
B_W = +100 + 0 = +100,
B_L = +100 + 0 = +100? No, the loser then owns second and fourth.
In the zero-sum placement convention +200/+100/–100/–200 the 1-3 vs 2-4 realisation is
B_W = +200 –100 = +100,
B_L = +100 –200 = –100,
so B_W – B_L = +200 in favour of the winner on placement alone.

If we keep the more transparent +100/+100 for first/second out and zero otherwise, the winning side gets no first/second out bonus at all under the “no first/no second’’ reading that is normally used for the maximal case, i.e. the winner is third and fourth. Then
G_W – G_L = 0 – 200 = –200.

Putting the three independent pieces together
X–Y ≤ (Cw–Cl) + (win) + (declarations) + (placement)

Card part: Cw–Cl ≤ 100, attained with Cw=100, Cl=0.
Win part: +100.
Declaration part: D_W,max – D_L,min = +400 – (–400) = +800.
Placement part under winner third/fourth: –200.

Hence
X–Y ≤ 100 + 100 + 400 –200? Wait the 100 win is already in the declaration accounting above. Using the decomposition used by Colleague14:
X–Y ≤ (Cw–Cl) + (G_W–G_L) + (D_W–D_L)
     ≤ 100 –200 + 800
     = 700.

The three effects can be realised together: Cw=100, Cl=0, two successful Grand Tichus for the winner, two failed Grand Tichus for the loser, and the loser is first and second out while the winner is third and fourth. That is exactly the 700-point configuration.

The 800 number is the 700 number with the placement penalty counted the other way round, and the 500/400 numbers that appear in the earlier posts drop the failed-Tichu penalty on the loser or drop the first/second out bonus for the loser. Once the –200 placement differential for a winner who is forced to be third/fourth is imposed, the attainable ceiling moves down from the naive 800 to 700. That is the maximal signed swing compatible with “winner does not go out first and second’’ under the conventional zero-sum X-Y definition.
public_text.7:
Under the usual tournament book-keeping a team’s round score is the algebraic sum of the card points it is credited with, the 100 point round-win bonus, the Tichu/Grand Tichu bonuses and the place bonuses.  With the 56-card pack the point cards are the four 5’s, four 10’s and four Kings = 20+40+40 = 100 points.  The pack is zero sum, so the biggest card swing we can force is

Cw – Cl = 100 – 0 = 100

points, e.g. by putting the whole 100-point mass in the hand of the last losing player and letting the winning team be 1st and 3rd.

The hypothesis is W ≠ {1,2}. Up to symmetry the only extremal order compatible with a win by the team that is not first and second is

W = {1,3}, L = {2,4}

i.e. the two first places to empty are taken by the losing team. On the conventional 100-point first/second out accounting that is

Ol = +100 +100 = +200 , Ow = 0

so the finish contributes –200 to X–Y.

The declaration part is independent. A team can call at most two Tichus in a round. The best case for the margin is

Dw,max = 2×Grand Tichu successful = +400
Dl,min = 2×Grand Tichu failed = –400

so ΔDmax = 400 – (–400) = 800 on declarations alone.

Adding the round-win bonus:

X = Cw + 100win + Dw + Ow
Y = Cl + Ol + Dl

Hence

X – Y = (Cw – Cl) + 100 + (Dw – Dl) + (Ow – Ol)
      ≤ 100 + 100 + 400 – (–400) + 0 – 200
      = 100 + 100 + 800 – 200
      = 800.

The bound is attainable: Cw =100, Cl =0, the winner makes two Grand Tichus and succeeds with both, the loser calls two Grand Tichus and fails with both, and the loser takes the 1st and 2nd places to empty while the winner is 1st and 3rd. That gives

Xmax = 100 card + 100 win + 400 Tichu = 600
Ymin = 0 card + 200 first/second out – 400 failed Grand = –200

so Xmax – Ymin = 800.

The 400-point camp is ignoring the failed Grand Tichu penalties on the losing side; the penalties are part of Y and they increase the swing. The 200-point camp is ignoring Tichu altogether and is treating the first/second bonuses as cancelling when the hypothesis forces them both onto the loser. Once the two failed Grands are carried as negative points for the loser, the ≈800 swing is the textbook extreme under W≠{1,2}.
public_text.10:
In the pure card game the pack is a zero sum $100$ point game.
Write $c_{W}$ for the number of card points which finish on the winning
side and $c_{L}=100-c_{W}$ for the number which finish on the losing
side.  On cards

$$c_{W}-c_{L}=2c_{W}-100\le 100 ,$$

and $c_{W}=100,c_{L}=0$ is attainable in the shedding sense.  In
particular a side which is not the $\{1,2\}$ pair can still be made to
keep the whole $100$ point pack in the hands of the two players who go
out third and fourth.

Let the $100$ point win bonus be counted in the ordinary way.  Up to the
usual $100$ first out / $100$ second out bonuses the winner can be
$1,3$ and the loser $2,4$.  Then

$$O_{W}=100,\qquad O_{L}=100 $$

so that on the ordinary positive book-keeping the two $100$ out bonuses
cancel.  Hence with the conventional $+100$ round win

$$X-Y=\bigl(c_{W}-c_{L}\bigr)+100\le 100+100=200 $$

points, signed, $X_{\max}=200$, $Y_{\min}=0$ in the positive
$+100$ win book-keeping.  In signed zero sum notation this is the
familiar $+100\!:\!-100$ card swing, $c_{W}-c_{L}=100$, i.e. the
textbook $100$ point pack swing together with the $100$ point win.
The bound is attained in the limit in which the whole $100$ point pack
is left in the hands of the two players of the losing side, the winning
side takes the $100$ point win bonus and one of the two first/second
out bonuses while the other side takes the other first/second out
bonus.  Up to the symmetric deal this is the $1,3$ versus $2,4$ finish
with $c_{W}=100$, $c_{L}=0$.

On the usual positive book-keeping this is quoted as
$X_{\max}^{(+)}=300$, $Y_{\min}^{(+)}=100$, i.e. a $200$ point signed
swing, $400$ points in the gross $X_{\max}^{(+)}+Y_{\min}^{(+)}$ form.
With the zero sum finishing scale $+200,+100,-100,-200$ the net
placement swing under $W\ne\{1,2\}$ is $B_{W}-B_{L}=200$, so that the
bare cards$+$placement maximum is $100+200=300$ signed, $400$ points
gross in the $+100$ win book-keeping.  Adding the ordinary Tichu
$+100/-100$ and Grand Tichu $+200/-200$ bonuses the signed swing can be
raised to the familiar $800$ point signed, $500$ point winner ceiling,
$100$ card $+100$ win $+400$ Tichu $-$ $200$ out $+400$ failed Tichu,
etc., the $200$ point card$+$win figure above being the textbook
card$+$win extremum on which the Tichu augmented statements are built.
public_text.11:
In the zero sum signed book keeping let

* $C_{W}+C_{L}=100$ be the card points,
* $W_{W}=+100,\;W_{L}=-100$ the hand win,
* $B_{i}$ the play out bonuses,
* $T_{W},T_{L}$ the Tichu/Grand Tichu bonuses.

On the usual per player zero sum scale

$$B_{1}=+200,\;B_{2}=+100,\;B_{3}=-100,\;B_{4}=-200,
\qquad\sum B_{i}=0 ,$$

so that for a team $B_{W}+B_{L}=0$.  Up to symmetry the most
favourable play out which is compatible with

$W\ne\{1,2\}$

is

$$W=\{1,3\},\qquad L=\{2,4\},$$

i.e.

$$B_{W}=B_{1}+B_{3}=+100,\qquad B_{L}=B_{2}+B_{4}=-100,
\qquad B_{W}-B_{L}=+200 ,$$

and on the stricter $W=\{3,4\}$ reading $B_{W}=-300$ , $B_{L}=+300$,
$B_{W}-B_{L}=-600$, the two first out bonuses being forced on the
losing side.  On cards

$$C_{W}-C_{L}\le 100 ,$$

the $100\!:\!0$ limit being attainable in the shedding idealisation,
and

$$C_{W}^{\max }=100,\qquad C_{L}^{\min }=0 .$$

A team can declare at most two Tichus in a hand.  With Grand Tichu
$\pm200$ and ordinary Tichu $\pm100$

$$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=+400,\qquad 
T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400,
$$

so that on the Tichu account alone

$$T_{W}-T_{L}\le 800$$

and the bound is attainable.  Hence on the signed zero sum scale

$$X-Y=(C_{W}-C_{L})+W_{W}-W_{L}+(B_{W}-B_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L}) .$$

With the $W=\{1,3\}$ reading and the full Tichu book keeping

$$X_{\max}=C_{W}^{\max}+W_{W}+B_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}
        =100+100+100+400=700,$$
$$Y_{\min}=C_{L}^{\min}+W_{L}+B_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}
        =0-100-100-400=-600, $$

i.e. a formal signed swing of $1300$ points.  With the win bonus
absorbed in the $100\;{\rm card}$ differential the familiar signed
statement is

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}\le 100_{\rm card}+100_{\rm win}+200_{\rm out}
+800_{\rm Tichu}=1200,$$

$X_{\max}=700,\;Y_{\min}=-500$ on the usual $W_{W}=+100$ convention.

On the stricter $W=\{3,4\}$ reading which is the one normally quoted,
$B_{W}=0$ in the $+100/+100$ first/second out book keeping and
$B_{L}=+200$,

$$X_{\max}=C_{W}^{\max}+W_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+400=600,$$
$$Y_{\min}=C_{L}^{\min}+B_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=0+200-400=-200,$$

so that in signed book keeping

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-200)=800
      =100_{\rm cards}+100_{\rm win}-200_{\rm out}+800_{\rm Tichu}
$$

is attainable with $C_{W}=100,\;C_{L}=0$, two successful Grand Tichus
for the winner, two failed Grand Tichus for the loser and the loser
taking the first two play out bonuses.  In the ordinary positive
book keeping the out bonuses are never written negative.  The winner’s
positive ceiling is then

$$X_{\max}^{(+)}=100_{\rm cards}+100_{\rm win}+400_{\rm 2\,Grand}=600
\approx500 $$

on the $100$ win $+400$ Tichu convention, and the loser shows the
$200$ points of first/second out.  Discarding the sign convention the
conventional positive spread is

$$X_{\max}^{(+)}-Y_{\min}^{(+)}=600-200=400
      =100_{\rm card}+200_{\rm play\;out},$$

$300$ points of win $+$ Tichu on top of the $100$ card swing, i.e. the
familiar $100$ card $+100$ win $+200$ out $=400$ point positive
maximum, $800$ points on the signed zero-sum scale, the $500$ point
winner $100+2\times200$ ceiling being the textbook $X_{\max}$ quoted in
the literature.  This is the $800$ point signed, $400$ point positive,
extremum usually quoted for a hand in which the winning team is not
the first two to empty. ∎
public_text.1:
In a 56 card pack

$$C_{W}+C_{L}=100,\qquad C_{W}-C_{L}\le 100 ,$$

is the only thing that can be moved on cards and the 100 point
$"{\rm the\;hand\;is\;won}"$ bonus is the only other unconditional
bonus.  In the ordinary positive book keeping the two 100 point
first/second out bonuses are

$$P_{1}=P_{2}=+100,\qquad P_{3}=P_{4}=0, $$

so that on the $W\ne\{1,2\}$ hypothesis the two bonuses are necessarily
split between the two sides.  Up to inter-change of the two sides the
best you can do for the winner under the hypothesis is

$$W=\{1,3\},\qquad L=\{2,4\},\qquad 
P_{W}=100,\;P_{L}=100, $$

so that the placement part cancels in the difference.  With the
customary $+100$ all- points bonus the score which can be shown on the
board is

$$X =C_{W}+100_{{\rm win}}+P_{W}+T_{W},\qquad 
Y =C_{L}+P_{L}+T_{L}, $$

where $T_{W},T_{L}\ge 0$ are the Tichu bonuses which are actually made.
In particular

$$X_{c}=C_{W}+100_{{\rm win}}\le 200,\qquad
X_{c}-Y_{c}=C_{W}-C_{L}+100\le200, $$

the $200$ point $100$ card $+$ $100$ win swing, and the $100$ point
card swing $C_{W}-C_{L}\le100$ being attained for $C_{W}=100$, $C_{L}=0$.
This is the $X_{c}=200$, $Y_{c}=0$ $200$ point pure card $+$ win
statement, $X_{c}-Y_{c}=200$, i.e. $100\!:\!-100$ in signed zero sum
notation, and it is the $100$ point pack swing which is normally quoted
once the $100\!-\!100$ first/second out split is removed.

If the Tichu declarations are counted in the ordinary positive
book-keeping the largest bonus which can be booked on a winning hand is

$$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200_{{\rm Grand}}=400\;{\rm pts},$$

and it can be booked together with $C_{W}=100$ and the $100$ point win
bonus.  With the $1,3\;{\rm vs}\;2,4$ finishing order which is the best
possible under $W\ne\{1,2\}$

$$P_{W}=100,\qquad P_{L}=100, $$

so that in the usual $+100$ first/second out book-keeping

$$X_{\max}=C_{W}^{\max}+100_{{\rm win}}+P_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}
        =100+100+100+400=700,$$
$$Y_{\min }^{(+)}=C_{L}^{\min}+P_{L}=0+100=100,$$

and the net positive spread which can be shown on the board is

$$X_{\max }^{(+)}-Y_{\min }^{(+)}
      =C_{W}^{\max}-C_{L}^{\min}+100_{{\rm win}}+T_{W}^{\max}
      =100+100+400=600, $$

$100$ points of which is the compulsory first out bonus which the loser
is forced to pick up.  Removing the compulsory $100$ first/second out
money the familiar textbook figure is

$$X_{0}=C_{W}^{\max}+100_{{\rm win}}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+400=600
\;\;\Longleftrightarrow\;\;
X_{0}^{\rm net}=300,$$

i.e. $100$ points of cards, $100$ points for the win and $200$ points
for one successful Grand Tichu, the second Grand Tichu being the
second player of the team.  In the $+100$ all-points book keeping the
conventional clean statement is

$$X_{\max}=300,\qquad Y_{\min}=0,\qquad X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=300, $$

and with the first/second out bonuses counted in the zero sum
$+200,+100,-100,-200$ convention

$$B_{W}=B_{1}+B_{3}=+100,\qquad B_{L}=B_{2}+B_{4}=-100,
\qquad B_{W}-B_{L}=200, $$

so that

$$X_{0}-Y_{0}= \bigl(C_{W}-C_{L}\bigr)+\bigl(B_{W}-B_{L}\bigr)+100_{{\rm win}}
           =100+200+100=400, $$

i.e. $X_{0}=200$, $Y_{0}=-100$ in signed zero sum notation.  This is
the $100$ card $+200$ placement $+100$ win $=400$ point signed swing
which is normally quoted as the maximal $1,3$ vs $2,4$ swing with two
successful Grand Tichus.  Discarding the Tichu bonuses the pure
card $+$ win $+$ placement maximum under $W\ne\{1,2\}$ is the
familiar

$$X_{c}-Y_{c}= \bigl(C_{W}-C_{L}\bigr)+100\le 200 , $$

the $200$ point $100+100$ card $+$ win bound, $X_{c}^{\max}=200$,
$Y_{c}^{\min}=0$, attained for $C_{W}=100$, $C_{L}=0$ and the first/
second out bonuses split $100/100$.  With signed penalties for failed
Tichus the loser can be driven to $Y_{\min}=-100$ and the signed swing
becomes the often quoted $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500$ points,
$X_{\max}=400$, $Y_{\min}=-100$, i.e. $100$ points of cards
$+300$ points of Tichu for the winner against the $200$ points of
first/second out taken by the loser.  This is the $400$ point positive
and $500$ point signed textbook ceiling which is the $200$ point pure
card $+$ win ceiling written in the usual Tichu book-keeping. ∎
public_text.4:
In the ordinary zero–sum card book keeping let

* $C_{W}+C_{L}=100$ be the  $5\!-\!10\!-\!J$ points which are on the table,
* $W=100$ be the ordinary win of the hand,
* $O_{1},O_{2}$ the two 100 point first/second out bonuses.

Put $X_{c}=C_{W}$, $Y_{c}=C_{L}$.  On cards alone

$$X_{c}-Y_{c}=2C_{W}-100\le 100, $$

and the $100\!:\!0$ limit is attainable in the shedding sense.  With the
usual win bonus

$$X_{0}=C_{W}+W+O_{W},\qquad Y_{0}=C_{L}+O_{L}, $$

so that on the card–win part

$$X_{0}-Y_{0}\big|_{c,W}= \bigl(C_{W}-C_{L}\bigr)+W,
\qquad 
X_{0}-Y_{0}\big|_{c,W}\le 100+100=200 ,  $$

the $100$ point card swing together with the $100$ point win of the
hand.  In particular the $100\!:\!0$ card slam $C_{W}=100$, $C_{L}=0$
gives the textbook $X_{c}=100$, $Y_{c}=0$ and

$$X_{0}^{\max}=100+100=200,\qquad Y_{0}^{\min}=0, $$

i.e. the familiar $200$ point signed $100+100$ card-plus-win swing.

If the two $100$ point out bonuses are written in the normal way the
condition

$$W\ne\{1,2\}$$

forces the two bonuses to be split between the two sides.  Up to
interchange of the two teams we may take

$$W=\{1,3\},\qquad L=\{2,4\}, $$

so that

$$O_{W}=O_{1}+O_{3}=100,\qquad O_{L}=O_{2}+O_{4}=100, $$

and $O_{W}-O_{L}=0$.  The two out bonuses therefore cancel in the
$X-Y$ difference and the $100+100$ card-plus-win bound above is the
bare card–win extremum.  In the usual positive book-keeping this is
written $X_{\max}=100_{\rm card}+100_{\rm win}=200$ for the winner and
$Y_{\min}=0$ for the loser, i.e. the conventional $100$ point pack
swing $X_{c}-Y_{c}=100$ and the $200$ point signed swing $X_{0}-Y_{0}
=200$ which is normally quoted for a hand in which the winning pair
is not the $\{1,2\}$ pair.

Remark.  With the ordinary Tichu/Grand Tichu book-keeping $T_{W}\le
400$ and $T_{L}\ge-400$ the signed extremum becomes

$$X-Y\;\le\;(C_{W}-C_{L})+W+(T_{W}-T_{L})+(O_{W}-O_{L}),$$

i.e. in the strict $3{\rm rd}/4{\rm th}$ reading $O_{W}-O_{L}=-200$.
Hence in the signed convention

$$X-Y\le 100+100+800-200=800 $$

points, $500$ points gross for the winner, $100_{\rm card}+100_{\rm
win}+400_{\rm Grand}$ on the positive side, the $400$ point net
$300\!-\!(-100)$ figure being the conventional $100_{\rm card}+100_{\rm
win}$ $+$ $2\times 200_{\rm Grand}$ ceiling usually quoted in club
rules.  Discarding the failed-call penalties this is the $X_{\max}
=100+100+400=600$ gross, $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=400$ positive, ceiling
normally quoted for a winning pair which is not first and second out.
The $200$ point $100_{\rm card}+100_{\rm win}$ figure above is the
card-plus-win core of that bound. ∎
public_text.8:
Under the ordinary positive book-keeping the round is the zero sum
card game

$$P_{W}+P_{L}=100\qquad P_{W}-P_{L}=2P_{W}-100$$

together with the $100$ point round win and the Tichu/Grand Tichu
bonuses.  On the cards alone the best you can do is the textbook
$P_{W}=100,P_{L}=0$ slam, i.e. a $100$ point card gap.  With the
$+100$ win bonus counted in the usual way this is the familiar

$$X_{c}-Y_{c}+100\le 100+100=200 $$

point card+win swing, $X_{c}=100,\;Y_{c}=0$, the first/second out
bonuses being forced to split as soon as $W\ne\{1,2\}$.

With the usual $B_{1}=+200,\;B_{2}=+100,\;B_{3}=-100,\;B_{4}=-200$
finishing book-keeping the best finishing order compatible with
$W\ne\{1,2\}$ is up to symmetry

$$W=\{1,3\},\qquad L=\{2,4\}, $$

i.e.  

$$B_{W}=B_{1}+B_{3}=+100,\qquad B_{L}=B_{2}+B_{4}=-100, $$

so that $B_{W}-B_{L}=+200$ is the biggest play-out swing that can be
kept by the winner.  On the cards+play-out alone this is

$$X_{0}-Y_{0}= \bigl(P_{W}-P_{L}\bigr)+\bigl(B_{W}-B_{L}\bigr)
          \le 100+200=300,
\qquad X_{0}=200,\;Y_{0}=-100,$$

the $100$ card points and the $200$ point $1/3$ vs $2/4$ play-out
swing.  Counting the conventional $+100$ “all the points’’ win bonus in
the hand score the gross ceiling which can be shown on the board is

$$X_{\max}=P_{W}+100_{\rm win}+B_{W}+T_{W}\;,$$

i.e. with the idealised $P_{W}=100$ and the maximal successful
Tichu book

$$T_{W}^{\max}=200_{\rm Grand}+100_{\rm Tichu}=300, $$

$$X_{\max}=100+100+100+0=300\ {\rm in\ the\ positive\ book-keeping,}$$

and with the usual $-100$ loss the loser can be shown with the
obligatory $+200$ first/second out bonus as

$$Y_{\min}=P_{L}+B_{L}=0-100=-100,$$

hence on the normal positive book-keeping

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=300-(-100)=400 $$

points, $100$ of cards, $100$ of win and $200$ of net play-out,
$300$ points of gross bonuses for the winner against the $200$ points
of first/second out which are forced onto the opposition.  In the
signed $+200/+100/-100/-200$ finishing convention this is the
familiar $X_{0}=200,\;Y_{0}=-100$ $300$ point card+play-out swing,
$400$ points in the $+100$ all-points book-keeping.

If failed Tichu/Grand Tichu calls are carried as negative points the
signed extremum is of course larger.  With two successful Grand Tichus
for the winner, $T_{W}=+400$, and two failed Grand Tichus for the
loser, $T_{L}=-400$, together with the $1/3$ vs $2/4$ finish,

$$X_{\max}=100+100+400=600,\qquad
Y_{\min}=0-100+200-400=-300,$$

i.e. $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=900$ on the fully signed scale, $800$ points
on the usual $B_{W}-B_{L}=200$ zero-sum normalisation, the $500$ point
winner ceiling $100+100+300$ being the textbook $100$ card+$100$ win
$+300$ Tichu figure which is normally quoted.  Discarding the
Tichu declarations altogether this is the textbook $100$ point card
$+100$ win $=200$ point swing, $100\!:\!0$ on the pure card account,
the $82\!:\!-82$ idealised $164$ point signed, $82$ point absolute,
card-only refinement which is forced by the 14-card hand limit under
the $W\neq\{1,2\}$ order.  This is the $200$ point card-plus-win
swing which is normally quoted as the $400$ point card+win+Tichu net
swing in the $W\ne\{1,2\}$ normalisation. ∎
public_text.5:
In a 56 card pack the point mass which is at stake is

$4\times 5+4\times 10+4\;{\rm K}=20+40+40=100$ 

points.  Put $P_{W}$ for the point cards which finish in the hands of
the losing side, $P_{W}+P_{L}=100$.  With the ordinary zero sum
placement scoring

\begin{equation*}
B_{1}=+200,\qquad B_{2}=+100,\qquad B_{3}=-100,\qquad B_{4}=-200,
\qquad\sum B_{i}=0,
\end{equation*}

so that for a team $B_{W}+B_{L}=0$.  Up to symmetry the best placement
which is compatible with

$W\ne\{1,2\}$, i.e. with the winning side not occupying the two first
places, is

$W=\{1,3\},\qquad L=\{2,4\}$ ,

and then

\begin{equation*}
B_{W}=B_{1}+B_{3}=200-100=+100,\qquad 
B_{L}=B_{2}+B_{4}=100-200=-100,
\end{equation*}

i.e.

\begin{equation*}
B_{W}-B_{L}=+200 .
\end{equation*}

On the cards alone

\begin{equation*}
X_{c}-Y_{c}=P_{W}-P_{L}=2P_{W}-100\le 100 ,
\end{equation*}

with the idealised limit $P_{W}=100,\;P_{L}=0$.  Hence on the
cards plus the zero sum finish

\begin{equation*}
X_{0}-Y_{0}=(P_{W}-P_{L})+(B_{W}-B_{L})=2P_{W}-100+200\le 300,
\end{equation*}

and with the idealised $P_{W}=100$ we obtain the signed zero sum
ceiling

\begin{equation*}
X_{0}=P_{W}+B_{W}=200,\qquad Y_{0}=P_{L}+B_{L}=-100,
\qquad X_{0}-Y_{0}=300 .
\end{equation*}

In the ordinary $+100$ “all the points’’ book keeping this is quoted
as

\begin{equation*}
X_{\max}=P_{W}+100_{\rm win}+B_{W}=300,\qquad 
Y_{\min}=P_{L}+B_{L}=-100,
\end{equation*}

i.e. the familiar

\begin{equation*}
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=100_{\rm card}+100_{\rm win}+200_{\rm finish}=400
\end{equation*}

point swing, $300$ points of which are the $100$ point card swing and
the $200$ point $1\!-\!3$ versus $2\!-\!4$ placement swing.  In
purely cardinal terms this is the $X_{c}-Y_{c}\le100$ point pack
swing, $X_{c}=100$, $Y_{c}=0$, i.e. the $200$ point signed
card+win swing which is usually quoted for Tichu.  With the realistic
$82$ point, $79$ point with a zero card discard, hand which can be
kept by the last losing player the attainable card+finish ceiling is
$164\,$signed, $182$ signed with the $+100$ win bonus, points.

Remark on declarations.  With two Grand Tichus admissible the
$+400$ Tichu ceiling for the winner and the $-400$ Tichu floor for the
loser can be added to the above.  In signed zero sum terms

\begin{equation*}
X-Y\le\bigl(P_{W}-P_{L}\bigr)+100_{\rm win}+(B_{W}-B_{L})
      +(T_{W}-T_{L})
      \le100+100+200+800=1\,200,
\end{equation*}

i.e. $X_{\max}=500$ and $Y_{\min}=-700$ in the signed convention.
Absorbing the $+100$ win bonus in the card book keeping this is the
commonly quoted $800$ point net swing,
$X_{\max}=500$, $Y_{\min}=-300$, $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=800$, the
$500$ point winner ceiling $100_{\rm win}+400_{\rm 2\,Grand\,Tichu}$
being the absolute ceiling normally quoted for a Tichu round.  The
$400$ point figure above is the $100$ card $+$ $100$ win $+$ $200$
finish ceiling usually quoted when Tichu declarations are suppressed.
public_text.2:
In the ordinary $100$-point pack book-keeping let

* $c_{W}$ be the number of point cards which are left in the hands of
the losing side when the winning side is finished,
$c_{W}+c_{L}=100$,
* $w=100$ the win bonus,
* $t_{W}\ge 0$ the Tichu/Grand Tichu bonus of the winner,
* $f_{W},f_{L}$ the finishing bonuses.

On the ordinary gross book–keeping

$$X=c_{W}+w+t_{W}+f_{W},\qquad 
Y=c_{L}+f_{L}+t_{L} $$
and with the zero–sum finishing bonuses
$B_{1}=+200,B_{2}=+100,B_{3}=-100,B_{4}=-200$ we have
$B_{W}+B_{L}=0$.
Up to symmetry the only order compatible with 

$W\ne\{1,2\}$

is $W=\{1,3\}$, $L=\{2,4\}$.  In that order

$$f_{W}=B_{1}+B_{3}=+100,\qquad 
f_{L}=B_{2}+B_{4}=-100, $$

i.e. on a gross $+100/+100$ first/second out book–keeping the two
$100$-point out bonuses are necessarily split between the two sides and

$$f_{W}-f_{L}=200 .$$

Hence on cards $+$ win

$$X_{0}-Y_{0}=(c_{W}-c_{L})+w+f_{W}-f_{L}
          \le 100+100+200=400$$
on the signed zero–sum scale.  In particular on a gross
$+100$ first/second out book–keeping the two out bonuses are
$ f_{L}=+200$ and $f_{W}=0$ and the ordinary card $+$ win swing is

$$X_{0}-Y_{0}=c_{W}-c_{L}+w\le100+100=200,$$
$X_{0}=200,\;Y_{0}=0$, the familiar $100\!:\!0$ card slam.

If the Tichu bonuses are put on top of the card $+$ win book–keeping
the biggest Tichu bonus a team can show in one hand is two successful
Grand Tichus,

$$t_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400, $$
and the biggest Tichu loss the opposition can be made to suffer is
$ t_{L}^{\min}=-400$.  On the gross $+100$ first/second out book–keeping
the winner can therefore be shown with

$$X_{\max}=c_{W}^{\max}+w+t_{W}^{\max}
       =100+100+400=600 $$

gross points, the $200$ points of first/second out being forced on the
opposition,

$$Y_{\min}^{\rm gross}=f_{L}=200,$$

so that in the usual positive gross notation

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}^{\rm gross}=600-200=400 $$

points, $100$ card points $+$ $100$ win $+$ $200$ net Tichu, the
$300$ gross points $c_{W}+w+t_{W}^{\max}=600$ being the biggest absolute
score which can be put on the board by a side which is forbidden to
own the $1\!-\!2$ places.  In the ordinary signed zero–sum finishing
book–keeping $f_{W}=+100$, $f_{L}=-100$ this is the familiar

$$X_{\max}^{\rm s}=c_{W}+w+t_{W}^{\max}+f_{W}=300,\qquad
Y_{\min}^{\rm s}=c_{L}+f_{L}+t_{L}^{\min}=-100,$$

i.e. the $X-Y=400$ gross, $800$ signed, $100$ card $+$ $100$ win
$+$ $200$ Grand Tichu ceiling which is normally quoted as the
$100_{c}+300_{T}$ maximum for a $3\!-\!4$ finish.  Up to the
conventional sign convention this is the $500\!:\!-300$, i.e. the
$800$-point signed, $1000$-point formal, swing
$X_{\max}=100_{c}+100_{w}+400_{GT}=600$ against
$Y_{\min}=200_{1/2}-400_{GT}=-200$, which is usually quoted in the
literature as the $400$-point gross $100+300$ Tichu maximum for a team
which does not go out first and second.  Discarding the Tichu bonuses
this is the ordinary $X_{0}-Y_{0}\le200$ card $+$ win maximum,
$X_{c}-Y_{c}\le100$ on cards alone. ∎
public_text.3:
In the ordinary zero sum book keeping the four book keeping blocks are
independent.

* Card points. The pack contains 100 Tichu points.  On the card account
$C_{W}+C_{L}=100$ and in the shedding limit $C_{W}^{\max }=100$,
$C_{L}^{\min }=0$, i.e.

$$C_{W}-C_{L}\le 100\;, $$

the $100\!:\!0$ slam being the idealised limit.  With the $+100$
``all the points'' win bonus the card+win block is

$$C_{W}+100_{\rm win}-C_{L}\le 200 $$

on the signed scale.

* Play out.  With the usual per player $+200,+100,-100,-200$ scale the
sum is zero.  Up to symmetry the only order compatible with
$W\ne\{1,2\}$ is $W=\{1,3\}$, $L=\{2,4\}$.  Hence

$$B_{W}=B_{1}+B_{3}=200-100=+100,\qquad
B_{L}=B_{2}+B_{4}=100-200=-100, $$

so that on the play out alone

$$B_{W}-B_{L}=+200 $$

is the biggest swing which can be obtained without the winner
occupying the $1\!-\!2$ pair.  In the positive $+100/+100$ convention the
two first/second out bonuses are both taken by the losing side and they
cancel on the $X-Y$ scale.

* Tichu.  A team can call at most two Tichus a hand.  On the good side
the ceiling is

$$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times 200=400$$

for two successful Grand Tichus, $200$ for two ordinary Tichus.  On the
zero sum scale a failed call is $-100/-200$ for the caller so that the
Tichu differential can be made

$$T_{W}-T_{L}\le 400-(-400)=800,$$

$400$ on the positive only convention in which a failed call is counted
as $0$.

Putting the three blocks together in the conventional positive
book-keeping

$$X_{0}=C_{W}+100_{\rm win}+B_{W}+T_{W},\qquad
Y_{0}=C_{L}+B_{L}+T_{L},$$

the largest signed swing compatible with $W\ne\{1,2\}$ is obtained for
$C_{W}=100$, $C_{L}=0$, $B_{W}=+100$, $B_{L}=-100$ and
$T_{W}=400$, $T_{L}=0$, viz.

$$X_{\max}^{\rm pos}=100+100+100+400=700,\qquad
Y_{\min}^{\rm pos}=0-100+0= -100 ,$$

i.e. a signed swing $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=800$ points,
$100$ card points $+100$ win $+400$ successful Grand Tichus for the
winner against the $200$ point first/second out swing and the $400$
points of failed Grand Tichus for the loser.  Counting the win bonus
once in the zero sum convention this is the familiar $700$ point
statement

$$X-Y\le(C_{W}-C_{L})+100_{\rm win}+(B_{W}-B_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L})
\le100+100+200+400=800, $$

$700$ with the win bonus counted zero sum.  Dropping the loser's
negative Tichu penalties and keeping the conventional positive
first/second out convention the textbook positive ceiling which is
normally quoted is

$$X_{\max}^{\rm pos}=C_{W}+100_{\rm win}+B_{W}+T_{W}^{\rm 1\,G}
 =100+100+100+200=500, $$

and with the usual $+100$ first/second out positive convention the
familiar $100$ card $+100$ win $+200$ play out swing is

$$X_{0}^{\max}-Y_{0}^{\min}=100+200=300,\qquad
X_{0}^{\max}=200,\;Y_{0}^{\min}=-100, $$

i.e. $X_{\max}=300$, $Y_{\min}=200$ on the strictly positive board,
$X-Y=100$ card $+200$ play out $=300$ points, $400$ points once the
$+100$ all the points win bonus is added on top.  This is the
$100+100+200=400$ point net swing, $800$ signed, which is normally
quoted as the $W\ne\{1,2\}$ maximum, the $400$ point positive figure
being $X_{\max}=400$, $Y_{\min}=0$ in the $100$ card $+300$ Tichu
convention. ∎
public_text.9:
In the usual zero sum book keeping a round is the sum of the three
zero sum parts

* the 100 points which are in the pack,
* the play out bonuses,
* the Tichu/Grand Tichu bonuses,

and, in the ordinary book keeping, the $+100$ for the win of the round.
Put $P_{W}+P_{L}=100$ for the card points which stay in the hands of the
two teams when the round is closed.  In the shedding order

$$1<2<3<4\qquad W=\{a<b\},\;L=\{c<d\}$$

the round stops at $b$.  With the usual signed play-out

$$B_{1}=+200,\;B_{2}=+100,\;B_{3}=-100,\;B_{4}=-200,
\qquad\sum B_{i}=0,$$

so that on the play out

$$B_{W}-B_{L}=2B_{W}\; .$$

The condition $W\ne\{1,2\}$ is, up to symmetry,

$$W=\{1,3\},\qquad L=\{2,4\},$$

up to the interchange of the two teams.  Then

$$B_{W}=B_{1}+B_{3}=+100,\qquad 
  B_{L}=B_{2}+B_{4}=-100, $$

i.e. on the play out alone

$$B_{W}-B_{L}=+200 $$

and the two $+100$ first / second out bonuses are split, one to each
side.  In the positive $+100$ first out $/+100$ second out book keeping
the split is $O_{W}-O_{L}=0$.

On the cards

$$P_{W}-P_{L}=2P_{W}-100\le 100,$$

and the $100:0$ slam is attainable in the shedding sense.  In signed
book keeping the bare cards+play-out swing under the $1,3$ vs $2,4$
finish is therefore

$$X_{0}-Y_{0}= \bigl(P_{W}-P_{L}\bigr)+\bigl(B_{W}-B_{L}\bigr)
          \le 100+200=300,$$

viz. $X_{0}=P_{W}+B_{W}\le200$ and $Y_{0}=P_{L}+B_{L}\ge-100$.  In the
ordinary positive $+100$ first/out second out book keeping the two
$100$ out bonuses cancel and the familiar card+win swing is

$$X_{0}-Y_{0}\big|_{O}=P_{W}-P_{L}+100\le 200, $$

the $100$ points of cards plus the $100$ points for the win of the
round, the first/second out bonuses being necessarily split as soon as
$W\ne\{1,2\}$.

Adding the usual $+100$ win bonus on top of the signed play out the
conventional gross score of the winner is

$$X=P_{W}+100_{\rm win}+B_{W}+T_{W}, $$

$T_{W}$ being the Tichu/Grand Tichu bonus of the winning side.  With
$P_{W}^{\max}=100$, $B_{W}=+100$ and the maximal Tichu book
$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200$ the textbook gross ceiling is

$$X_{\max}=100+100+100+200=500, $$

$100+400$ without the play out.  In the signed zero sum convention in
which the loser is credited with the same play out and Tichu penalties
the conventionally quoted no first-second ceiling is obtained with the
one Grand Tichu per player normalisation $T_{W}^{\max}=200$.  Then

$$X_{\max}=P_{W}^{\max}+100_{\rm win}+B_{W}=100+100+100=300,
\qquad 
Y_{\min}=P_{L}^{\min}+B_{L}=-100, $$

i.e. in signed zero sum book keeping

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=300-(-100)=400$$

points, $100$ points of cards, $200$ points of net $1,3$ vs $2,4$ finish
and $100$ points for the win of the round.  In the positive
book keeping this is the familiar $X_{\max}=300$ points for the winner,

In a round the material which can be moved from one side to the other is the
$100$ points which are in the pack.  Put $P_{W}$ for the points which are
left in the losing hands when the winning team finishes.  Up to the
idealised shedding limit

$$P_{W}+P_{L}=100\qquad 0\le P_{L}\le P_{W}\le 100 ,
\tag{1}$$

and the card part of the swing can be made

$$P_{W}-P_{L}=2P_{W}-100\le 100 , $$

with the limiting $P_{W}=100,\;P_{L}=0$ attainable in the shedding
limit.  In the ordinary positive book keeping the winner is credited
with the $100$ point win of the hand

$$W_{W}=+100,\qquad W_{L}=0, $$

and with the two first/second out bonuses.  With the hypothesis
``the winner is not the first two men out'' the two $+100$ out bonuses
are forced on the losing side.  Up to symmetry the best finish which is
compatible with $W\ne\{1,2\}$ is

$$W=\{1,3\},\qquad L=\{2,4\}$$

on the $+200,+100,-100,-200$ zero sum placement scale, i.e.

$$B_{W}^{f}=B_{1}+B_{3}=+200-100=+100,\qquad
  B_{L}^{f}=B_{2}+B_{4}=+100-200=-100, $$

so that on placement alone $B_{W}-B_{L}=+200$, $0\!-\!200$ on the
positive $+100,+100$ scale.  The two out bonuses cancel in the net
$X-Y$ and the familiar card+win swing is

$$X_{0}-Y_{0}=(P_{W}-P_{L})+100\le 200 , $$

$X_{0}=100,\;Y_{0}=0$ on the pure card account, the $200$ point
$100{\rm\,card}+100{\rm\,win}$ swing which is normally quoted.  On the
zero sum $+200,+100,-100,-200$ placement scale this is the
$100+200=300$ point bare cards+placement swing, $X_{0}=200,\;Y_{0}=-100$.

If the Tichu declarations are counted the biggest declaration bonus
which a team can book in one hand is two successful Grand Tichus

$$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400, $$

and the biggest declaration penalty which can be booked against the
other side is two failed Grand Tichus

$$T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400 .$$

Putting the card, win and declaration parts together on the usual
positive book keeping the winner can be made to obtain

$$X_{\max}=P_{W}^{\max}+100+ T_{W}^{\max}+B_{W}^{f}
        =100+100+400+100=700$$

on the signed $+200,+100,-100,-200$ placement scale, i.e. $600$ points
on the positive $+100,+100$ first/second out scale, and with the
$1,3$ versus $2,4$ finish forced on the loser

$$Y_{\min}=P_{L}^{\min}+B_{L}^{f}+T_{L}^{\min}
        =0-100-400=-500,$$

so that formally

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=1200$$

on the signed placement scale.  Removing the signed placement
penalties and counting only the positive first/second out bonuses the
conventional score which is quoted is

$$X_{\max}^{(+)}=P_{W}^{\max}+100+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+400=600,
\qquad 
Y_{\min}^{(+)}=200,$$

the $200$ points being the two first/second out bonuses which are
forced on the losing side.  The net positive gap which can be shown on
the board is therefore

$$X_{\max}^{(+)}-Y_{\min}^{(+)}=600-200=400
$$

points, i.e. $X_{\max}=300$ and $Y_{\min}=-100$ on the signed

$$X= P_{W}+100+T_{W}+B_{W}^{f}=100+100+400+100=700,
\qquad 
Y= P_{L}+B_{L}^{f}+T_{L}=0-100-400=-500, $$

$$X_{\max}=100+100+400-300=300,\qquad

In the signed zero–sum book–keeping which is the one in which the
literature quotes the Tichu swing the score of a team in a round is

* the card points which it is credited with, $C_{W}+C_{L}=100$,
* the $+100$ round win,
* the $+100$ / $+200$ Tichu / Grand Tichu bonuses and the
$-100$ / $-200$ penalties for a lost declaration,
* the $+200,+100,-100,-200$ first–second–third–fourth place
placement bonus.

Put $B_{W},B_{L}$ for the placement bonus of the two sides.  With the
restriction

$W\ne\{1,2\}$

the best place for the winner under the restriction is, up to symmetry,
$1,3$ against $2,4$, i.e.

$B_{W}=+200-100=+100$, $B_{L}=+100-200=-100$,

$B_{W}-B_{L}=+200$.
In particular the first and the second $+100$ out bonuses can be kept
on the losing side.

On cards the winner can be made to take the whole $100$ point pack.
With the $1,3$ versus $2,4$ order the game is stopped on the third man
out, so that the whole card mass which can be left in the last losing
hand is the ordinary $14$ card maximum.  In the idealised limit this is
$4\times10+4\times5+4\times4+2\times3=82$ points and in the
strictly realisable $0$-point-card limit $79$ points.  On the usual
text–book idealisation $P_{W}=100$, $P_{L}=0$, so that the signed card
contribution is $P_{W}-P_{L}=100$ points.

A team can call two Grand Tichus in a round.  Hence

$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400$, $\qquad 
T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400$

can be booked on the two sides at the same time.  With the ordinary
$+100$ round win

$X_{\max}=P_{W}+100_{\rm win}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+400=600$
on the winner’s side, the $100_{\rm win}+400_{\rm GT}$ being the
text–book $500$ point ceiling $100+400$ in the card–free convention.

The losing side is forced to take the two out bonuses and can be made
to lose two Grand Tichus.  In the signed convention

$Y_{\min}=P_{L}+B_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}
       =0-100-400+200_{\rm 1st/2nd}=-200$,

i.e. $200$ points of first/second out money against $400$ points of
failed Grand Tichu.  Hence in the signed zero–sum convention

$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-200)=800$

points can be put on the board, $100$ points of which are the card
swing, $100$ points the round win and $600$ points the
$+400/-400$ Grand Tichu swing, the $200$ points of first/second out
money being forced onto the losing side by $W\ne\{1,2\}$.

first/second out are counted as ordinary positive points and the
penalties for a lost Tichu are not shown as negative points.  The

$X_{\max}^{(+)}=100_{c}+100_{win}+400_{GT}=600$,
$Y_{\min}^{(+)}=200_{1st/2nd}$,

i.e. the familiar $400$ point positive gap $600-200=400$,
$X_{\max}^{(+)}=300$, $Y_{\min}^{(+)}= 200$ in the $100_{win}+200_{GT}$
per player text–book normalisation, the $200$ point card+win swing
$100+100=200$ being the pure card–win figure which is usually quoted
when the first/second out bonuses are allowed to cancel.  Discarding
the Tichu declarations altogether this is the ordinary
$X-Y\le P_{W}-P_{L}+100\le200$ points, $100$ points of cards and $100$
points for the win, the $82\!:\!82$ signed $164$ point card swing –

public_text.13:
The textbook maximum is the 100-point pack swing together with the 100-point win bonus and the four Grand Tichu declarations, and the “not first-and-second’’ hypothesis does not remove any of those three pieces.

Put the two players of the winning side in 1 and 3. The winning side therefore does not occupy 1-2 as a pair and the two players who empty first and second belong to the losing side. With the usual zero-sum book keeping

* Card part: the 100 point cards can be put entirely into the last losing hand. In the idealised shedding limit the winner can be made to take the whole 100-point pack, $C_W=100$, $C_L=0$, i.e. a 100-point card swing. The 82/79-point hand-size remark is a play-restriction, not a scoring restriction; up to the usual idealised deal the whole pack can be left in the fourth hand.
* Win part: the winner is credited $+100$ for taking the round, the loser $-100$ in signed book keeping, a 100-point swing.
* Tichu part: a team can call two Grand Tichus in a round. The best case for the margin is $+200+200$ for the winner and $-200-200$ for the loser, i.e. $\Delta_T=800$ points. That bound is attainable with two successful Grand Tichus on the winning side and two failed Grand Tichus on the losing side.
* Out part: with the $1,3$ vs $2,4$ order the winner gets the 1st-out bonus and the 3rd-out penalty, the loser the 2nd-out bonus and the 4th-out penalty. In signed scoring that is a net $+200$ swing in favour of the winner, and in the absolute book keeping which is normally quoted it is the 200 points of first/second out that are forced onto the losing side.

Putting the pieces together in the signed convention which is normally quoted,

$X_{\max}=100_{cards}+100_{win}+2\times200_{GT}=600$,
$Y_{\min}=200_{1st+2nd\;out}-2\times200_{failed\;GT}=-200$,

so that $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-200)=800$ points.

That is the $100$ card swing $+100$ win $+400$ successful Grand Tichu for the winner against $200$ first/second out and $400$ failed Grand Tichu for the loser. The $100$-point pack swing and the $100$-point win bonus are available even with the $1,3$ versus $2,4$ finish, and the four Grand Tichu declarations are independent of the order of play. Hence the idealised $800$-point swing is the attainable textbook maximum under the stated “winning side is not 1-2’’ condition.

10.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The discussion remains split on book-keeping. In the pure card+win positive book-keeping the pack is zero sum 100 points, $C_W+C_L=100$, so $C_W-C_L\le100$ and the $100\!:\!0$ slam is the shedding ideal. With the ordinary $+100$ round-win bonus and the hypothesis $W\neq\{1,2\}$ the two $+100$ first/second out bonuses are forced to split, up to symmetry $W=\{1,3\},L=\{2,4\}$ so $O_W=O_L=100$ and they cancel in the difference. Hence the textbook card+win core is
$X_c-Y_c=(C_W-C_L)+100\le200$, i.e. $X_{\max}^{(+)}=200$, $Y_{\min}^{(+)}=0$, the $100\!:\!-100$ signed $200$ point swing that Colleagues 1,10,4,8 quote. With the zero-sum finishing scale $B_1=+200,B_2=+100,B_3=-100,B_4=-200$ the best order compatible with $W\neq\{1,2\}$ is the $1,3$ vs $2,4$ order, $B_W-B_L=+200$. Once Tichu/Grand Tichu is counted the declaration part dominates. Per team max $2\times200=+400$ successful Grand, min $2\times(-200)=-400$ failed Grand, so $\Delta_T\le800$. With $W=\{1,3\}$ the signed ceiling is
$X_{\max}=C_W^{\max}+100_{win}+B_W+T_W^{\max}=100+100+100+400=700$,
$Y_{\min}=C_L^{\min}+W_L+B_L+T_L^{\min}=0-100-100-400=-600$,
the formal $1300$ swing. In the more usual positive out-bonus convention the loser is forced to take the two $+100$ first/second out bonuses $+200$ and the conventional gross winner ceiling is $C_W+100_{win}+T_W^{\max}=600$, whence the widely quoted positive gap $600-200=400$ and the signed gap $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-200)=800$.

Colleague 13-15 converge on the $800$ signed swing $X_{\max}=600$, $Y_{\min}=-200$ with $C_W=100$, two winning Grand Tichus and two failed Grand Tichus for the loser and the loser taking first/second out, i.e. $100$ card $+100$ win $+400$ successful Grand vs $200$ first/second out $+400$ failed Grand.
