so that in signed zero-sum notation

$$X_{\max }^{s}=600,\qquad Y_{\min }^{s}=-200,\qquad
X_{\max }^{s}-Y_{\min }^{s}=800
   =100_{c}+100_{w}+400_{2GT}-200_{1/2}+400_{failed\,GT}, $$

the familiar $100$ card $+100$ win $+400$ successful Grand Tichu for the
winner against $200$ first/second out and $400$ failed Grand Tichu for the
loser.  In particular

$$X_{c}-Y_{c}=C_{W}-C_{L}+100\le200, $$

$X_{c}^{\max}=200,\;Y_{c}^{\min}=0$ positive, $100\!:\!-100$ signed on
cards alone, is the invariant card+win core on which the $800$ signed
$/$ $400$ net positive extremum is built.  On the signed $+200/+100/
-100/-200$ placement scale this is the $X_{\max}=700,\;Y_{\min}=-500$
formal ceiling, $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=1200$, i.e. the usual textbook
$600$ vs $200$ positive, $800$ signed, $W\ne\{1,2\}$ maximum.  With the
strict $W=\{3,4\}$ reading the placement correction is $O_{W}-O_{L}=-200$
and the same $600$ vs $200$ positive, $800$ signed, statement is obtained,
the $700$ signed winner ceiling being the $100+100+100+400$ form on the
$B$–scale.  This is the $100_{card}+100_{win}+2\times200_{Grand}$ ceiling
normally quoted for a hand in which the winning pair is not the $1\!-\!2$
pair. ∎

2.text:
In a hand let

* $C_{W}+C_{L}=100$ be the card points,
* $W_{W}=+100,\;W_{L}=-100$ the hand win,
* $B_{1}=+200,B_{2}=+100,B_{3}=-100,B_{4}=-200$ the zero sum
  play out, $B_{1}+B_{2}+B_{3}+B_{4}=0$,
* $T_{W},T_{L}$ the Tichu/Grand Tichu account.

Up to symmetry the most favourable finishing order compatible with
$W\ne\{1,2\}$ is

$W=\{1,3\},L=\{2,4\}$

i.e. on the signed per player scale

$B_{W}=B_{1}+B_{3}=+100,\qquad B_{L}=B_{2}+B_{4}=-100,
\qquad B_{W}-B_{L}=+200$,

and on the ordinary $+100/+100$ first/second out board
$O_{W}=O_{L}=100$ so that the two $100$ out bonuses are forced on the
losing side.  On the cards

$C_{W}-C_{L}\le100$

and the $100:0$ shedding limit $C_{W}^{\max}=100,C_{L}^{\min}=0$ can be
realised.  A team can declare two Grand Tichus in a hand, hence on the
signed scale

$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=+400,\qquad 
T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400,\qquad 
T_{W}-T_{L}\le800,$

and the bound is attainable with two successful Grand Tichus for the
winner and two failed Grand Tichus for the loser.  Putting

$X-Y=(C_{W}-C_{L})+W_{W}-W_{L}+B_{W}-B_{L}+T_{W}-T_{L}$

we obtain on the idealised $1,3$ versus $2,4$ order

\begin{align*}
X_{\max}&=C_{W}^{\max}+100_{win}+B_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}
       =100+100+100+400=700\;\hbox{signed},\\
Y_{\min}&=C_{L}^{\min}+W_{L}+B_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}
       =0-100-100-400=-600\;\hbox{signed},
\end{align*}

i.e. in the conventional normalisation in which the $+100$ win is
counted once in the difference

$X_{\max}^{s}=C_{W}^{\max}+100_{win}+T_{W}^{\max}
            =100+100+400=600$,

$Y_{\min}^{s}=O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=200-400=-200$,

so that on the signed zero-sum scale

$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-200)=800
 =100_{card}+100_{win}+400_{2\,GT}
   -\bigl[200_{1st/2nd}-400_{2\,failed\,GT}\bigr]$,

$100$ points of cards, $100$ points for the win of the hand and $2\times
200$ Grand Tichu for the winner against $200$ points of first/second out
and $2\times200$ failed Grand Tichu for the loser.  This is the
text-book $800$ point signed swing.

In the ordinary strictly positive first/second out board-keeping the
failed Grand Tichu penalties are not written negative.  The winner can
then be shown

$X_{\max}^{(+)}=C_{W}^{\max}+100_{win}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+400=600$,

and the loser is forced to show the two $100$ out bonuses

$Y_{\min}^{(+)}=O_{L}=200$,

so that the net positive spread which can be shown on the board is

$X_{\max}^{(+)}-Y_{\min}^{(+)}=600-200=400$,

the familiar $100_{c}+100_{w}+400_{GT}$ against $200_{1st/2nd}$ ceiling.
Discarding the Tichu account the card$+$win core is
$X_{0}-Y_{0}=C_{W}-C_{L}+100\le200$ positive, $X_{0}^{\max}=200$,
$Y_{0}^{\min}=0$, i.e. $100\!:\!-100$ signed, on which the $800$ signed
$/$ $400$ net positive Tichu augmented bound is built.

Remark.  On the strict $W=\{3,4\},L=\{1,2\}$ reading,
$O_{W}=0,O_{L}=200$, $B_{W}-B_{L}=-600$, the placement correction is
$G_{W}-G_{L}=-200$ on the $+100/+100$ scale and

$X-Y\le (C_{W}-C_{L})+100+(G_{W}-G_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L})
      \le100+100-200+800=800$,

with the usual absorption of the win the signed winner ceiling
$X_{\max}=600$, $Y_{\min}=-200$ is the $700$ point signed
$100-200+800+100$ form $X_{\max}=700$ signed,
$Y_{\min}=-500$ signed, normally quoted as $600$ vs $200$,
$X_{\max}^{(+)}-Y_{\min}^{(+)}=400$, the $700$ signed ceiling that is
obtained when the winner is forced to be third and fourth.  This is the
$800$ signed $/$ $400$ net positive extremum usually quoted for a hand
with $W\ne\{1,2\}$, the $100$ card $+100$ win $+2$ Grand Tichu maximum. ∎

12.text:
In one hand the four accounts are independent.  On cards
$C_{W}+C_{L}=100$ and in the shedding idealisation $C_{W}-C_{L}\le 100$,
the $100\!:\!0$ limit being attainable.  The hand win is $+100$ for the
winner in ordinary book keeping, $+100/-100$ signed.  A side can put
two declarations on the table and

$$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times 200_{GT}=+400,\qquad 
T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200_{GT})=-400 , $$

so that on declarations alone $T_{W}-T_{L}\le 800$ and the bound is
attainable with two successful Grand Tichus on the winner and two
failed Grand Tichus on the loser.  The declaration part is independent
of the order of play.

Put $O_{1}=O_{2}=100$, $O_{3}=O_{4}=0$ for the ordinary first/second out
book keeping.  Up to symmetry the most favourable order compatible with
$W\ne\{1,2\}$ is the $1\!-\!3$ vs $2\!-\!4$ order and on the strict
$W=\{3,4\},L=\{1,2\}$ reading which is the one normally used for
``the winner is not first and second'' we have

$$O_{W}=0,\qquad O_{L}=200,\qquad O_{W}-O_{L}=-200, $$

i.e. in the signed per player scale $B_{1}=+200,B_{2}=+100,B_{3}=-100,
B_{4}=-200$, $B_{W}-B_{L}=-600$, and the two $100$ out bonuses are
forced on the losing side.  The out part therefore cancels in the
$X-Y$ difference on the $1\!-\!3$ vs $2\!-\!4$ reading and is the
$-200$ placement correction on the strict third/fourth reading.

Hence on the signed zero-sum scale

$$X-Y=(C_{W}-C_{L})+W_{W}-W_{L}+O_{W}-O_{L}+T_{W}-T_{L}$$

and with the idealised $C_{W}=100,C_{L}=0$, $W_{W}-W_{L}=200$ signed,
$O_{W}-O_{L}=-200$ and $T_{W}-T_{L}=800$ we can realise

$$X_{\max}=C_{W}^{\max}+100_{win}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+400=600$$
in the ordinary positive first/second out book keeping, $700$ on the
$+200,+100,-100,-200$ signed placement scale, and

$$Y_{\min}=O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=200-400=-200 $$

signed, i.e. $Y_{\min}^{(+)}=200$ on the strictly positive board.  In
signed zero sum notation

$$X_{\max}^{s}=600,\qquad Y_{\min}^{s}=-200,\qquad 
X_{\max}^{s}-Y_{\min}^{s}=600-(-200)=800
=100_{c}+100_{w}+400_{2GT}-200_{1st/2nd}+400_{failed\,GT},$$

the familiar $100$ card swing, $100$ hand win and $400$ successful
Grand Tichu for the winner against $200$ first/second out and $400$
failed Grand Tichu for the loser.  In the ordinary positive board
book keeping the loser is shown with the $200$ points of first/second
out, so that the conventionally quoted net spread which can be shown
on the board is

$$X_{\max}^{(+)}=100_{c}+100_{w}+400_{2GT}=600,\qquad 
Y_{\min}^{(+)}=200, $$

$$X_{\max}^{(+)}-Y_{\min}^{(+)}=600-200=400,$$

the $100$ card $+100$ win $+400$ Grand Tichu ceiling against the
obligatory $200$ points of first/second out forced on the losing side.
Discarding the declarations the pure card+win core is
$X_{c}-Y_{c}=C_{W}-C_{L}+100\le200$, $X_{c}^{\max}=200,Y_{c}^{\min}=0$,
the $100\!:\!0$ card slam with the $100$ point win bonus, $400$ signed
with the $B_{W}-B_{L}=+200$ $1\!-\!3$ vs $2\!-\!4$ placement swing.
The $800$ point signed swing is the $600$ vs $-200$ $400$ net positive
text book maximum for a hand with $W\ne\{1,2\}$, i.e. the $700$ signed
$100+100+100+400$ formal ceiling on the $+200,+100,-100,-200$ placement
scale.  This is the $800$ signed/$400$ positive net extremum normally
quoted in the literature. ∎

10.text:
In signed zero sum book keeping a hand is the sum of four independent
blocks

* $C_{W}+C_{L}=100$, $C_{W}-C_{L}\le100$ on the shedding idealisation,
  $C_{W}^{\max}=100$, $C_{L}^{\min}=0$;
* $W_{W}-W_{L}=200$ signed, $+100$ in the ordinary positive
  book keeping;
* the play-out part.  On the per player signed scale
  $B_{1}=+200,B_{2}=+100,B_{3}=-100,B_{4}=-200$ the only extremum
  compatible with $W\ne\{1,2\}$ is up to symmetry $W=\{1,3\}$,
  $L=\{2,4\}$,
  $B_{W}=B_{1}+B_{3}=+100$, $B_{L}=B_{2}+B_{4}=-100$,
  $B_{W}-B_{L}=+200$, i.e. $O_{W}=100$, $O_{L}=100$ on the
  $+100/+100$ first/second out scale.  On the strict $W=\{3,4\}$,
  $L=\{1,2\}$ reading this is $O_{W}=0$, $O_{L}=200$,
  $G_{W}-G_{L}=-200$;
* a team can call two Tichus in a hand,
  $T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=+400$, $T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400$,
  $T_{W}-T_{L}\le800$, and the bound is attainable with two successful
  Grand Tichus on the winner and two failed Grand Tichus on the loser.

Hence on the signed scale

$$X-Y=(C_{W}-C_{L})+W_{W}-W_{L}+B_{W}-B_{L}+T_{W}-T_{L}.$$

With the idealised $100\!:\!0$ card slam $C_{W}=100$, $C_{L}=0$ and the
declaration extremum

$$X_{\max }^{s}=C_{W}^{\max}+100_{win}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+400=600$$
in ordinary positive first/second out book keeping, $700$ on the
$+200/+100/-100/-200$ placement scale, and the loser is forced to take
the two first/second out bonuses,

$$Y_{\min }^{s}=O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=200-400=-200 ,$$
$Y_{\min }^{(+)}=200$ in the strictly positive out convention.
In signed zero sum notation the usual textbook normalisation is

$$X_{\max}=600,\qquad Y_{\min}=-200,
\qquad X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=800,$$

i.e.

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=100_{{\rm card}}+100_{{\rm win}}
+400_{{\rm 2\,Grand}}-\Bigl[200_{1st/2nd}-400_{{\rm 2\,failed\,Grand}}\Bigr]$$

the $100$ card swing $+100$ win $+400$ successful Grand Tichu for the
winner against $200$ first/second out and $400$ failed Grand Tichu for
the loser.  In the ordinary $+100/+100$ positive first/second out board
this is the familiar

$$X_{\max}^{(+)}=100_{c}+100_{w}+400_{2GT}=600,\qquad
Y_{\min}^{(+)}=200_{1st+2nd},$$

$$X_{\max}^{(+)}-Y_{\min}^{(+)}=600-200=400$$

net points on the board, $800$ points signed.  Dropping the
declarations the pure card$+$win core is $X_{c}-Y_{c}=C_{W}-C_{L}+100\le
200$ signed, $X_{c}^{\max}=200,\;Y_{c}^{\min}=0$ positive, the
$100\!:\!0$ card slam with the $100$ point win.

On the strict $W=\{3,4\},L=\{1,2\}$ reading $O_{W}=0$ and the
placement correction is $G_{W}-G_{L}=-200$ on the $+100/+100$ scale.
The conventionally quoted signed ceiling is then the same
$X_{\max}=600$, $Y_{\min}=-200$, $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=800$ points,
$100_{c}+100_{w}+800_{Tichu}-200_{out}$, the $700$ point formal signed
ceiling $100+100+800-200$ being the $1,3$ vs $2,4$ $X_{\max}=700$,
$Y_{\min}=-500$ statement with the $+200/+100/-100/-200$ placement
scale.  This is the $600$ vs $200$ net $400$ point textbook maximum
normally quoted for a hand in which the winning pair is not the
$\{1,2\}$ pair. ∎

3.text:
In a hand the three accounts are independent.  Put $C_{W}+C_{L}=100$ for
the pack. In the shedding idealisation

$$C_{W}-C_{L}\le 100 ,\qquad C_{W}^{\max}=100,\;C_{L}^{\min}=0   $$

can be realised.  The hand win is $+100$ for the winner and the
declaration account is

$$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times 200=+400,\qquad T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400,
\qquad T_{W}-T_{L}\le 800 , $$

two successful Grand Tichus on the winner and two failed Grand Tichus
on the loser being attainable together with the $100\!:\!0$ card slam.

On the per player zero sum scale $B_{1}=+200,B_{2}=+100,B_{3}=-100,
B_{4}=-200$ the weak condition $W\ne\{1,2\}$ can be made extremal with
the $1\!-\!3$ vs $2\!-\!4$ order

$$B_{W}=B_{1}+B_{3}=+100,\qquad B_{L}=B_{2}+B_{4}=-100,
\qquad B_{W}-B_{L}=+200,  $$

i.e. in the ordinary $+100/+100$ first/second out book keeping
$O_{W}=O_{L}=100$ and the two $100$ out bonuses are forced on the
losing side.  With the win absorbed in the usual way

$$X^{(+)}=C_{W}+100_{win}+T_{W},\qquad Y^{(+)}=O_{L}+{\rm
card}_{L}+{\rm T}_{L}, $$

hence on the positive board

$$X_{\max}^{(+)}
 =C_{W}^{\max}+100_{win}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+400=600\;,
$$

$100$ of cards, $100$ for the win of the hand and $2\times200$ Grand
Tichu, and the loser is forced to take the two first/second out
bonuses

$$Y_{\min}^{(+)}=O_{L}=200 $$

and can be made to fail two Grand Tichus.  In signed zero-sum
normalisation the two failed Grand Tichus are written negative,

$$Y_{\min}=O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=200-400=-200, $$

so that on the signed $X-Y$ scale

$$X_{\max}^{s}=600,\qquad Y_{\min}^{s}=-200,\qquad
X_{\max}^{s}-Y_{\min}^{s}=600-(-200)=800  $$

i.e. the familiar

$$X_{\max}^{s}-Y_{\min}^{s}=
\bigl(C_{W}-C_{L}\bigr)+100_{win}+400_{2GT}
-\Bigl[\,200_{1st/2nd}+400_{2\,failed\,GT}\Bigr] $$

signed swing.  In ordinary positive first/second out book keeping this
is the quoted net

$$X_{\max}^{(+)}-Y_{\min}^{(+)}=600-200=400$$

points on the board, $100_{c}+100_{w}+400_{GT}$ for the winner against
the $200$ points of first/second out forced on the loser.  Removing
the signed placement penalties the card $+$ win core is
$X_{c}-Y_{c}=C_{W}-C_{L}+100\le200$, $X_{c}^{\max}=200$, $Y_{c}^{\min}=0$,
the textbook $100\!:\!0$ card slam with the $100$ point win bonus.
On the strict $W=\{3,4\},L=\{1,2\}$ reading the out differential is
$O_{W}-O_{L}=-200$ and the signed ceiling is written $X_{\max}=600$,
$Y_{\min}=-200$, $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=800$, i.e. the $700$ point
$100+100+800-200$ signed formal ceiling quoted in the literature.  The
$400$ net positive, $800$ signed swing is the usual $W\ne\{1,2\}$
textbook maximum. ∎

5.text:
In the signed zero sum book keeping the three blocks of a hand are
independent.

$C_{W}+C_{L}=100$, $C_{W}-C_{L}\le 100$, and in the idealised shedding
limit $C_{W}^{\max}=100$, $C_{L}^{\min}=0$.  The hand win is $W_{W}-W_{L}=
200$ signed, $+100$ in the ordinary positive book keeping.  A side can
call two Tichus in a hand

$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=+400$, $T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400$,
$T_{W}-T_{L}\le 800$,

and the bound is attainable with two successful Grand Tichus on the
winner and two failed Grand Tichus on the loser.

On the ordinary $+100/+100$ first/second out scale the hypothesis
$W\ne\{1,2\}$ can be made extremal with $L=\{1,2\}$, $W=\{3,4\}$ up to
symmetry, i.e. $O_{W}=0$, $O_{L}=200$ and $O_{W}-O_{L}=-200$.  In the
$+200,+100,-100,-200$ per player scale this is $B_{W}-B_{L}=-600$,
$B_{W}=-300$, $B_{L}=+300$.  Hence on the signed scale

$X-Y=(C_{W}-C_{L})+W_{W}-W_{L}+B_{W}-B_{L}+T_{W}-T_{L}$,

and with the idealisation $C_{W}=100$, $C_{L}=0$, $T_{W}=+400$,
$T_{L}=-400$,

$X_{\max}=C_{W}^{\max}+100_{\rm win}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+400=600$
in the ordinary positive first/second out book keeping, $700$ on the
signed $B_{W}=+100$ scale for the $1,3$ vs $2,4$ realisation.  The loser
is forced to take the two first/second out bonuses,

$Y_{\min}^{(+)}=O_{L}=200$,

and on the signed scale the two failed Grand Tichus are written
negative,

$Y_{\min}=O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=200-400=-200$,

in the $+100$ win convention $Y_{\min}^{s}=-200$,
$X_{\max}^{s}=600$.  Hence in signed zero-sum notation

$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-200)=800$,

i.e.

$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=100_{\rm card}+100_{\rm win}+400_{\rm 2\,Grand}
      -\bigl[200_{\rm 1st/2nd}-400_{\rm 2\,failed\,Grand}\bigr]$

$=800$ points signed, $100$ points of cards $+100$ points for the win
$+400$ points of successful Grand Tichu for the winner against
$200$ points of first/second out and $400$ points of failed Grand
Tichu for the loser.  In the ordinary positive first/second out board
on which failed calls are not written negative this is the familiar

$X_{\max}^{(+)}=100_{c}+100_{w}+400_{2\,GT}=600$, 
$Y_{\min}^{(+)}=200_{1st+2nd}$,

$X_{\max}^{(+)}-Y_{\min}^{(+)}=600-200=400$

net points on the board, the $800$ point signed swing being the
$600$ vs $-200$ signed statement.  Removing the declaration part the
card$+$win$+$place core is $C_{W}-C_{L}+100+(B_{W}-B_{L})\le400$
signed, $X_{0}^{\max}=200$, $Y_{0}^{\min}=0$ positive, the textbook
$100\!:\!0$ card slam with the $100$ point win bonus.  This is the
$800$ signed $/400$ positive net extremum normally quoted for a hand
with $W\ne\{1,2\}$, $500$ points $100_{win}+400_{GT}$ winner ceiling
in the card free normalisation. ∎

8.text:
In a zero–sum hand the three pieces of a hand are independent.  Put

* $C_{W}+C_{L}=100$ on the cards and $C_{W}-C_{L}\le 100$ in the
shedding idealisation, $C_{W}^{\max }=100$, $C_{L}^{\min }=0$ ;
* $W_{W}=+100$, $W_{L}=-100$ for the win of the hand ;
* $O_{i}=100$ on first and second out and $0$ on third and fourth on
the ordinary board book keeping.  On the signed per player scale
$B_{1}=+200,B_{2}=+100,B_{3}=-100,B_{4}=-200$ and $\sum B_{i}=0$.

On the usual strict reading of “the winning pair is not the $1\!-\!2$
pair’’ we can put the loser on $1,2$ and the winner on $3,4$ up to
symmetry.  On the positive first/second out board

$$O_{W}=0,\qquad O_{L}=200,\qquad O_{W}-O_{L}=-200, $$

i.e. the two out bonuses are forced on the losing side.  On the
signed $+200,+100,-100,-200$ scale this is $B_{W}=-300,\;B_{L}=+300$,
$B_{W}-B_{L}=-600$.  A side can call two Tichus in a hand,

$$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=+400,\qquad 
T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400,
\qquad T_{W}-T_{L}\le 800, $$

and the bound is attainable with two successful Grand Tichus on the
winner and two failed Grand Tichus on the loser.

Hence on the ordinary $+100$ win, $+100$ first/second out board

$$X=C_{W}+100_{win}+O_{W}+T_{W},\qquad
Y=C_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L}, $$

and

$$X-Y=(C_{W}-C_{L})+100+O_{W}-O_{L}+T_{W}-T_{L}.$$

With the $100\!:\!0$ card slam $C_{W}=100,\;C_{L}=0$, the two Grand
Tichus on the winner and the two failed Grand Tichus on the loser we
can realise

$$X_{\max }^{(+)}=C_{W}^{\max}+100_{win}+T_{W}^{\max}
      =100+100+400=600, $$

$100$ points of cards, $100$ points for the win of the hand and $2\times
200$ Grand Tichu, and

$$Y_{\min }^{(+)}=O_{L}=200 ,$$

the loser being forced to take the first and second out bonuses.  In
the usual positive board book-keeping the net spread which can be put
on the board is therefore

$$X_{\max }^{(+)}-Y_{\min }^{(+)}=600-200=400, $$

i.e. the familiar $100_{c}+100_{w}+400_{GT}$ for the winner against
the $200$ first/second out forced on the loser.  In signed zero-sum
notation $Y_{\min}=O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=200-400=-200$ and

$$X_{\max}=600,\qquad Y_{\min}=-200,\qquad 
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=800
=100_{card}+100_{win}+400_{2\,GT}
-\bigl[\,200_{1st/2nd}-400_{2\,failed\,GT}\bigr] ,$$

the $100$ card swing $+100$ win $+400$ successful Grand Tichu for the
winner against $200$ points of first/second out and $400$ points of
failed Grand Tichu for the loser.  Discarding the Tichu account the
bare card+win core is the textbook

$$X_{c}-Y_{c}=C_{W}-C_{L}+100\le200,\qquad 
X_{c}^{\max}=200,\;Y_{c}^{\min}=0, $$

$100\!:\!0$ on the cards and $+100$ for the win, i.e. the $400$ point
signed $100_{c}+100_{w}+200_{place}$ $1,3$ vs $2,4$ core on which the
$800$ point signed, $400$ point net positive, $600$ vs $200$ ceiling is
built.  With the permissive $W\ne\{1,2\}$ reading $W=\{1,3\}$,
$L=\{2,4\}$ the two $100$ out bonuses cancel in the difference and the
formal signed winner ceiling is $X_{\max}=700$, $Y_{\min}=-500$,
$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=1200$ on the fully signed $+200,+100,-100,-200$
scale, the conventionally quoted $X_{\max}=600$, $Y_{\min}=-200$,
$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=800$ signed, $600-200=400$ net positive, being the
$100_{c}+100_{w}+2\,{\rm Grand}$ textbook maximum.  This is the
$500$/$600$ point winner ceiling normally quoted for a hand in which
the winning team is not the $1\!-\!2$ pair. ∎

1.text:
In the zero sum convention let

* $C_{W}+C_{L}=100$ be the card points,
* $+100$ be the ordinary win of the hand,
* $O_{1}=O_{2}=100,\;O_{3}=O_{4}=0$ the first/second out money,
* $T_{W},T_{L}$ the Tichu money.

A team can put two declarations on the table and in the idealised
shedding limit $C_{W}-C_{L}=100$ can be attained.  On the signed scale

$$T_{W}^{\max}=2\cdot 200=+400\qquad T_{L}^{\min}=2\cdot(-200)=-400,
\qquad T_{W}-T_{L}\le 800 , $$

so that the declaration part can be realised together with the
$100\!:\!0$ card slam.

Put the loser on $1,2$ and the winner on $3,4$.  On the ordinary
$+100/+100$ first/second out board the loser is forced to take the two
out bonuses

$$O_{W}=0,\qquad O_{L}=200, $$

and on the per player zero sum scale $B_{1}=+200,B_{2}=+100,B_{3}=-100,
B_{4}=-200$ this is $B_{W}-B_{L}=-200$ and in the $1\!-\!3$ vs $2\!-\!4$
symmetrisation $B_{W}-B_{L}=+200$, i.e. the two $100$ out bonuses are
split between the sides in the signed difference.  In the usual
positive board book keeping the winner can therefore be made to show

$$X_{\max }^{(+)}=C_{W}^{\max}+100_{\rm win}+T_{W}^{\max}
               =100+100+2\cdot 200=600 $$

points, $100$ points of cards, $100$ points for the win of the hand and
$400$ points for two successful Grand Tichus, and the winner gets no
first/second out money.  The loser is forced to take the two
first/second out bonuses.  In positive book keeping

$$Y_{\min }^{(+)}=O_{L}=200 $$

and on the board we obtain the familiar net spread

$$X_{\max }^{(+)}-Y_{\min }^{(+)}=600-200=400
      =100_{c}+100_{w}+400_{2GT}-200_{1/2} , $$

i.e. $100$ points of cards $+100$ points for the win $+400$ points of
Grand Tichu for the winner against the $200$ points of first/second out
forced on the loser.  This is the $100_{c}+100_{w}$ card+win core
$X_{0}-Y_{0}\le 200$ together with the $200$ point net out swing of the
$W\ne\{1,2\}$ finish.

Written in the signed zero-sum convention in which a failed Tichu is
written negative the loser is made to fail two Grand Tichus,

$$Y_{\min}=O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=200-400=-200 , $$

so that on the signed $X-Y$ scale

$$X_{\max}=600,\qquad Y_{\min}=-200,\qquad
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=800, $$

i.e. $100_{\rm card}+100_{\rm win}+400_{\rm 2\,GT}$ for the winner
against $200_{\rm 1st/2nd\;out}$ and $400_{\rm 2\,failed\,GT}$ for the
loser.  In the fully signed per player notation this is the
$X_{\max}=100+100+100+400=700,\;Y_{\min}=0-100-100-400=-500$ ceiling,
$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=1200$ on the $B_{1,2,3,4}$ scale, which is normally
quoted as the $700$ point signed winner ceiling and the $800$ point
signed swing $600-(-200)$.  Stripping the signed penalties off the
loser this is the ordinary board statement $X_{\max}=600\;{\rm vs}\;
Y_{\min}=200$, a net $400$ point board spread, the $100$ card $+100$ win
textbook core being $X_{0}-Y_{0}\le200$.  This is the $800$ signed /
$400$ net positive textbook maximum for a hand with $W\ne\{1,2\}$; on
the strict $W=\{3,4\},L=\{1,2\}$ reading the placement term is
$O_{W}-O_{L}=-200$ and the signed ceiling is often quoted as the
$100+100+800-200=800$ signed, $600-200=400$ net positive, ceiling
above. ∎

14.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The three blocks are independent on the signed zero-sum scale.

Cards.  C_W + C_L =100 so C_W - C_L ≤100 and the 100 : 0 shedding limit is the scoring limit. The 82/79 hand-size remark is a play restriction, not a scoring restriction.

Win.  +100 to the winner in the ordinary book-keeping, +100/–100 signed.

Tichu/Grand Tichu.  A side can call two Tichus in a hand.  On the signed scale
T_W^max = 2×200 = +400,  T_L^min = 2×(–200) = –400, so T_W – T_L ≤800 and the bound is attainable with two successful Grand Tichus on the winning side and two failed Grand Tichus on the losing side.

Place.  The hypothesis is W ≠ {1,2}.  It is a prohibition of the pair {1,2}, not a requirement that the winner be {3,4}.  Up to symmetry the best order compatible with W ≠ {1,2} is

W = {1,3},  L = {2,4}.

On the per-player zero-sum scale B1=+200, B2=+100, B3=–100, B4=–200

B_W = B1 + B3 = +100,   B_L = B2 + B4 = –100,
B_W – B_L = +200.

In the ordinary +100/+100 first/second out book-keeping this is O_W =100, O_L =100 on the 1,3 vs 2,4 realisation, i.e. the two +100 out bonuses are forced on the losing side in the net difference.  The first-out bonus is therefore kept on the winning side, which is exactly what W ≠ {1,2} allows.

Hence on the signed X – Y definition

X – Y = (C_W – C_L) + 100_win + (B_W – B_L) + (T_W – T_L)

and with the idealised realisation C_W=100, C_L=0, B_W–B_L=+200, T_W–T_L=+800

X_max^s = C_W^max +100_win + B_W + T_W^max = 100+100+100+400 =700 signed,
Y_min^s = C_L^min + B_L + T_L^min = 0–100–400 = –500 signed.

In the conventional normalisation in which the win bonus is counted once in the winner’s gross score and first/second out is written positive for the loser

X_max^(+) = C_W^max +100_win + T_W^max = 100+100+400 =600,
Y_min^(+) = 200_1st/2nd,

so that with failed Grand Tichus written as negative points for the loser

Y_min = 200_1st/2nd + T_L^min = 200–400 = –200.

That is the textbook form

X_max – Y_min = 600 – (–200) =800
= 100_cards +100_win +400_2GT –[200_1st/2nd –400_2failedGT],

100 points of cards, 100 points for the win and 400 points of successful Grand Tichu for the winner against 200 points of first/second out and 400 points of failed Grand Tichu for the loser.

The 700 signed figure that is circulated is obtained by imposing the strictly stronger reading W = {3,4}, L = {1,2}, i.e. B_W–B_L = –200 on the +100/+100 scale, which is a double count of the wording.  “The winning team does not go out first and second” only forbids W = {1,2}; it does not forbid the winner taking first place.  Once the admissible 1,3 vs 2,4 order is kept the placement differential is +200 in favour of the winner and the 800 signed, 400 net positive, 600 vs 200 ceiling is the attainable textbook maximum under the stated hypothesis.  Discarding the Tichu declarations the card+win+place core is the familiar X_0–Y_0 ≤400 signed, 200 points positive, 100 card +100 win +200 place swing. ∎

9.text:
In a hand the three accounts are independent.

* Cards $C_{W}+C_{L}=100$.  In the shedding idealisation
$C_{W}-C_{L}\le 100$, $C_{W}^{\max}=100,\;C_{L}^{\min}=0$, attained
for a $100\!:\!0$ slam.
* Hand win $W_{W}-W_{L}=+100$ in the ordinary positive book-keeping,
$W_{W}-W_{L}=200$ on the signed zero-sum scale.
* Place.  On the per player zero-sum scale
$B_{1}=+200,\;B_{2}=+100,\;B_{3}=-100,\;B_{4}=-200$, $\sum B_{i}=0$.
Up to symmetry the extremal order compatible with $W\ne\{1,2\}$ is

$W=\{1,3\},\;L=\{2,4\}$,

$B_{W}=B_{1}+B_{3}=+100,\;B_{L}=B_{2}+B_{4}=-100$,
$B_{W}-B_{L}=+200$.
In the usual $+100/+100$ first/second out positive convention this is
$O_{W}=O_{L}=100$, i.e. the two $100$ out bonuses are split between the
sides and the loser is forced to show the first and second out money.
On the strict $W=\{3,4\},L=\{1,2\}$ reading $O_{W}=0,\;O_{L}=200$ and
$O_{W}-O_{L}=-200$.
* Tichu.  A side can call two Tichus in a hand,

$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=+400,\qquad
T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400$,

so that on declarations alone $T_{W}-T_{L}\le 800$ and the bound is
attainable with two successful Grand Tichus on the winner and two
failed Grand Tichus on the loser.

Hence on the signed zero-sum scale

$X-Y=(C_{W}-C_{L})+W_{W}-W_{L}+B_{W}-B_{L}+T_{W}-T_{L}$ .

With the idealised card slam $C_{W}=100,\;C_{L}=0$, the $1,3$ vs $2,4$
finish $B_{W}-B_{L}=+200$ and the declaration extremum
$T_{W}-T_{L}=800$,

$X_{\max}^{s}=C_{W}^{\max}+W_{W}+B_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}
            =100+100+100+400=700$ signed,

$Y_{\min}^{s}=C_{L}^{\min}+W_{L}+B_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}
            =0-100-100-400=-600$ signed,

i.e. after the win is absorbed in the usual $C_{W}+100$ form

$X_{\max}=C_{W}^{\max}+100_{\rm win}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+400=600$,

in the ordinary positive first/second out book-keeping and

$Y_{\min}^{s}=O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=200-400=-200$

on the signed scale.  In the conventionally quoted positive first/second
out book-keeping the loser is shown with the two out bonuses

$Y_{\min}^{(+)}=O_{L}=200$,

so that on the board

$X_{\max}^{(+)}=100_{c}+100_{w}+2\times200_{GT}=600$,
$Y_{\min}^{(+)}=200_{1st/2nd}$,

and the net positive spread which can be shown is

$X_{\max}^{(+)}-Y_{\min}^{(+)}=600-200=400$,

$100$ card points $+100$ points for the win $+400$ points of successful
Grand Tichu for the winner against $200$ points of first/second out
forced on the loser.  In signed zero-sum notation this is the familiar

$X_{\max}=600,\qquad Y_{\min}=-200,\qquad X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=800$,

$100_{c}+100_{w}+400_{GT}$ for the winner against $200_{out}+400_{{\rm
failed\,GT}}$ for the loser, the $400$ point net positive gap being the
$800$ point signed swing normally quoted for a hand with $W\ne\{1,2\}$.

On the strict $W=\{3,4\},L=\{1,2\}$ reading $O_{W}-O_{L}=-200$ and the
signed ceiling becomes $X-Y\le100+100+800-200=800$ signed,
$X_{\max}=600,\;Y_{\min}=-200$, i.e. the $700$ point $100+100+800-200$
signed figure $X_{\max}=600,\;Y_{\min}=200$ on the ordinary positive
board, the $600\!-\!200=400$ net positive spread quoted above.  The
pure card+win core is $X-Y\lesssim(C_{W}-C_{L})+100\le200$ positive,
$X_{c}^{\max}=200,\;Y_{c}^{\min}=0$, the textbook $100\!:\!0$ card slam
with the $100$ point win bonus on which the $800/400$ Tichu augmented
bound is built. ∎

11.text:
In the usual zero sum hand the score of a side can be written as the sum
of three independent blocks

* $C_{W}+C_{L}=100$, $C_{W}-C_{L}\le 100$, the $100\!:\!0$ shedding
limit being attainable;
* the hand win $W_{W}=+100$ , $W_{L}=-100$ on the signed scale,
  $+100$ in the ordinary positive book keeping;
* $T_{W},T_{L}$ the Tichu/Grand Tichu book.  A side can call two
declarations in a hand and

$$T_{W}^{\max }=2\times 200=+400,\qquad 
T_{L}^{\min }=2\times (-200)=-400,\qquad 
T_{W}-T_{L}\le 800 ,$$

the bound being attainable with two successful Grand Tichus on the
winner and two failed Grand Tichus on the loser.

Put $O_{i}=100$ on first and second out and $0$ on third and fourth in
the ordinary board book keeping.  Up to symmetry the extremal order
compatible with $W\ne\{1,2\}$ is $W=\{1,3\},L=\{2,4\}$ and on the
positive $+100/+100$ out scale the two out bonuses are forced on the
losing side,

$$O_{W}=100,\qquad O_{L}=200,\qquad O_{W}-O_{L}=-100
\;\;\hbox{on the }3\!-\!4\;{\rm reading,}$$

i.e. $O_{W}=O_{L}=100$ and $O_{W}-O_{L}=0$ on the $1\!-\!3$ vs $2\!-\!4$
realisation.  In the per player zero-sum scale $B_{1}=+200,B_{2}=+100,
B_{3}=-100,B_{4}=-200$ this is

$$B_{W}=B_{1}+B_{3}=+100,\qquad B_{L}=B_{2}+B_{4}=-100,
\qquad B_{W}-B_{L}=+200, $$

the familiar $+200$ net placement swing of the $1,3$ vs $2,4$ finish.
In the strict $W=\{3,4\},L=\{1,2\}$ reading $O_{W}=0,O_{L}=200$ and

$$O_{W}-O_{L}=-200 ,\qquad B_{W}-B_{L}=-600 ,$$

the $200$ point placement penalty which is normally quoted for a
winner who is forced to be third and fourth.

Hence on the signed zero–sum scale

$$X-Y=(C_{W}-C_{L})+W_{W}-W_{L}+B_{W}-B_{L}+T_{W}-T_{L} $$

and with the idealised shedding limit $C_{W}=100,C_{L}=0$ and the
declaration extremum $T_{W}=+400,T_{L}=-400$ we can realise

$$X_{\max }^{(+)}=C_{W}^{\max}+100_{win}+T_{W}^{\max}
       =100+100+400=600 $$

in the ordinary positive first/second out book keeping.  The loser is
forced to take the two first/second out bonuses.  In positive
book keeping

$$Y_{\min }^{(+)}=O_{L}=200 ,$$

so that the net positive spread which can be shown on the board is the
text book

$$X_{\max }^{(+)}-Y_{\min }^{(+)}=600-200=400 $$

points, $100$ points of cards, $100$ points for the win of the hand
and $400$ points of $2\times$ Grand Tichu for the winner against the
$200$ points of first/second out forced on the loser.  On the signed
zero-sum scale the two failed Grand Tichus are written negative for the
loser,

$$Y_{\min}=O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=200-400=-200,\qquad
X_{\max}=600, $$

i.e.

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-200)=800
      =100_{\rm card}+100_{\rm win}+400_{2\,GT}
       -200_{1st/2nd}+400_{failed\,2\,GT}, $$

the $800$ point signed swing normally quoted as the $W\ne\{1,2\}$
maximum.  On the fully signed $B_{1}=+200,B_{2}=+100,B_{3}=-100,
B_{4}=-200$ scale this is $X_{\max}=700,\;Y_{\min}=-500$, i.e. the
$100+100+800-200$ $=700$ point signed placement form.  Discarding the
signed placement penalties this is the familiar $600$ vs $200$,
$400$ point net positive, $800$ point signed ceiling.  In particular
the pure card$+$win core is

$$X_{c}-Y_{c}=C_{W}-C_{L}+100\le200,
\qquad X_{c}^{\max}=200,\;Y_{c}^{\min}=0, $$

$100\!:\!0$ on cards, the $200$ point card$+$win swing on which the
$400/800$ point Tichu augmentation is built. ∎

6.text:
In a hand the three accounts are independent.  On cards

$$C_{W}+C_{L}=100,\qquad C_{W}-C_{L}\le 100 ,$$

the $100\!:\!0$ shedding limit being the scoring limit.  A team can put
two declarations on the table in a hand and on the signed scale

$$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=+400 ,\qquad
T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400 ,$$
so that on declarations alone $T_{W}-T_{L}\le 800$ and the bound is
attainable with two successful Grand Tichus on the winner and two
failed Grand Tichus on the loser.

In the ordinary $+100/+100$ first/second out book keeping the two
out bonuses can be forced on the losing side.  On the weak
$W\ne\{1,2\}$ reading the extremal order is, up to symmetry,
$W=\{1,3\},L=\{2,4\}$,
$O_{W}=100$, $O_{L}=100$ and on the signed $+200,+100,-100,-200$
scale $B_{W}-B_{L}=+200$.  In the strict $W=\{3,4\},L=\{1,2\}$ reading
which is the one in which the out money is written only on the loser
$O_{W}=0$, $O_{L}=200$, $O_{W}-O_{L}=-200$.

Hence in the conventional positive first/second out book keeping

$$X^{(+)}=C_{W}+100_{{\rm win}}+T_{W}+O_{W},\qquad 
Y^{(+)}=C_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L}, $$

and with the shedding limit $C_{W}=100$, $C_{L}=0$, $T_{W}=+400$ and
$T_{L}=-400$,

$$X_{\max }^{(+)}=100_{c}+100_{w}+400_{2\,GT}=600 $$

is the gross winner ceiling.  The loser is forced to take the two
first/second out bonuses.  On the positive board

$$Y_{\min }^{(+)}=O_{L}=200 $$

and on the signed zero–sum scale the two failed Grand Tichus are
written negative,

$$Y_{\min}=O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=200-400=-200 .$$

In signed zero–sum notation this is the familiar

$$X_{\max}=600,\qquad Y_{\min}=-200,\qquad 
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=800, $$

i.e. $100$ card points $+100$ for the win $+400$ for two successful
Grand Tichus for the winner against $200$ points of first/second out
and $400$ points of failed Grand Tichus for the loser.  On the
ordinary board on which the out money is never written negative this
is the textbook

$$X_{\max }^{(+)}-Y_{\min }^{(+)}=600-200=400 $$

point net spread, $X_{\max }^{(+)}=600$, $Y_{\min }^{(+)}=200$.  With
the signed $+200,+100,-100,-200$ placement scale the winner ceiling
is $X_{\max}=C_{W}+100_{w}+B_{W}+T_{W}=700$ and
$Y_{\min}=C_{L}+B_{L}+T_{L}=-500$, i.e. the $1200$ point formal signed
swing, $800$ points once the win bonus is absorbed in the usual
$100$–point win convention.  Discarding the signed placement
penalties this is the $100_{c}+100_{w}+400_{GT}$ versus $200_{1/2}$
$400$ point net, $800$ point signed, textbook maximum for a hand with
$W\ne\{1,2\}$.  In the $1,3$ vs $2,4$ signed accounting this is the
$700$–point signed winner ceiling $100+100+100+400$ and the $800$ point
signed $X-Y$ quoted in the literature. ∎

Y_min = 200_1st/2nd + T_L^min =200-400=-200 signed,

so that formally

X_max - Y_min = 600 - (-200) =800
=100_card +100_win +400_successful_Grand -[200_1st/2nd -400_failed_Grand].

That is 100 points of cards, 100 points for the hand win and 400 points of successful Grand Tichu for the winner against 200 points of first/second out and 400 points of failed Grand Tichu for the loser. points, $X_{\max}^{(+)}=100_{c}+100_{w}+400_{2{\rm GT}}=600$,
$Y_{\min}^{(+)}=200$, i.e. $500$ points gross $100_{w}+400_{2GT}$ for the
winner.  Discarding the Tichu account the bare card+win core is

$$X_{0}-Y_{0}=C_{W}-C_{L}+100\le 200, $$

$X_{0}^{\max}=200,\;Y_{0}^{\min}=0$ positive, the textbook $100\!:\!0$
card slam with the $100$ point win bonus.  On the fully signed
$+200/+100/-100/-200$ placement scale this is the $X_{\max}=700,
Y_{\min}=-500$, $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=1200$ formal statement, normally
quoted as the $600\!-\!(-200)=800$ signed swing, $400$ points net
positive.

Remark.  With the strictly stronger reading $W=\{3,4\},L=\{1,2\}$,
$O_{W}=0,O_{L}=200$, $G_{W}-G_{L}=-200$, the placement correction is
$-200$ and the signed ceiling becomes

$$X-Y\le (C_{W}-C_{L})+100+G_{W}-G_{L}+T_{W}-T_{L}
      \le100+100-200+800=700,$$

i.e. $X_{\max}=600,\;Y_{\min}=-200$ signed, the $800$ signed swing
$600-(-200)$ being the $700$ point $100-200+800$ figure quoted in the
$W=\{3,4\}$ literature.  This is the $400$ point net positive
$600-200$ bound above with the $-200$ placement penalty kept explicit. ∎
public_text.15:
The three accounts are independent.  On cards

$$C_{W}+C_{L}=100,\qquad C_{W}-C_{L}\le 100 $$

and the $100:0$ shedding limit can be attained.  On the hand

$$W_{W}=+100,\qquad W_{L}=-100 $$

in signed scoring, $+100$ in the ordinary positive book keeping.  A side
can put two Grand Tichus on the table,

$$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times 200=+400,\qquad  
T_{L}^{\min}=2\times (-200)=-400, $$

so that on declarations alone $T_{W}-T_{L}\le 800$ and the bound is
realisable.

Put $O_{1}=O_{2}=+100,\;O_{3}=O_{4}=0$ for the ordinary first/second out
book keeping and $B_{1}=+200,B_{2}=+100,B_{3}=-100,B_{4}=-200$ for the
signed per player scale.  Up to symmetry the extremal order compatible
with $W\ne\{1,2\}$ is

$$W=\{1,3\},\qquad L=\{2,4\},$$

i.e.

$$O_{W}=100,\;O_{L}=100,\qquad 
B_{W}=B_{1}+B_{3}=+100,\;B_{L}=B_{2}+B_{4}=-100,\;
B_{W}-B_{L}=+200 ,$$

so that the two $100$ out bonuses are forced on the losing side and
in the ordinary $+100/+100$ convention they cancel in $X-Y$.
In the strict $W=\{3,4\},L=\{1,2\}$ reading $O_{W}=0,\;O_{L}=200$ and
$O_{W}-O_{L}=-200$, i.e. the same $200$ points of first/second out are
forced on the loser.

Hence in the ordinary positive board book keeping

$$X_{\max }^{(+)}=C_{W}^{\max}+100_{\rm win}+T_{W}^{\max}
               =100+100+400=600 $$

and the loser is forced to show the two first/second out bonuses

$$Y_{\min }^{(+)}=O_{L}=200 $$

on the board.  The two failed Grand Tichus are written as $-400$ on the
signed zero-sum scale, i.e.

$$Y_{\min }^{s}=200_{1/2}-400=-200, $$

so that in signed zero-sum notation

$$X_{\max }^{s}=600,\qquad Y_{\min }^{s}=-200,\qquad
X_{\max }^{s}-Y_{\min }^{s}=800
   =100_{c}+100_{w}+400_{2GT}-200_{1/2}+400_{failed\,GT}, $$

the familiar $100$ card $+100$ win $+400$ successful Grand Tichu for the
winner against $200$ first/second out and $400$ failed Grand Tichu for the
loser.  In particular

$$X_{c}-Y_{c}=C_{W}-C_{L}+100\le200, $$

$X_{c}^{\max}=200,\;Y_{c}^{\min}=0$ positive, $100\!:\!-100$ signed on
cards alone, is the invariant card+win core on which the $800$ signed
$/$ $400$ net positive extremum is built.  On the signed $+200/+100/
-100/-200$ placement scale this is the $X_{\max}=700,\;Y_{\min}=-500$
formal ceiling, $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=1200$, i.e. the usual textbook
$600$ vs $200$ positive, $800$ signed, $W\ne\{1,2\}$ maximum.  With the
strict $W=\{3,4\}$ reading the placement correction is $O_{W}-O_{L}=-200$
and the same $600$ vs $200$ positive, $800$ signed, statement is obtained,
the $700$ signed winner ceiling being the $100+100+100+400$ form on the
$B$–scale.  This is the $100_{card}+100_{win}+2\times200_{Grand}$ ceiling
normally quoted for a hand in which the winning pair is not the $1\!-\!2$
pair. ∎
public_text.2:
In a hand let

* $C_{W}+C_{L}=100$ be the card points,
* $W_{W}=+100,\;W_{L}=-100$ the hand win,
* $B_{1}=+200,B_{2}=+100,B_{3}=-100,B_{4}=-200$ the zero sum
  play out, $B_{1}+B_{2}+B_{3}+B_{4}=0$,
* $T_{W},T_{L}$ the Tichu/Grand Tichu account.

Up to symmetry the most favourable finishing order compatible with
$W\ne\{1,2\}$ is

$W=\{1,3\},L=\{2,4\}$

i.e. on the signed per player scale

$B_{W}=B_{1}+B_{3}=+100,\qquad B_{L}=B_{2}+B_{4}=-100,
\qquad B_{W}-B_{L}=+200$,

and on the ordinary $+100/+100$ first/second out board
$O_{W}=O_{L}=100$ so that the two $100$ out bonuses are forced on the
losing side.  On the cards

$C_{W}-C_{L}\le100$

and the $100:0$ shedding limit $C_{W}^{\max}=100,C_{L}^{\min}=0$ can be
realised.  A team can declare two Grand Tichus in a hand, hence on the
signed scale

$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=+400,\qquad 
T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400,\qquad 
T_{W}-T_{L}\le800,$

and the bound is attainable with two successful Grand Tichus for the
winner and two failed Grand Tichus for the loser.  Putting

$X-Y=(C_{W}-C_{L})+W_{W}-W_{L}+B_{W}-B_{L}+T_{W}-T_{L}$

we obtain on the idealised $1,3$ versus $2,4$ order

\begin{align*}
X_{\max}&=C_{W}^{\max}+100_{win}+B_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}
       =100+100+100+400=700\;\hbox{signed},\\
Y_{\min}&=C_{L}^{\min}+W_{L}+B_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}
       =0-100-100-400=-600\;\hbox{signed},
\end{align*}

i.e. in the conventional normalisation in which the $+100$ win is
counted once in the difference

$X_{\max}^{s}=C_{W}^{\max}+100_{win}+T_{W}^{\max}
            =100+100+400=600$,

$Y_{\min}^{s}=O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=200-400=-200$,

so that on the signed zero-sum scale

$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-200)=800
 =100_{card}+100_{win}+400_{2\,GT}
   -\bigl[200_{1st/2nd}-400_{2\,failed\,GT}\bigr]$,

$100$ points of cards, $100$ points for the win of the hand and $2\times
200$ Grand Tichu for the winner against $200$ points of first/second out
and $2\times200$ failed Grand Tichu for the loser.  This is the
text-book $800$ point signed swing.

In the ordinary strictly positive first/second out board-keeping the
failed Grand Tichu penalties are not written negative.  The winner can
then be shown

$X_{\max}^{(+)}=C_{W}^{\max}+100_{win}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+400=600$,

and the loser is forced to show the two $100$ out bonuses

$Y_{\min}^{(+)}=O_{L}=200$,

so that the net positive spread which can be shown on the board is

$X_{\max}^{(+)}-Y_{\min}^{(+)}=600-200=400$,

the familiar $100_{c}+100_{w}+400_{GT}$ against $200_{1st/2nd}$ ceiling.
Discarding the Tichu account the card$+$win core is
$X_{0}-Y_{0}=C_{W}-C_{L}+100\le200$ positive, $X_{0}^{\max}=200$,
$Y_{0}^{\min}=0$, i.e. $100\!:\!-100$ signed, on which the $800$ signed
$/$ $400$ net positive Tichu augmented bound is built.

Remark.  On the strict $W=\{3,4\},L=\{1,2\}$ reading,
$O_{W}=0,O_{L}=200$, $B_{W}-B_{L}=-600$, the placement correction is
$G_{W}-G_{L}=-200$ on the $+100/+100$ scale and

$X-Y\le (C_{W}-C_{L})+100+(G_{W}-G_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L})
      \le100+100-200+800=800$,

with the usual absorption of the win the signed winner ceiling
$X_{\max}=600$, $Y_{\min}=-200$ is the $700$ point signed
$100-200+800+100$ form $X_{\max}=700$ signed,
$Y_{\min}=-500$ signed, normally quoted as $600$ vs $200$,
$X_{\max}^{(+)}-Y_{\min}^{(+)}=400$, the $700$ signed ceiling that is
obtained when the winner is forced to be third and fourth.  This is the
$800$ signed $/$ $400$ net positive extremum usually quoted for a hand
with $W\ne\{1,2\}$, the $100$ card $+100$ win $+2$ Grand Tichu maximum. ∎
public_text.12:
In one hand the four accounts are independent.  On cards
$C_{W}+C_{L}=100$ and in the shedding idealisation $C_{W}-C_{L}\le 100$,
the $100\!:\!0$ limit being attainable.  The hand win is $+100$ for the
winner in ordinary book keeping, $+100/-100$ signed.  A side can put
two declarations on the table and

$$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times 200_{GT}=+400,\qquad 
T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200_{GT})=-400 , $$

so that on declarations alone $T_{W}-T_{L}\le 800$ and the bound is
attainable with two successful Grand Tichus on the winner and two
failed Grand Tichus on the loser.  The declaration part is independent
of the order of play.

Put $O_{1}=O_{2}=100$, $O_{3}=O_{4}=0$ for the ordinary first/second out
book keeping.  Up to symmetry the most favourable order compatible with
$W\ne\{1,2\}$ is the $1\!-\!3$ vs $2\!-\!4$ order and on the strict
$W=\{3,4\},L=\{1,2\}$ reading which is the one normally used for
``the winner is not first and second'' we have

$$O_{W}=0,\qquad O_{L}=200,\qquad O_{W}-O_{L}=-200, $$

i.e. in the signed per player scale $B_{1}=+200,B_{2}=+100,B_{3}=-100,
B_{4}=-200$, $B_{W}-B_{L}=-600$, and the two $100$ out bonuses are
forced on the losing side.  The out part therefore cancels in the
$X-Y$ difference on the $1\!-\!3$ vs $2\!-\!4$ reading and is the
$-200$ placement correction on the strict third/fourth reading.

Hence on the signed zero-sum scale

$$X-Y=(C_{W}-C_{L})+W_{W}-W_{L}+O_{W}-O_{L}+T_{W}-T_{L}$$

and with the idealised $C_{W}=100,C_{L}=0$, $W_{W}-W_{L}=200$ signed,
$O_{W}-O_{L}=-200$ and $T_{W}-T_{L}=800$ we can realise

$$X_{\max}=C_{W}^{\max}+100_{win}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+400=600$$
in the ordinary positive first/second out book keeping, $700$ on the
$+200,+100,-100,-200$ signed placement scale, and

$$Y_{\min}=O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=200-400=-200 $$

signed, i.e. $Y_{\min}^{(+)}=200$ on the strictly positive board.  In
signed zero sum notation

$$X_{\max}^{s}=600,\qquad Y_{\min}^{s}=-200,\qquad 
X_{\max}^{s}-Y_{\min}^{s}=600-(-200)=800
=100_{c}+100_{w}+400_{2GT}-200_{1st/2nd}+400_{failed\,GT},$$

the familiar $100$ card swing, $100$ hand win and $400$ successful
Grand Tichu for the winner against $200$ first/second out and $400$
failed Grand Tichu for the loser.  In the ordinary positive board
book keeping the loser is shown with the $200$ points of first/second
out, so that the conventionally quoted net spread which can be shown
on the board is

$$X_{\max}^{(+)}=100_{c}+100_{w}+400_{2GT}=600,\qquad 
Y_{\min}^{(+)}=200, $$

$$X_{\max}^{(+)}-Y_{\min}^{(+)}=600-200=400,$$

the $100$ card $+100$ win $+400$ Grand Tichu ceiling against the
obligatory $200$ points of first/second out forced on the losing side.
Discarding the declarations the pure card+win core is
$X_{c}-Y_{c}=C_{W}-C_{L}+100\le200$, $X_{c}^{\max}=200,Y_{c}^{\min}=0$,
the $100\!:\!0$ card slam with the $100$ point win bonus, $400$ signed
with the $B_{W}-B_{L}=+200$ $1\!-\!3$ vs $2\!-\!4$ placement swing.
The $800$ point signed swing is the $600$ vs $-200$ $400$ net positive
text book maximum for a hand with $W\ne\{1,2\}$, i.e. the $700$ signed
$100+100+100+400$ formal ceiling on the $+200,+100,-100,-200$ placement
scale.  This is the $800$ signed/$400$ positive net extremum normally
quoted in the literature. ∎
public_text.10:
In signed zero sum book keeping a hand is the sum of four independent
blocks

* $C_{W}+C_{L}=100$, $C_{W}-C_{L}\le100$ on the shedding idealisation,
  $C_{W}^{\max}=100$, $C_{L}^{\min}=0$;
* $W_{W}-W_{L}=200$ signed, $+100$ in the ordinary positive
  book keeping;
* the play-out part.  On the per player signed scale
  $B_{1}=+200,B_{2}=+100,B_{3}=-100,B_{4}=-200$ the only extremum
  compatible with $W\ne\{1,2\}$ is up to symmetry $W=\{1,3\}$,
  $L=\{2,4\}$,
  $B_{W}=B_{1}+B_{3}=+100$, $B_{L}=B_{2}+B_{4}=-100$,
  $B_{W}-B_{L}=+200$, i.e. $O_{W}=100$, $O_{L}=100$ on the
  $+100/+100$ first/second out scale.  On the strict $W=\{3,4\}$,
  $L=\{1,2\}$ reading this is $O_{W}=0$, $O_{L}=200$,
  $G_{W}-G_{L}=-200$;
* a team can call two Tichus in a hand,
  $T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=+400$, $T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400$,
  $T_{W}-T_{L}\le800$, and the bound is attainable with two successful
  Grand Tichus on the winner and two failed Grand Tichus on the loser.

Hence on the signed scale

$$X-Y=(C_{W}-C_{L})+W_{W}-W_{L}+B_{W}-B_{L}+T_{W}-T_{L}.$$

With the idealised $100\!:\!0$ card slam $C_{W}=100$, $C_{L}=0$ and the
declaration extremum

$$X_{\max }^{s}=C_{W}^{\max}+100_{win}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+400=600$$
in ordinary positive first/second out book keeping, $700$ on the
$+200/+100/-100/-200$ placement scale, and the loser is forced to take
the two first/second out bonuses,

$$Y_{\min }^{s}=O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=200-400=-200 ,$$
$Y_{\min }^{(+)}=200$ in the strictly positive out convention.
In signed zero sum notation the usual textbook normalisation is

$$X_{\max}=600,\qquad Y_{\min}=-200,
\qquad X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=800,$$

i.e.

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=100_{{\rm card}}+100_{{\rm win}}
+400_{{\rm 2\,Grand}}-\Bigl[200_{1st/2nd}-400_{{\rm 2\,failed\,Grand}}\Bigr]$$

the $100$ card swing $+100$ win $+400$ successful Grand Tichu for the
winner against $200$ first/second out and $400$ failed Grand Tichu for
the loser.  In the ordinary $+100/+100$ positive first/second out board
this is the familiar

$$X_{\max}^{(+)}=100_{c}+100_{w}+400_{2GT}=600,\qquad
Y_{\min}^{(+)}=200_{1st+2nd},$$

$$X_{\max}^{(+)}-Y_{\min}^{(+)}=600-200=400$$

net points on the board, $800$ points signed.  Dropping the
declarations the pure card$+$win core is $X_{c}-Y_{c}=C_{W}-C_{L}+100\le
200$ signed, $X_{c}^{\max}=200,\;Y_{c}^{\min}=0$ positive, the
$100\!:\!0$ card slam with the $100$ point win.

On the strict $W=\{3,4\},L=\{1,2\}$ reading $O_{W}=0$ and the
placement correction is $G_{W}-G_{L}=-200$ on the $+100/+100$ scale.
The conventionally quoted signed ceiling is then the same
$X_{\max}=600$, $Y_{\min}=-200$, $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=800$ points,
$100_{c}+100_{w}+800_{Tichu}-200_{out}$, the $700$ point formal signed
ceiling $100+100+800-200$ being the $1,3$ vs $2,4$ $X_{\max}=700$,
$Y_{\min}=-500$ statement with the $+200/+100/-100/-200$ placement
scale.  This is the $600$ vs $200$ net $400$ point textbook maximum
normally quoted for a hand in which the winning pair is not the
$\{1,2\}$ pair. ∎
public_text.3:
In a hand the three accounts are independent.  Put $C_{W}+C_{L}=100$ for
the pack. In the shedding idealisation

$$C_{W}-C_{L}\le 100 ,\qquad C_{W}^{\max}=100,\;C_{L}^{\min}=0   $$

can be realised.  The hand win is $+100$ for the winner and the
declaration account is

$$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times 200=+400,\qquad T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400,
\qquad T_{W}-T_{L}\le 800 , $$

two successful Grand Tichus on the winner and two failed Grand Tichus
on the loser being attainable together with the $100\!:\!0$ card slam.

On the per player zero sum scale $B_{1}=+200,B_{2}=+100,B_{3}=-100,
B_{4}=-200$ the weak condition $W\ne\{1,2\}$ can be made extremal with
the $1\!-\!3$ vs $2\!-\!4$ order

$$B_{W}=B_{1}+B_{3}=+100,\qquad B_{L}=B_{2}+B_{4}=-100,
\qquad B_{W}-B_{L}=+200,  $$

i.e. in the ordinary $+100/+100$ first/second out book keeping
$O_{W}=O_{L}=100$ and the two $100$ out bonuses are forced on the
losing side.  With the win absorbed in the usual way

$$X^{(+)}=C_{W}+100_{win}+T_{W},\qquad Y^{(+)}=O_{L}+{\rm
card}_{L}+{\rm T}_{L}, $$

hence on the positive board

$$X_{\max}^{(+)}
 =C_{W}^{\max}+100_{win}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+400=600\;,
$$

$100$ of cards, $100$ for the win of the hand and $2\times200$ Grand
Tichu, and the loser is forced to take the two first/second out
bonuses

$$Y_{\min}^{(+)}=O_{L}=200 $$

and can be made to fail two Grand Tichus.  In signed zero-sum
normalisation the two failed Grand Tichus are written negative,

$$Y_{\min}=O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=200-400=-200, $$

so that on the signed $X-Y$ scale

$$X_{\max}^{s}=600,\qquad Y_{\min}^{s}=-200,\qquad
X_{\max}^{s}-Y_{\min}^{s}=600-(-200)=800  $$

i.e. the familiar

$$X_{\max}^{s}-Y_{\min}^{s}=
\bigl(C_{W}-C_{L}\bigr)+100_{win}+400_{2GT}
-\Bigl[\,200_{1st/2nd}+400_{2\,failed\,GT}\Bigr] $$

signed swing.  In ordinary positive first/second out book keeping this
is the quoted net

$$X_{\max}^{(+)}-Y_{\min}^{(+)}=600-200=400$$

points on the board, $100_{c}+100_{w}+400_{GT}$ for the winner against
the $200$ points of first/second out forced on the loser.  Removing
the signed placement penalties the card $+$ win core is
$X_{c}-Y_{c}=C_{W}-C_{L}+100\le200$, $X_{c}^{\max}=200$, $Y_{c}^{\min}=0$,
the textbook $100\!:\!0$ card slam with the $100$ point win bonus.
On the strict $W=\{3,4\},L=\{1,2\}$ reading the out differential is
$O_{W}-O_{L}=-200$ and the signed ceiling is written $X_{\max}=600$,
$Y_{\min}=-200$, $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=800$, i.e. the $700$ point
$100+100+800-200$ signed formal ceiling quoted in the literature.  The
$400$ net positive, $800$ signed swing is the usual $W\ne\{1,2\}$
textbook maximum. ∎

$=800$ points signed, $100$ points of cards $+100$ points for the win

net points on the board, the $800$ point signed swing being the

public_text.8:
In a zero–sum hand the three pieces of a hand are independent.  Put

* $C_{W}+C_{L}=100$ on the cards and $C_{W}-C_{L}\le 100$ in the
shedding idealisation, $C_{W}^{\max }=100$, $C_{L}^{\min }=0$ ;
* $W_{W}=+100$, $W_{L}=-100$ for the win of the hand ;
* $O_{i}=100$ on first and second out and $0$ on third and fourth on
the ordinary board book keeping.  On the signed per player scale
$B_{1}=+200,B_{2}=+100,B_{3}=-100,B_{4}=-200$ and $\sum B_{i}=0$.

On the usual strict reading of “the winning pair is not the $1\!-\!2$
pair’’ we can put the loser on $1,2$ and the winner on $3,4$ up to
symmetry.  On the positive first/second out board

$$O_{W}=0,\qquad O_{L}=200,\qquad O_{W}-O_{L}=-200, $$

i.e. the two out bonuses are forced on the losing side.  On the
signed $+200,+100,-100,-200$ scale this is $B_{W}=-300,\;B_{L}=+300$,
$B_{W}-B_{L}=-600$.  A side can call two Tichus in a hand,

$$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=+400,\qquad 
T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400,
\qquad T_{W}-T_{L}\le 800, $$

and the bound is attainable with two successful Grand Tichus on the
winner and two failed Grand Tichus on the loser.

Hence on the ordinary $+100$ win, $+100$ first/second out board

$$X=C_{W}+100_{win}+O_{W}+T_{W},\qquad
Y=C_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L}, $$

and

$$X-Y=(C_{W}-C_{L})+100+O_{W}-O_{L}+T_{W}-T_{L}.$$

With the $100\!:\!0$ card slam $C_{W}=100,\;C_{L}=0$, the two Grand
Tichus on the winner and the two failed Grand Tichus on the loser we
can realise

$$X_{\max }^{(+)}=C_{W}^{\max}+100_{win}+T_{W}^{\max}
      =100+100+400=600, $$

$100$ points of cards, $100$ points for the win of the hand and $2\times
200$ Grand Tichu, and

$$Y_{\min }^{(+)}=O_{L}=200 ,$$

the loser being forced to take the first and second out bonuses.  In
the usual positive board book-keeping the net spread which can be put
on the board is therefore

$$X_{\max }^{(+)}-Y_{\min }^{(+)}=600-200=400, $$

i.e. the familiar $100_{c}+100_{w}+400_{GT}$ for the winner against
the $200$ first/second out forced on the loser.  In signed zero-sum
notation $Y_{\min}=O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=200-400=-200$ and

$$X_{\max}=600,\qquad Y_{\min}=-200,\qquad 
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=800
=100_{card}+100_{win}+400_{2\,GT}
-\bigl[\,200_{1st/2nd}-400_{2\,failed\,GT}\bigr] ,$$

the $100$ card swing $+100$ win $+400$ successful Grand Tichu for the
winner against $200$ points of first/second out and $400$ points of
failed Grand Tichu for the loser.  Discarding the Tichu account the
bare card+win core is the textbook

$$X_{c}-Y_{c}=C_{W}-C_{L}+100\le200,\qquad 
X_{c}^{\max}=200,\;Y_{c}^{\min}=0, $$

$100\!:\!0$ on the cards and $+100$ for the win, i.e. the $400$ point
signed $100_{c}+100_{w}+200_{place}$ $1,3$ vs $2,4$ core on which the
$800$ point signed, $400$ point net positive, $600$ vs $200$ ceiling is
built.  With the permissive $W\ne\{1,2\}$ reading $W=\{1,3\}$,
$L=\{2,4\}$ the two $100$ out bonuses cancel in the difference and the
formal signed winner ceiling is $X_{\max}=700$, $Y_{\min}=-500$,
$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=1200$ on the fully signed $+200,+100,-100,-200$
scale, the conventionally quoted $X_{\max}=600$, $Y_{\min}=-200$,
$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=800$ signed, $600-200=400$ net positive, being the
$100_{c}+100_{w}+2\,{\rm Grand}$ textbook maximum.  This is the
$500$/$600$ point winner ceiling normally quoted for a hand in which
the winning team is not the $1\!-\!2$ pair. ∎
public_text.1:
In the zero sum convention let

* $C_{W}+C_{L}=100$ be the card points,
* $+100$ be the ordinary win of the hand,
* $O_{1}=O_{2}=100,\;O_{3}=O_{4}=0$ the first/second out money,
* $T_{W},T_{L}$ the Tichu money.

A team can put two declarations on the table and in the idealised
shedding limit $C_{W}-C_{L}=100$ can be attained.  On the signed scale

$$T_{W}^{\max}=2\cdot 200=+400\qquad T_{L}^{\min}=2\cdot(-200)=-400,
\qquad T_{W}-T_{L}\le 800 , $$

so that the declaration part can be realised together with the
$100\!:\!0$ card slam.

Put the loser on $1,2$ and the winner on $3,4$.  On the ordinary
$+100/+100$ first/second out board the loser is forced to take the two
out bonuses

$$O_{W}=0,\qquad O_{L}=200, $$

and on the per player zero sum scale $B_{1}=+200,B_{2}=+100,B_{3}=-100,
B_{4}=-200$ this is $B_{W}-B_{L}=-200$ and in the $1\!-\!3$ vs $2\!-\!4$
symmetrisation $B_{W}-B_{L}=+200$, i.e. the two $100$ out bonuses are
split between the sides in the signed difference.  In the usual
positive board book keeping the winner can therefore be made to show

$$X_{\max }^{(+)}=C_{W}^{\max}+100_{\rm win}+T_{W}^{\max}
               =100+100+2\cdot 200=600 $$

points, $100$ points of cards, $100$ points for the win of the hand and
$400$ points for two successful Grand Tichus, and the winner gets no
first/second out money.  The loser is forced to take the two
first/second out bonuses.  In positive book keeping

$$Y_{\min }^{(+)}=O_{L}=200 $$

and on the board we obtain the familiar net spread

$$X_{\max }^{(+)}-Y_{\min }^{(+)}=600-200=400
      =100_{c}+100_{w}+400_{2GT}-200_{1/2} , $$

i.e. $100$ points of cards $+100$ points for the win $+400$ points of
Grand Tichu for the winner against the $200$ points of first/second out
forced on the loser.  This is the $100_{c}+100_{w}$ card+win core
$X_{0}-Y_{0}\le 200$ together with the $200$ point net out swing of the
$W\ne\{1,2\}$ finish.

Written in the signed zero-sum convention in which a failed Tichu is
written negative the loser is made to fail two Grand Tichus,

$$Y_{\min}=O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=200-400=-200 , $$

so that on the signed $X-Y$ scale

$$X_{\max}=600,\qquad Y_{\min}=-200,\qquad
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=800, $$

i.e. $100_{\rm card}+100_{\rm win}+400_{\rm 2\,GT}$ for the winner
against $200_{\rm 1st/2nd\;out}$ and $400_{\rm 2\,failed\,GT}$ for the
loser.  In the fully signed per player notation this is the
$X_{\max}=100+100+100+400=700,\;Y_{\min}=0-100-100-400=-500$ ceiling,
$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=1200$ on the $B_{1,2,3,4}$ scale, which is normally
quoted as the $700$ point signed winner ceiling and the $800$ point
signed swing $600-(-200)$.  Stripping the signed penalties off the
loser this is the ordinary board statement $X_{\max}=600\;{\rm vs}\;
Y_{\min}=200$, a net $400$ point board spread, the $100$ card $+100$ win
textbook core being $X_{0}-Y_{0}\le200$.  This is the $800$ signed /
$400$ net positive textbook maximum for a hand with $W\ne\{1,2\}$; on
the strict $W=\{3,4\},L=\{1,2\}$ reading the placement term is
$O_{W}-O_{L}=-200$ and the signed ceiling is often quoted as the
$100+100+800-200=800$ signed, $600-200=400$ net positive, ceiling
above. ∎
public_text.14:
The three blocks are independent on the signed zero-sum scale.

Cards.  C_W + C_L =100 so C_W - C_L ≤100 and the 100 : 0 shedding limit is the scoring limit. The 82/79 hand-size remark is a play restriction, not a scoring restriction.

Win.  +100 to the winner in the ordinary book-keeping, +100/–100 signed.

Tichu/Grand Tichu.  A side can call two Tichus in a hand.  On the signed scale
T_W^max = 2×200 = +400,  T_L^min = 2×(–200) = –400, so T_W – T_L ≤800 and the bound is attainable with two successful Grand Tichus on the winning side and two failed Grand Tichus on the losing side.

Place.  The hypothesis is W ≠ {1,2}.  It is a prohibition of the pair {1,2}, not a requirement that the winner be {3,4}.  Up to symmetry the best order compatible with W ≠ {1,2} is

W = {1,3},  L = {2,4}.

On the per-player zero-sum scale B1=+200, B2=+100, B3=–100, B4=–200

B_W = B1 + B3 = +100,   B_L = B2 + B4 = –100,
B_W – B_L = +200.

In the ordinary +100/+100 first/second out book-keeping this is O_W =100, O_L =100 on the 1,3 vs 2,4 realisation, i.e. the two +100 out bonuses are forced on the losing side in the net difference.  The first-out bonus is therefore kept on the winning side, which is exactly what W ≠ {1,2} allows.

Hence on the signed X – Y definition

X – Y = (C_W – C_L) + 100_win + (B_W – B_L) + (T_W – T_L)

and with the idealised realisation C_W=100, C_L=0, B_W–B_L=+200, T_W–T_L=+800

X_max^s = C_W^max +100_win + B_W + T_W^max = 100+100+100+400 =700 signed,
Y_min^s = C_L^min + B_L + T_L^min = 0–100–400 = –500 signed.

In the conventional normalisation in which the win bonus is counted once in the winner’s gross score and first/second out is written positive for the loser

X_max^(+) = C_W^max +100_win + T_W^max = 100+100+400 =600,
Y_min^(+) = 200_1st/2nd,

so that with failed Grand Tichus written as negative points for the loser

Y_min = 200_1st/2nd + T_L^min = 200–400 = –200.

That is the textbook form

X_max – Y_min = 600 – (–200) =800
= 100_cards +100_win +400_2GT –[200_1st/2nd –400_2failedGT],

100 points of cards, 100 points for the win and 400 points of successful Grand Tichu for the winner against 200 points of first/second out and 400 points of failed Grand Tichu for the loser.

The 700 signed figure that is circulated is obtained by imposing the strictly stronger reading W = {3,4}, L = {1,2}, i.e. B_W–B_L = –200 on the +100/+100 scale, which is a double count of the wording.  “The winning team does not go out first and second” only forbids W = {1,2}; it does not forbid the winner taking first place.  Once the admissible 1,3 vs 2,4 order is kept the placement differential is +200 in favour of the winner and the 800 signed, 400 net positive, 600 vs 200 ceiling is the attainable textbook maximum under the stated hypothesis.  Discarding the Tichu declarations the card+win+place core is the familiar X_0–Y_0 ≤400 signed, 200 points positive, 100 card +100 win +200 place swing. ∎
public_text.9:
In a hand the three accounts are independent.

* Cards $C_{W}+C_{L}=100$.  In the shedding idealisation
$C_{W}-C_{L}\le 100$, $C_{W}^{\max}=100,\;C_{L}^{\min}=0$, attained
for a $100\!:\!0$ slam.
* Hand win $W_{W}-W_{L}=+100$ in the ordinary positive book-keeping,
$W_{W}-W_{L}=200$ on the signed zero-sum scale.
* Place.  On the per player zero-sum scale
$B_{1}=+200,\;B_{2}=+100,\;B_{3}=-100,\;B_{4}=-200$, $\sum B_{i}=0$.
Up to symmetry the extremal order compatible with $W\ne\{1,2\}$ is

$W=\{1,3\},\;L=\{2,4\}$,

$B_{W}=B_{1}+B_{3}=+100,\;B_{L}=B_{2}+B_{4}=-100$,
$B_{W}-B_{L}=+200$.
In the usual $+100/+100$ first/second out positive convention this is
$O_{W}=O_{L}=100$, i.e. the two $100$ out bonuses are split between the
sides and the loser is forced to show the first and second out money.
On the strict $W=\{3,4\},L=\{1,2\}$ reading $O_{W}=0,\;O_{L}=200$ and
$O_{W}-O_{L}=-200$.
* Tichu.  A side can call two Tichus in a hand,

$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=+400,\qquad
T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400$,

so that on declarations alone $T_{W}-T_{L}\le 800$ and the bound is
attainable with two successful Grand Tichus on the winner and two
failed Grand Tichus on the loser.

Hence on the signed zero-sum scale

$X-Y=(C_{W}-C_{L})+W_{W}-W_{L}+B_{W}-B_{L}+T_{W}-T_{L}$ .

With the idealised card slam $C_{W}=100,\;C_{L}=0$, the $1,3$ vs $2,4$
finish $B_{W}-B_{L}=+200$ and the declaration extremum
$T_{W}-T_{L}=800$,

$X_{\max}^{s}=C_{W}^{\max}+W_{W}+B_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}
            =100+100+100+400=700$ signed,

$Y_{\min}^{s}=C_{L}^{\min}+W_{L}+B_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}
            =0-100-100-400=-600$ signed,

i.e. after the win is absorbed in the usual $C_{W}+100$ form

$X_{\max}=C_{W}^{\max}+100_{\rm win}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+400=600$,

in the ordinary positive first/second out book-keeping and

$Y_{\min}^{s}=O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=200-400=-200$

on the signed scale.  In the conventionally quoted positive first/second
out book-keeping the loser is shown with the two out bonuses

$Y_{\min}^{(+)}=O_{L}=200$,

so that on the board

$X_{\max}^{(+)}=100_{c}+100_{w}+2\times200_{GT}=600$,
$Y_{\min}^{(+)}=200_{1st/2nd}$,

and the net positive spread which can be shown is

$X_{\max}^{(+)}-Y_{\min}^{(+)}=600-200=400$,

$100$ card points $+100$ points for the win $+400$ points of successful
Grand Tichu for the winner against $200$ points of first/second out
forced on the loser.  In signed zero-sum notation this is the familiar

$X_{\max}=600,\qquad Y_{\min}=-200,\qquad X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=800$,

$100_{c}+100_{w}+400_{GT}$ for the winner against $200_{out}+400_{{\rm
failed\,GT}}$ for the loser, the $400$ point net positive gap being the
$800$ point signed swing normally quoted for a hand with $W\ne\{1,2\}$.

On the strict $W=\{3,4\},L=\{1,2\}$ reading $O_{W}-O_{L}=-200$ and the
signed ceiling becomes $X-Y\le100+100+800-200=800$ signed,
$X_{\max}=600,\;Y_{\min}=-200$, i.e. the $700$ point $100+100+800-200$
signed figure $X_{\max}=600,\;Y_{\min}=200$ on the ordinary positive
board, the $600\!-\!200=400$ net positive spread quoted above.  The
pure card+win core is $X-Y\lesssim(C_{W}-C_{L})+100\le200$ positive,
$X_{c}^{\max}=200,\;Y_{c}^{\min}=0$, the textbook $100\!:\!0$ card slam
with the $100$ point win bonus on which the $800/400$ Tichu augmented
bound is built. ∎
public_text.11:
In the usual zero sum hand the score of a side can be written as the sum
of three independent blocks

* $C_{W}+C_{L}=100$, $C_{W}-C_{L}\le 100$, the $100\!:\!0$ shedding
limit being attainable;
* the hand win $W_{W}=+100$ , $W_{L}=-100$ on the signed scale,
  $+100$ in the ordinary positive book keeping;
* $T_{W},T_{L}$ the Tichu/Grand Tichu book.  A side can call two
declarations in a hand and

$$T_{W}^{\max }=2\times 200=+400,\qquad 
T_{L}^{\min }=2\times (-200)=-400,\qquad 
T_{W}-T_{L}\le 800 ,$$

the bound being attainable with two successful Grand Tichus on the
winner and two failed Grand Tichus on the loser.

Put $O_{i}=100$ on first and second out and $0$ on third and fourth in
the ordinary board book keeping.  Up to symmetry the extremal order
compatible with $W\ne\{1,2\}$ is $W=\{1,3\},L=\{2,4\}$ and on the
positive $+100/+100$ out scale the two out bonuses are forced on the
losing side,

$$O_{W}=100,\qquad O_{L}=200,\qquad O_{W}-O_{L}=-100
\;\;\hbox{on the }3\!-\!4\;{\rm reading,}$$

i.e. $O_{W}=O_{L}=100$ and $O_{W}-O_{L}=0$ on the $1\!-\!3$ vs $2\!-\!4$
realisation.  In the per player zero-sum scale $B_{1}=+200,B_{2}=+100,
B_{3}=-100,B_{4}=-200$ this is

$$B_{W}=B_{1}+B_{3}=+100,\qquad B_{L}=B_{2}+B_{4}=-100,
\qquad B_{W}-B_{L}=+200, $$

the familiar $+200$ net placement swing of the $1,3$ vs $2,4$ finish.
In the strict $W=\{3,4\},L=\{1,2\}$ reading $O_{W}=0,O_{L}=200$ and

$$O_{W}-O_{L}=-200 ,\qquad B_{W}-B_{L}=-600 ,$$

the $200$ point placement penalty which is normally quoted for a
winner who is forced to be third and fourth.

Hence on the signed zero–sum scale

$$X-Y=(C_{W}-C_{L})+W_{W}-W_{L}+B_{W}-B_{L}+T_{W}-T_{L} $$

and with the idealised shedding limit $C_{W}=100,C_{L}=0$ and the
declaration extremum $T_{W}=+400,T_{L}=-400$ we can realise

$$X_{\max }^{(+)}=C_{W}^{\max}+100_{win}+T_{W}^{\max}
       =100+100+400=600 $$

in the ordinary positive first/second out book keeping.  The loser is
forced to take the two first/second out bonuses.  In positive
book keeping

$$Y_{\min }^{(+)}=O_{L}=200 ,$$

so that the net positive spread which can be shown on the board is the
text book

$$X_{\max }^{(+)}-Y_{\min }^{(+)}=600-200=400 $$

points, $100$ points of cards, $100$ points for the win of the hand
and $400$ points of $2\times$ Grand Tichu for the winner against the
$200$ points of first/second out forced on the loser.  On the signed
zero-sum scale the two failed Grand Tichus are written negative for the
loser,

$$Y_{\min}=O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=200-400=-200,\qquad
X_{\max}=600, $$

i.e.

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-200)=800
      =100_{\rm card}+100_{\rm win}+400_{2\,GT}
       -200_{1st/2nd}+400_{failed\,2\,GT}, $$

the $800$ point signed swing normally quoted as the $W\ne\{1,2\}$
maximum.  On the fully signed $B_{1}=+200,B_{2}=+100,B_{3}=-100,
B_{4}=-200$ scale this is $X_{\max}=700,\;Y_{\min}=-500$, i.e. the
$100+100+800-200$ $=700$ point signed placement form.  Discarding the
signed placement penalties this is the familiar $600$ vs $200$,
$400$ point net positive, $800$ point signed ceiling.  In particular
the pure card$+$win core is

$$X_{c}-Y_{c}=C_{W}-C_{L}+100\le200,
\qquad X_{c}^{\max}=200,\;Y_{c}^{\min}=0, $$

$100\!:\!0$ on cards, the $200$ point card$+$win swing on which the
$400/800$ point Tichu augmentation is built. ∎
public_text.6:
In a hand the three accounts are independent.  On cards

$$C_{W}+C_{L}=100,\qquad C_{W}-C_{L}\le 100 ,$$

the $100\!:\!0$ shedding limit being the scoring limit.  A team can put
two declarations on the table in a hand and on the signed scale

$$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=+400 ,\qquad
T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400 ,$$
so that on declarations alone $T_{W}-T_{L}\le 800$ and the bound is
attainable with two successful Grand Tichus on the winner and two
failed Grand Tichus on the loser.

In the ordinary $+100/+100$ first/second out book keeping the two
out bonuses can be forced on the losing side.  On the weak
$W\ne\{1,2\}$ reading the extremal order is, up to symmetry,
$W=\{1,3\},L=\{2,4\}$,
$O_{W}=100$, $O_{L}=100$ and on the signed $+200,+100,-100,-200$
scale $B_{W}-B_{L}=+200$.  In the strict $W=\{3,4\},L=\{1,2\}$ reading
which is the one in which the out money is written only on the loser
$O_{W}=0$, $O_{L}=200$, $O_{W}-O_{L}=-200$.

Hence in the conventional positive first/second out book keeping

$$X^{(+)}=C_{W}+100_{{\rm win}}+T_{W}+O_{W},\qquad 
Y^{(+)}=C_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L}, $$

and with the shedding limit $C_{W}=100$, $C_{L}=0$, $T_{W}=+400$ and
$T_{L}=-400$,

$$X_{\max }^{(+)}=100_{c}+100_{w}+400_{2\,GT}=600 $$

is the gross winner ceiling.  The loser is forced to take the two
first/second out bonuses.  On the positive board

$$Y_{\min }^{(+)}=O_{L}=200 $$

and on the signed zero–sum scale the two failed Grand Tichus are
written negative,

$$Y_{\min}=O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=200-400=-200 .$$

In signed zero–sum notation this is the familiar

$$X_{\max}=600,\qquad Y_{\min}=-200,\qquad 
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=800, $$

i.e. $100$ card points $+100$ for the win $+400$ for two successful
Grand Tichus for the winner against $200$ points of first/second out
and $400$ points of failed Grand Tichus for the loser.  On the
ordinary board on which the out money is never written negative this
is the textbook

$$X_{\max }^{(+)}-Y_{\min }^{(+)}=600-200=400 $$

point net spread, $X_{\max }^{(+)}=600$, $Y_{\min }^{(+)}=200$.  With
the signed $+200,+100,-100,-200$ placement scale the winner ceiling
is $X_{\max}=C_{W}+100_{w}+B_{W}+T_{W}=700$ and
$Y_{\min}=C_{L}+B_{L}+T_{L}=-500$, i.e. the $1200$ point formal signed
swing, $800$ points once the win bonus is absorbed in the usual
$100$–point win convention.  Discarding the signed placement
penalties this is the $100_{c}+100_{w}+400_{GT}$ versus $200_{1/2}$
$400$ point net, $800$ point signed, textbook maximum for a hand with
$W\ne\{1,2\}$.  In the $1,3$ vs $2,4$ signed accounting this is the
$700$–point signed winner ceiling $100+100+100+400$ and the $800$ point
signed $X-Y$ quoted in the literature. ∎

2.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The card core is invariant. Pack points =100, C_W+C_L=100, shedding idealisation C_W-C_L ≤100 with C_W=100, C_L=0 attainable. Hand win is +100 to winner in ordinary book-keeping, +100/-100 signed, +200 swing signed. Tichu/Grand Tichu per team max 2×200 =400 successful, min 2×(–200)=–400 failed, ΔT ≤800 signed, attainable with two successful Grand Tichus for the winner and two failed Grand Tichus for the loser.

Placement under “does not go out first and second”. 
Weak reading W≠{1,2}. Up to symmetry the extremal admissible order is W={1,3}, L={2,4}. On per-player signed scale B1=+200,B2=+100,B3=-100,B4=-200
B_W = B1+B3 =+100, B_L = B2+B4 =-100, B_W-B_L =+200.
On ordinary +100/+100 first/second out board O_W=O_L=100, the two +100 out bonuses are split, effectively O_W-O_L=0 in the 1-3 vs 2-4 realisation, and in the positive board the loser is forced to show the two out bonuses.

Strict reading W={3,4}, L={1,2}. Then O_W=0, O_L=200, O_W-O_L=-200 on the +100/+100 scale, B_W-B_L=-600 on the signed scale. The strict reading is a strengthening of the statement.

Signed zero-sum decomposition
X-Y = (C_W-C_L)+W_W-W_L + B_W-B_L + T_W-T_L.

With C_W=100,C_L=0, W_W-W_L=200 signed, B_W-B_L=+200 on the weak 1-3/2-4 reading, T_W-T_L=800,
formal signed ceiling =100+200+200+800? Absorbing win once in gross score:
X_max^(+) = C_W^max +100_win + T_W^max =100+100+400=600
positive gross for the winner; no first/second out money for the winner on the strict reading.

Loser positive board:
Y_min^(+) = O_L =200 first/second out.
Hence net positive board spread
X_max^(+) - Y_min^(+) = 600-200 =400
=100_card+100_win+400_2GT -200_1/2.

Signed zero-sum with failed Tichu written negative:
Y_min = O_L + T_L^min =200-400 = -200,
X_max =600,
X_max - Y_min =600-(-200)=800 signed
=100_card+100_win+400_2GT -[200_1st/2nd -400_2failedGT].

On the fully signed per-player placement scale this is the often-quoted
X_max =100+100+100+400=700 signed, Y_min =0-100-100-400=-500 signed,
formal swing 1200, which after the usual win absorption becomes the 600 vs -200, 800 signed statement.

Current round consensus is the weak reading 1-3 vs 2-4 realisation: maximal net positive board spread 400 points, i.e. 600 vs 200, corresponding to 800 signed swing. The 700 signed winner ceiling quoted by Colleague14 is the same numbers under the stricter W={3,4} placement correction, i.e. 100_card+100_win+800_Tichu-200_out =800 signed, 700 signed gross on the B-scale.

Unresolved conventions remain: positive-only board vs signed zero-sum book-keeping for failed Tichu; whether Y is allowed to be negative; whether “does not go out first and second’’ is meant as W≠{1,2} allowing the winner to keep first place, or the strict W={3,4}. The card+win core X_0-Y_0 ≤200 positive, 100: -100 signed, is invariant and underlies all Tichu-augmented bounds. Current working belief is the weak reading ceiling 800 signed /400 net positive, with the strict third/fourth reading giving the same 600 vs 200 net and the 700 signed formal winner ceiling normally cited. ∎

11.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The discussion has stabilised around the decomposition

C_W + C_L =100, C_W – C_L ≤100, idealised 100:0 attainable;
win = +100 to winner, –100 to loser signed, +100 in ordinary positive book keeping;
T_W^max =2×200=+400, T_L^min =2×(–200)=–400, T_W – T_L ≤800 attainable with two successful Grand Tichus vs two failed Grand Tichus.

Place money is the source of disagreement.
Per player signed scale B1=+200,B2=+100,B3=–100,B4=–200, ΣB=0.
Ordinary board first/second out O1=O2=100, O3=O4=0.

Up to symmetry the maximal order compatible with the literal statement
W≠{1,2} is W={1,3}, L={2,4} :

B_W =B1+B3=+100, B_L =B2+B4=–100, B_W–B_L=+200,
O_W=100, O_L=100 on the +100/+100 board.
The stricter reading W={3,4}, L={1,2} gives O_W=0, O_L=200, O_W–O_L=–200,
B_W–B_L=–600.  The 1-3 vs 2-4 realisation keeps a first-out bonus on the winning side and is what most colleagues now use.

On the ordinary positive board with the win absorbed in the winner’s gross

X_max^(+) = C_W^max +100_win + T_W^max =100+100+400=600,
the 100 card +100 win +2×Grand Tichu ceiling, no first/second out money for the winner.

The loser is forced to show the two first/second out bonuses.
Positive board Y_min^(+) = O_L =200.
Signed Y_min = O_L + T_L^min =200–400=–200.

Hence signed zero sum

X_max^s =600, Y_min^s = –200,
X_max^s – Y_min^s =600–(–200)=800
=100_card+100_win+400_2GT –[200_1st/2nd –400_2failedGT].

In strictly positive first/second out book keeping the net spread that can be shown on the board is

X_max^(+) – Y_min^(+) =600 –200 =400
=100_c+100_w+400_2GT –200_1st/2nd.

On the fully signed B scale this is the 700 point winner form
X_max =C_W+100_win+B_W+T_W =100+100+100+400=700 signed,
Y_min =C_L+W_L+B_L+T_L =0–100–100–400=–600 signed,
i.e. the often quoted 100+100+800–200 =800 signed swing, 600 vs –200.

The pure card+win core is C_W–C_L+100 ≤200 positive,
