Y=C_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L} ,$$

so that with the $100\!:\!0$ card slam

$$
X_{\max }^{(+)}=C_{W}^{\max}+100_{w}+T_{W}^{\max}
               =100+100+2\times 200=600
$$

is the gross winner ceiling, $100$ points of cards, $100$ points for the
win of the hand and $400$ points for two successful Grand Tichus, and the
loser is forced to take the two first/second out bonuses

$$
Y_{\min }^{(+)}=O_{L}=200 ,
$$

the two failed Grand Tichus being written $T_{L}^{\min}=-400$ on the
signed zero-sum scale.  Hence on the board

$$
X_{\max }^{(+)}-Y_{\min }^{(+)}=600-200=400
      =100_{c}+100_{w}+400_{2GT}-200_{1/2} ,
$$

the textbook $100_{c}+100_{w}$ core $X_{0}-Y_{0}\le200$ augmented by
the $200$ point first/second out penalty forced on the loser.  In the
signed zero-sum normalisation the loser’s two failed Grand Tichus are
written negative,

$$
Y_{\min}=O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=200-400=-200,\qquad X_{\max}=600,
$$

so that on the signed $X-Y$ scale

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-200)=800
     =100_{card}+100_{win}+400_{2\,Grand}
      -\Big[\,200_{1st/2nd}-400_{2\,failed\,Grand}\Big] ,
$$

i.e. $100$ points of cards $+100$ points for the hand win $+400$ points
of successful Grand Tichu for the winner against $200$ points of
first/second out and $400$ points of failed Grand Tichu for the loser.
With the $+200/+100/-100/-200$ placement scale this is the familiar
$X_{\max}=100+100+100+400=700$, $Y_{\min}=0-100-100-400=-500$,
$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=1200$ formal statement, normally quoted as the
$600$ vs $200$, net $400$ point, $800$ signed point textbook maximum for
a hand in which the winning pair is not the $\{1,2\}$ pair.  Discarding
the signed penalties the ordinary board statement is the $600$ vs $200$
$400$ point net spread, the $800$ point signed swing $600-(-200)$ being
the signed zero-sum form of the same extremum.  This is the
$100_{c}+100_{w}+2\times200_{GT}$ ceiling on which the usual
$X_{c}-Y_{c}=C_{W}-C_{L}+100\le200$ card+win core is built. ∎

15.text:
In a hand the four accounts are independent on the signed zero-sum
scale

* $C_{W}+C_{L}=100$ and $C_{W}-C_{L}\le 100$ in the shedding
idealisation, $C_{W}^{\max}=100$, $C_{L}^{\min}=0$;
* $W_{W}-W_{L}=200$ signed, $+100$ in the ordinary positive book
keeping;
* $T_{W}^{\max}=2\times 200=+400$, $T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400$,
$T_{W}-T_{L}\le 800$ and the bound is attainable with two successful
Grand Tichus on the winner and two failed Grand Tichus on the loser;
* $B_{1}=+200,B_{2}=+100,B_{3}=-100,B_{4}=-200$, $\sum B_{i}=0$.

Up to symmetry the extremal order compatible with $W\ne\{1,2\}$ is
$W=\{1,3\},L=\{2,4\}$,

$$
B_{W}=B_{1}+B_{3}=+100,\qquad B_{L}=B_{2}+B_{4}=-100,
\qquad B_{W}-B_{L}=+200,
$$

i.e. $O_{W}=O_{L}=100$ on the $+100/+100$ first/second out board and
the two $+100$ out bonuses are forced on the losing side in the
$X-Y$ difference.  On the strict $W=\{3,4\},L=\{1,2\}$ reading
$O_{W}=0,O_{L}=200$, $O_{W}-O_{L}=-200$, the $-200$ placement
correction which is normally quoted.

Hence on the signed scale

$$
X-Y=(C_{W}-C_{L})+W_{W}-W_{L}+B_{W}-B_{L}+T_{W}-T_{L}\;,
$$

and with the idealised $100\!:\!0$ card slam $C_{W}=100,C_{L}=0$ and
the declaration extremum $T_{W}=+400,T_{L}=-400$ we can realise

$$
X_{\max }^{(+)}=C_{W}^{\max}+100_{\rm win}+T_{W}^{\max}
      =100+100+400=600
$$

in the ordinary $+100/+100$ first/second out book keeping.  The loser
is forced to show the two first/second out bonuses

$$
Y_{\min }^{(+)}=O_{L}=200,
$$

so that on the board the net positive spread which can be shown is

$$
X_{\max }^{(+)}-Y_{\min }^{(+)}=600-200=400
=100_{c}+100_{w}+400_{2\,GT}-200_{1/2},
$$

$100$ points of cards, $100$ points for the win of the hand and
$2\times200$ Grand Tichu for the winner against the $200$ points of
first/second out forced on the loser.  Written in signed zero-sum
notation the two failed Grand Tichus are written negative for the
loser,

$$
Y_{\min}=O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=200-400=-200,
\qquad X_{\max}=600,
$$

i.e. the familiar textbook signed swing

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-200)=800
=100_{\rm card}+100_{\rm win}+400_{\rm 2\,Grand}
-\big[\,200_{\rm 1st/2nd}-400_{\rm 2\,failed\,Grand}\big],
$$

$100$ card swing $+100$ win $+400$ successful Grand Tichu for the
winner against $200$ first/second out and $400$ failed Grand Tichu for
the loser.  On the fully signed $+200/+100/-100/-200$ placement scale
this is the $X_{\max}=100+100+100+400=700$ signed winner ceiling,
$Y_{\min}=-600$ signed, $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=1300$, the $700$ signed
$100+100+800-200$ form normally quoted as the $600$ vs $-200$ signed,
$600$ vs $200$ positive, $400$ net positive, $800$ signed textbook
maximum for a hand with $W\ne\{1,2\}$.  Discarding the Tichu account
the pure card+win core is $C_{W}-C_{L}+100\le200$, $X_{c}^{\max}=200$,
$Y_{c}^{\min}=0$ positive, the $100\!:\!0$ slam with the $100$ point
win.  This is the $800$ point signed, $400$ point net positive,
$600\!-\!200$ ceiling usually quoted in the literature. ∎

12.text:
In a hand the four accounts are independent on the zero sum scale.
On cards $C_{W}+C_{L}=100$ and on the shedding idealisation
$C_{W}-C_{L}\le 100$ and the $100\!:\!0$ slam can be attained.
The hand win is $+100$ in ordinary book keeping, $W_{W}-W_{L}=200$
signed.  A side can put two declarations on the table

$$T_{W}^{\max }=2\times 200=+400 ,\qquad 
T_{L}^{\min }=2\times (-200)=-400 ,\qquad T_{W}-T_{L}\le 800,$$

and the bound is attainable with two successful Grand Tichus on the
winner and two failed Grand Tichus on the loser.

On the ordinary $+100/+100$ first/second out board let
$O_{1}=O_{2}=100$, $O_{3}=O_{4}=0$.  Up to symmetry the extremal order
compatible with $W\ne\{1,2\}$ is the $1\!-\!3$ vs $2\!-\!4$ order.
In the usual positive book keeping the two out bonuses are forced on
the losing side, $O_{W}=0$ on the strict $W=\{3,4\},L=\{1,2\}$ reading
and $O_{L}=200$.  On the signed per player scale
$B_{1}=+200,B_{2}=+100,B_{3}=-100,B_{4}=-200$

$$B_{W}=B_{1}+B_{3}=+100,\qquad B_{L}=B_{2}+B_{4}=-100,\qquad
B_{W}-B_{L}=+200,$$

i.e. $O_{W}=O_{L}=100$ on the $1\!-\!3$ vs $2\!-\!4$ realisation and
$O_{W}-O_{L}=-200$ on the strict third/fourth reading.

Hence in ordinary positive first/second out book keeping

$$
X^{(+)}=C_{W}+100_{w}+O_{W}+T_{W},\qquad 
Y^{(+)}=C_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L},
$$

and with the idealised $C_{W}=100$, $C_{L}=0$, $T_{W}=+400$ we can
realise

$$
X_{\max }^{(+)}=C_{W}^{\max}+100_{w}+T_{W}^{\max}
      =100+100+2\times200=600,
$$

$100$ points of cards, $100$ points for the win of the hand and $400$
points for two successful Grand Tichus, and the winner gets no
first/second out money.  The loser is forced to take the two
first/second out bonuses,

$$
Y_{\min }^{(+)}=O_{L}=200,
$$

and can be made to fail two Grand Tichus.  In the signed zero sum
normalisation the two failed Grand Tichus are written negative for the
loser,

$$
Y_{\min}=O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=200-400=-200,
\qquad X_{\max}=600,
$$

so that on the signed $X-Y$ scale

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-200)=800
      =100_{c}+100_{w}+400_{2\,GT}
       -\Bigl[200_{1st/2nd}-400_{2\,failed\,GT}\Bigr],
$$

i.e. $100$ card swing $+100$ win $+400$ successful Grand Tichu for the
winner against $200$ first/second out and $400$ failed Grand Tichu for
the loser.  In ordinary positive board book keeping this is the
familiar net spread

$$
X_{\max }^{(+)}-Y_{\min }^{(+)}=600-200=400
$$

points on the board, $X_{\max }^{(+)}=600$, $Y_{\min }^{(+)}=200$,
the $100_{c}+100_{w}+400_{GT}$ ceiling against the obligatory $200$
first/second out forced on the losing side.  On the fully signed
$+200/+100/-100/-200$ placement scale this is the $X_{\max}=700$,
$Y_{\min}=-500$ formal statement, $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=800$ signed,
$600$ vs $200$, $400$ net positive, the textbook $W\ne\{1,2\}$ maximum.
Removing the Tichu account the pure card$+$win core is
$X_{c}-Y_{c}=C_{W}-C_{L}+100\le200$, $X_{c}^{\max}=200$, $Y_{c}^{\min}=0$
positive, the $100\!:\!0$ card slam with the $100$ point win.  The
$800$ signed swing is the $400$ net positive swing normally quoted in
the literature. ∎

4.text:
In a hand the three accounts are independent.  Write the scores on the
ordinary $+100/+100$ first/second out board

$X=C_{W}+100_{w}+O_{W}+T_{W}, \qquad
 Y=C_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L}\,$ ,

can be idealised,  $C_{W}^{\max}=100,\;C_{L}^{\min}=0$.
A side can put two declarations on the table

$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=+400,\qquad 
T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400,\qquad 
T_{W}-T_{L}\le800,$

and the bound is jointly realisable with the $100\!:\!0$ card slam.

out board

Hence in the conventional positive first/second out book keeping

$X_{\max }^{(+)}=C_{W}^{\max}+100_{\rm win}+T_{W}^{\max}
           =100+100+400=600$

$100$ cards, $100$ for the win of the hand and $2\times200$ successful
Grand Tichu, and the loser is forced to show the two first/second out
bonuses

$Y_{\min }^{(+)}=O_{L}=200$

on the board.  In signed zero sum notation the two failed Grand Tichus
are written negative for the loser,

$Y_{\min}=O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=200-400=-200,\qquad
X_{\max}=600,$

so that on the signed $X-Y$ scale

$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-200)=800
 =100_{\rm card}+100_{\rm win}+400_{\rm 2GT}
   -\bigl[\,200_{\rm 1st/2nd}-400_{\rm 2failedGT}\bigr]$,

i.e. $100$ points of cards $+100$ points for the win and $400$ points of
successful Grand Tichu for the winner against $200$ points of first/
second out and $400$ points of failed Grand Tichu for the loser.
In ordinary positive board book keeping this is the familiar net
spread

$X_{\max }^{(+)}-Y_{\min }^{(+)}=600-200=400$

points on the board, $100_{c}+100_{w}+400_{2GT}$ for the winner against
the obligatory $200$ points of first/second out forced on the loser.
Discarding the Tichu account the pure card+win core is
$X_{c}-Y_{c}=C_{W}-C_{L}+100\le200$, $X_{c}^{\max}=200$,
$Y_{c}^{\min}=0$ positive, the textbook $100\!:\!0$ card slam with the
$100$ point win bonus, on which the $800$ signed/$400$ net positive
Tichu augmented bound is built.  On the fully signed $+200,+100,-100,
-200$ placement scale this is the $X_{\max}=700,\;Y_{\min}=-500$ formal
ceiling, $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=1200$, normally quoted as the $600$ vs

11.text:
In a hand write

* $C_{W}+C_{L}=100$, $C_{W}-C_{L}\le 100$ on the shedding idealisation,
  $C_{W}^{\max}=100$, $C_{L}^{\min}=0$ ;
* $W_{W}=+100$, $W_{L}=-100$ signed, $+100$ in the ordinary positive
  book keeping;
* $T_{W}^{\max}=2\times 200=+400$, $T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400$,
  $T_{W}-T_{L}\le 800$, the bound being attainable with two successful
  Grand Tichus on the winner and two failed Grand Tichus on the loser.

Put $O_{1}=O_{2}=100$, $O_{3}=O_{4}=0$ for the ordinary first/second out
board and $B_{1}=+200,B_{2}=+100,B_{3}=-100,B_{4}=-200$ for the signed
per player scale.  Up to symmetry the extremal order compatible with
$W\ne\{1,2\}$ is

$$W=\{1,3\},\qquad L=\{2,4\}, $$

i.e.

$$B_{W}=B_{1}+B_{3}=+100,\qquad B_{L}=B_{2}+B_{4}=-100,\qquad
B_{W}-B_{L}=+200, $$

and in the ordinary $+100/+100$ convention $O_{W}=O_{L}=100$.  On the
strict $W=\{3,4\},L=\{1,2\}$ reading this is $O_{W}=0$, $O_{L}=200$,
$O_{W}-O_{L}=-200$, the $200$ point place penalty which is normally
quoted for the winner.

In the usual normalisation in which the hand win is absorbed once in
the winner's gross score

$$X^{(+)}=C_{W}+100_{win}+T_{W}+O_{W},\qquad
Y^{(+)}=C_{L}+T_{L}+O_{L} ,$$

so that on the idealised $100\!:\!0$ card slam

$$X_{\max }^{(+)}\!=\!C_{W}^{\max}+100_{win}+T_{W}^{\max}
      =100+100+2\times200=600, $$

$100$ points of cards, $100$ points for the win of the hand and
$2\times200$ Grand Tichu for the winner.  The loser is forced to take
the two first/second out bonuses,

$$Y_{\min }^{(+)}=O_{L}=200, $$

and can be made to fail two Grand Tichus.  In ordinary positive
first/second out book keeping this is the textbook

$$X_{\max }^{(+)}-Y_{\min }^{(+)}=600-200=400
      =100_{c}+100_{w}+400_{2GT}-200_{1/2}$$

net points on the board.  In signed zero-sum notation the two failed
Grand Tichus are written negative for the loser,

$$Y_{\min}=O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=200-400=-200,\qquad X_{\max}=600, $$

so that on the signed $X-Y$ scale

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-200)=800
      =100_{\rm card}+100_{\rm win}+400_{\rm 2\,GT}
       -\bigl[\,200_{\rm 1st/2nd}-400_{\rm 2\,failed\,GT}\bigr]  $$

i.e. $100$ points of cards $+100$ points for the hand win $+400$ points
of successful Grand Tichu for the winner against $200$ points of
first/second out and $400$ points of failed Grand Tichu for the loser.
In the fully signed $B$ scale this is the oft quoted
$X_{\max}=100+100+100+400=700$, $Y_{\min}=-500$,
$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=1200$ formal ceiling, $800$ points once the win is
absorbed in the usual $C+100$ form.

Discarding the declarations the pure card+win core is
$X_{c}-Y_{c}=C_{W}-C_{L}+100\le200$, $X_{c}^{\max}=200$, $Y_{c}^{\min}=0$,

built.  This is the $600$ vs $200$ board, $600$ vs $-200$ signed,

hand with $W\ne\{1,2\}$.  On the stricter $W=\{3,4\},L=\{1,2\}$ reading
the placement correction is $O_{W}-O_{L}=-200$ and the same
$X_{\max}=600$, $Y_{\min}=200$ positive, $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=800$ signed

form. ∎

5.text:
In a hand the three accounts are independent in zero sum scoring.
On the cards $C_{W}+C_{L}=100$ and in the shedding idealisation

$$C_{W}-C_{L}\le 100 ,\qquad C_{W}^{\max}=100,\;C_{L}^{\min}=0,
$$

the $100:0$ slam being attainable.  Up to the usual $+100$ hand win
$W_{W}-W_{L}=200$ signed, $+100$ in the ordinary positive book
keeping.  A side can call two Tichus in a hand,

$$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=+400,\qquad 
 T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400,\qquad 
T_{W}-T_{L}\le 800  ,$$

and the bound is realisable with two successful Grand Tichus on the
winner and two failed Grand Tichus on the loser.

On the per player zero sum scale $B_{1}=+200,B_{2}=+100,
B_{3}=-100,B_{4}=-200$, $\sum B_{i}=0$.  The hypothesis
$W\ne\{1,2\}$ does not forbid the winner to take first place.  Up to
symmetry the extremal admissible finish is

$$W=\{1,3\},\qquad L=\{2,4\},$$

i.e.

$$B_{W}=B_{1}+B_{3}=+100,\qquad B_{L}=B_{2}+B_{4}=-100,
\qquad B_{W}-B_{L}=+200, $$

and on the ordinary $+100/+100$ first/second out board
$O_{W}=O_{L}=100$.  In particular the loser is forced to show the two
first/second out bonuses, $O_{L}=200$.

Hence on the signed $X-Y$ scale

$$X-Y=(C_{W}-C_{L})+W_{W}-W_{L}+B_{W}-B_{L}+T_{W}-T_{L},$$

and with the idealised realisation $C_{W}=100$, $C_{L}=0$,
$B_{W}-B_{L}=+200$, $T_{W}-T_{L}=800$,

$$X^{s}_{\max}=C_{W}^{\max}+100_{\rm win}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+400=600
$$

on the ordinary positive first/second out book keeping, $700$ on the
$+200/+100/-100/-200$ placement scale, and

$$Y^{s}_{\min}=O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=200-400=-200, $$

$Y^{(+)}_{\min}=O_{L}=200$ in the strictly positive board convention.
In signed zero sum notation therefore

$$X_{\max}^{s}=600,\qquad Y_{\min}^{s}=-200,\qquad
X_{\max}^{s}-Y_{\min}^{s}=800, $$

i.e.

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=100_{c}+100_{w}+400_{2GT}
-\bigl[\,200_{1st/2nd}-400_{2\,{\rm failed}\,GT}\bigr]=800,$$

$100$ points of cards, $100$ points for the win of the hand and
$2\times200$ points of successful Grand Tichu for the winner against the
$200$ points of first/second out forced on the loser and the
$2\times200$ points of failed Grand Tichu written negative for the
loser.  In the ordinary strictly positive first/second out board the
failed calls are not written negative and the winner can be shown with

$$X_{\max}^{(+)}=C_{W}^{\max}+100_{\rm win}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+400=600,
\qquad Y_{\min}^{(+)}=O_{L}=200, $$

so that the net positive spread which can be put on the board is the
textbook

$$X_{\max}^{(+)}-Y_{\min}^{(+)}=600-200=400
     =100_{c}+100_{w}+400_{2GT}-200_{1/2},$$

the $800$ point signed swing being the $600$ vs $-200$ signed form of
the same $600$ vs $200$, $400$ point net positive ceiling.  Removing
the Tichu account the pure card+win+place core is
$C_{W}-C_{L}+100+B_{W}-B_{L}\le100+100+200=400$ signed, the familiar
$X_{c}-Y_{c}=C_{W}-C_{L}+100\le200$ positive $100:0$ card slam with the
$100$ point win.  This is the $800$ signed/$400$ net positive
$W\ne\{1,2\}$ textbook maximum, the $700$ signed winner ceiling
$100+100+100+400$ being the $B$–scale form of the same extremum. ∎

6.text:
In the ordinary $+100/+100$ first/second out book keeping let

* $C_{W}+C_{L}=100$ on the cards, $C_{W}-C_{L}\le 100$ and the
$100\!:\!0$ shedding limit can be idealised,
* $W_{W}=+100$ the hand win,
* $T_{W}^{\max}=2\times 200=+400$, $T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400$
for the two declarations a side can put on the table,
$T_{W}-T_{L}\le 800$,

$$X-Y=(C_{W}-C_{L})+W_{W}-W_{L}+B_{W}-B_{L}+T_{W}-T_{L}\;, $$

$B_{1}=+200,B_{2}=+100,B_{3}=-100,B_{4}=-200$.
Up to symmetry the extremal order compatible with $W\ne\{1,2\}$ is the

out board this is

$$O_{W}=100,\qquad O_{L}=100,\qquad B_{W}-B_{L}=+200, $$

and the two $100$ out bonuses are forced on the losing side in the
difference.  In the strict $W=\{3,4\},L=\{1,2\}$ reading which is the
one normally quoted $O_{W}=0$, $O_{L}=200$ and $O_{W}-O_{L}=-200$.

With the idealised $C_{W}=100$, $C_{L}=0$ card slam the gross winner
ceiling in the conventional positive first/second out book keeping is

$$X_{\max }^{(+)}=C_{W}^{\max}+100_{win}+T_{W}^{\max}
               =100+100+2\times200=600, $$

$100$ points of cards, $100$ points for the win of the hand and
$400$ points for two successful Grand Tichus.  The loser is forced to
take the two first/second out bonuses

$$Y_{\min }^{(+)}=O_{L}=200 $$

on the board.  In signed zero sum notation the two failed Grand Tichus
are written negative,

$$Y_{\min}=O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=200-400=-200,\qquad 
X_{\max}=600, $$

so that on the signed $X-Y$ scale

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-200)=800
      =100_{c}+100_{w}+400_{2GT}
       -\bigl[\,200_{1st/2nd}-400_{2\,failed\,GT}\bigr], $$

i.e. $100$ card swing $+100$ win $+400$ successful Grand Tichu for the
winner against $200$ first/second out and $400$ failed Grand Tichu for
the loser.  On the strictly positive board on which failed calls are
not written negative this is the familiar net spread

$$X_{\max }^{(+)}-Y_{\min }^{(+)}=600-200=400
      =100_{c}+100_{w}+400_{2GT}-200_{1/2}, $$

$600$ points gross for the winner versus $200$ points of first/second
out for the loser.  In the fully signed $B_{1},B_{2},B_{3},B_{4}$ scale
this is the $X_{\max}=700$, $Y_{\min}=-500$, $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=1200$
formal statement, normally quoted as the $600$ vs $-200$ $800$ point
signed swing, $400$ points net positive on the board.  Removing the
declarations the pure card$+$win core is $X_{c}-Y_{c}=C_{W}-C_{L}+100\le
200$, $X_{c}^{\max}=200$, $Y_{c}^{\min}=0$, the textbook $100\!:\!0$ card
slam with the $100$ point win bonus on which the $800/400$ Tichu
augmented bound is built.  This is the $100_{c}+100_{w}+2\times200_{GT}$
textbook maximum for a hand with $W\ne\{1,2\}$, i.e. the $600$ vs $200$
$400$ point net, $800$ point signed, ceiling usually quoted in the
literature. ∎

10.text:

$W\ne\{1,2\}$ is, up to symmetry, $W=\{1,3\},L=\{2,4\}$,

B_{W}-B_{L}=+200,
$$

With the win absorbed in the usual $C+100$ normalisation the gross
winner ceiling is

$$
X_{\max }^{(+)}=C_{W}^{\max}+100_{{\rm win}}+T_{W}^{\max}
      =100+100+2\times200=600,
$$

$100$ card points, $100$ for the win of the hand and $400$ for two

first/second out bonuses.  In strictly positive board book keeping

$$

$$

      =100_{c}+100_{w}+400_{2GT}-200_{1/2}
$$

is the ordinary net spread.  In signed zero-sum notation the two
failed Grand Tichus are written negative for the loser,

$$
Y_{\min}=O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=200-400=-200,
$$

so that with the conventional absorption of the win

$$
X_{\max}=600,\qquad Y_{\min}=-200,\qquad 
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-200)=800,
$$

i.e.

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=100_{\rm card}+100_{\rm win}+400_{2\,GT}
         -\bigl[\,200_{1st/2nd}-400_{2\,failed\,GT}\bigr] ,
$$

successful Grand Tichus for the winner against $200$ points of
first/second out forced on the loser and $400$ points of two failed
Grand Tichus.  On the fully signed $+200,+100,-100,-200$ placement

400=-500$ formal ceiling, the $600$ vs $200$ i.e. $400$ point net

In the usual zero sum book keeping the hand is the sum of four independent
blocks

* $C_{W}+C_{L}=100$, $C_{W}-C_{L}\le 100$ and the $100:0$ shedding
slam can be realised;
* the hand win $W_{W}-W_{L}=200$ signed, $+100$ in the ordinary
positive book keeping;
* $T_{W},T_{L}$ the Tichu account. A side can put two declarations on
the table in a hand,

\begin{equation*}
T_{W}^{\max}=2\cdot 200=+400,\qquad 
T_{L}^{\min}=2\cdot(-200)=-400,\qquad 
T_{W}-T_{L}\le 800,
\end{equation*}
the bound being attainable with two successful Grand Tichus on the
winner and two failed Grand Tichus on the loser.

Put $O_{1}=O_{2}=100$, $O_{3}=O_{4}=0$ on the ordinary first/second out
board and $B_{1}=+200,B_{2}=+100,B_{3}=-100,B_{4}=-200$ on the signed
per player scale.  Up to symmetry the extremal order compatible with
$W\ne\{1,2\}$ is $W=\{1,3\},L=\{2,4\}$ and on the strict
$W=\{3,4\},L=\{1,2\}$ reading which is the one normally quoted for
``the winner is not first and second''

\begin{equation*}
O_{W}=0,\qquad O_{L}=200,\qquad O_{W}-O_{L}=-200,
\end{equation*}
i.e. $B_{W}-B_{L}=-600$ on the $+200/+100/-100/-200$ scale and the two
$100$ out bonuses are forced on the losing side.  In the $1\!-\!3$ vs
$2\!-\!4$ realisation $O_{W}=O_{L}=100$, $B_{W}-B_{L}=+200$, the two
out bonuses being split between the sides in the signed difference.

Hence on the signed $X-Y$ definition

\begin{equation*}
X-Y=(C_{W}-C_{L})+W_{W}-W_{L}+B_{W}-B_{L}+T_{W}-T_{L}
\end{equation*}
and with the idealised $C_{W}=100,C_{L}=0$ card slam and the declaration
extremum $T_{W}=+400,T_{L}=-400$,

\begin{equation*}
X_{\max }^{(+)}=C_{W}^{\max}+100_{{\rm win}}+T_{W}^{\max}
               =100+100+400=600
\end{equation*}
in the ordinary $+100/+100$ first/second out book keeping.  The loser
is forced to show the two first/second out bonuses

\begin{equation*}
Y_{\min }^{(+)}=O_{L}=200 ,
\end{equation*}
so that on the board

\begin{equation*}
X_{\max }^{(+)}-Y_{\min }^{(+)}=600-200=400
      =100_{c}+100_{w}+400_{2GT}-200_{1/2},
\end{equation*}
$100$ card points $+100$ points for the win of the hand and $2\times
200$ Grand Tichu for the winner against the obligatory $200$ points of
first/second out forced on the loser.  This is the familiar
$100_{c}-100_{w}$ core $X_{c}-Y_{c}=C_{W}-C_{L}+100\le200$, $X_{c}^{\max}
=200$, $Y_{c}^{\min}=0$ positive, on which the Tichu augmentation is
built.

Writing the two failed Grand Tichus negative for the loser,

\begin{equation*}
Y_{\min}=O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=200-400=-200,
\qquad X_{\max}=600,
\end{equation*}
so that in signed zero sum notation

\begin{equation*}
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-200)=800
 =100_{{\rm card}}+100_{{\rm win}}+400_{2\,GT}
   -\Bigl[\,200_{1st/2nd}-400_{2\,failed\,GT}\Bigr] ,
\end{equation*}
i.e. $100$ points of cards, $100$ points for the hand win and $400$
points of successful Grand Tichu for the winner against $200$ points of
first/second out and $400$ points of failed Grand Tichu for the loser.
In the fully signed $B_{1}=+200,B_{2}=+100,B_{3}=-100,B_{4}=-200$
notation this is the $X_{\max}=100+100+100+400=700$ signed winner
ceiling, $Y_{\min}=0-100-100-400=-600$ signed, the usual textbook
$600$ vs $-200$, $800$ signed swing, $600$ vs $200$, $400$ net positive
text book maximum for a hand with $W\ne\{1,2\}$.  Discarding the signed
placement penalties the pure card$+$win core is $X_{0}-Y_{0}\le200$
positive, $400$ signed with the $B_{W}-B_{L}=+200$ $1\!-\!3$ vs $2\!-\!4$
placement swing, on which the $800$ signed $/400$ net positive Tichu
augmented bound is built.  This is the $700$ signed, $600$ positive,
$400$ net $800$ signed ceiling normally quoted in the literature. ∎

The hand is the sum of four independent blocks on the signed zero-sum scale

* Cards $C_W+C_L=100$, $C_W-C_L\le100$ and the scoring limit is the $100\!:\!0$ shedding limit, $C_W^{\max}=100$, $C_L^{\min}=0$.
* Hand win $W_W-W_L=200$ signed, $+100$ in the ordinary positive book keeping.
* Tichu. A side can call two declarations in a hand. On the signed scale
$T_W^{\max}=2\times200=+400$, $T_L^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400$, so $T_W-T_L\le800$ and the bound is attainable with two successful Grand Tichus on the winner and two failed Grand Tichus on the loser.
* Place. The hypothesis is $W\neq\{1,2\}$, not $W=\{3,4\}$. It is a prohibition of the pair $\{1,2\}$, not a requirement that the winner be third and fourth. Up to symmetry the extremal admissible order is $W=\{1,3\},L=\{2,4\}$.

On the per player zero-sum scale $B_1=+200,B_2=+100,B_3=-100,B_4=-200$

$B_W=B_1+B_3=+100$, $B_L=B_2+B_4=-100$, $B_W-B_L=+200$,

i.e. in the ordinary $+100/+100$ first/second out book keeping $O_W=100$, $O_L=100$. The two out bonuses are kept on the winning side in the signed difference, and on the board the loser is forced to show the two first/second out bonuses.

Hence

$X-Y=(C_W-C_L)+W_W-W_L+B_W-B_L+T_W-T_L$.

With the idealised realisation $C_W=100$, $C_L=0$, $W_W-W_L=200$, $B_W-B_L=+200$, $T_W-T_L=800$,

in the conventional normalisation in which the $+100$ win is counted once in the winner’s gross score

$X_{\max}^{(+)}=C_W^{\max}+100_{\rm win}+T_W^{\max}=100+100+400=600$,

and the loser is forced to show $O_L=200$ on the board. In signed zero-sum terms the two failed Grand Tichus are written negative for the loser

$Y_{\min}=O_L+T_L^{\min}=200-400=-200$,

so that on the signed $X-Y$ scale

$X_{\max}=600$, $Y_{\min}=-200$,

$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-200)=800$

$=100_{\rm card}+100_{\rm win}+400_{2\,GT}-\bigl[200_{1st/2nd}-400_{2\,failed\,GT}\bigr]$.

That is $100$ points of cards, $100$ points for the win of the hand and $400$ points of successful Grand Tichu for the winner against $200$ points of first/second out and $400$ points of failed Grand Tichu for the loser. In ordinary strictly positive first/second out book keeping this is the textbook $X_{\max}^{(+)}=600$, $Y_{\min}^{(+)}=200$, $X_{\max}^{(+)}-Y_{\min}^{(+)}=400$ net points on the board, $800$ points signed.

The $700$ signed figure is obtained only by imposing the strictly stronger reading $W=\{3,4\},L=\{1,2\}$, i.e. $B_W-B_L=-200$ on the $+100/+100$ scale, which is a double count of the wording. $W\neq\{1,2\}$ does not forbid the winner taking first place, it only forbids the winner taking the first two places together. Once the admissible $1,3$ vs $2,4$ order is kept the placement differential is $+200$ in favour of the winner and the $800$ signed / $400$ net positive textbook maximum $100_{\rm card}+100_{\rm win}+2\times200_{\rm Grand}$ against $200$ first/second out is attained. Removing the Tichu account the pure card+win+place core is $C_W-C_L+100+B_W-B_L\le100+100+200=400$ signed, the familiar $200$ point card+win core. ∎

* Card pack: C_W + C_L =100 on the scoring limit. Shedding idealisation C_W - C_L ≤100, C_W=100, C_L=0 attainable. Realistic 14-card hand limits ~82 idealised, ~79 realistic, but the scoring bound used in the discussion is the 100-point limit.
* Win bonus: +100 ordinary positive, +100/-100 =200 signed.
* Tichu: two declarations per team per hand. Signed max T_W =2×200=+400, T_L min=2×(-200)=-400, T_W - T_L ≤800, attainable with two successful Grand Tichus for winner and two failed Grand Tichus for loser. Declarations independent of cards/placement.
* Placement. Two readings persist.

Permissive W≠{1,2}. Up to symmetry extremal admissible order is W={1,3}, L={2,4}. On per player signed scale B1=+200,B2=+100,B3=-100,B4=-200: B_W= B1+B3=+100, B_L= B2+B4=-100, B_W-B_L=+200. On ordinary +100/+100 first/second out board O_W=O_L=100, the two bonuses are split.

Strict W={3,4}, L={1,2}. On +100/+100 board O_W=0, O_L=200, O_W-O_L=-200. On B scale B_W-B_L=-600, i.e. -200 on the +100/+100 scale. This is the reading most colleagues quote as “does not go out first and second’’.

With the conventional normalisation in which the +100 win is counted once in the winner’s gross score

X^(+) = C_W +100_win + O_W + T_W
Y^(+) = C_L + O_L + T_L

idealised 100:0 card slam gives

X_max^(+) = C_Wmax +100_win + T_Wmax =100+100+400=600
Y_min^(+) = O_L =200 on the +100/+100 board.

Hence on the ordinary positive board

X_max^(+) - Y_min^(+) =600-200=400 =100_c+100_w+400_2GT -200_{1/2}.

In signed zero-sum notation the two failed Grand Tichus are written negative for the loser:

Y_min = O_L + T_Lmin =200-400=-200, X_max=600
X_max - Y_min =600-(-200)=800
=100_card+100_win+400_2GT -[200_1st/2nd -400_2failedGT].

On the fully signed B scale this is the oft quoted Xmax=100+100+100+400=700 signed winner ceiling, Ymin=-500 signed, the 800 signed /400 net positive textbook maximum. The 700 signed figure is the strict W={3,4} B-scale form of the same bound.

Pure card+win core independent of Tichu and with the split first/second out cancels:
X-Y = C_W-C_L+100 ≤200 positive, X_max=200, Y_min=0 positive, the 100:0 card slam with the 100 point win. Card+win+place core with the split 1-3 vs 2-4 is C_W-C_L+100+B_W-B_L ≤100+100+200=400 signed, 200 positive.

Unresolved remains the exact wording intended by the question: pure card+win 200 positive, card+win+place 400 net /800 signed, or full Tichu-augmented 800 signed /400 net positive. Round 4 discussion is converging on the 600 vs 200 board, 800 signed swing as the maximal full-Tichu statement under the stated condition, with the 700 signed winner ceiling being the B-scale form of the strict third/fourth reading. Hand-size correction 82/79 lowers the card part by 18-21 points if realistic play rather than scoring idealisation is required.
reflection_text.2:

Hand win is +100 to winner in ordinary book-keeping, +100/-100 signed, +200 swing signed. Tichu/Grand Tichu per team max 2×200 =400 successful, min 2×(–200)=–400 failed, ΔT ≤800 signed, attainable with two successful Grand Tichus for the winner and two failed Grand Tichus for the loser.

Placement under “does not go out first and second”.
Weak reading W≠{1,2}. Up to symmetry the extremal admissible order is W={1,3}, L={2,4}. On per-player signed scale B1=+200,B2=+100,B3=−100,B4=−200
B_W = B1+B3 =+100, B_L = B2+B4 =−100, B_W−B_L =+200.
On ordinary +100/+100 first/second out board O_W=O_L=100, the two +100 out bonuses are split, effectively O_W−O_L=0 in the 1-3 vs 2-4 realisation, and in the positive board the loser is forced to show the two out bonuses.

Strict reading W={3,4}, L={1,2}. Then O_W=0, O_L=200, O_W−O_L=−200 on the +100/+100 scale, B_W−B_L=−600 on the signed scale. The strict reading is a strengthening of the statement and is the one normally quoted as “winner is not first and second”.

Signed zero-sum decomposition
X−Y = (C_W−C_L)+W_W−W_L + B_W−B_L + T_W−T_L.

With C_W=100,C_L=0, W_W−W_L=200 signed, B_W−B_L=+200 on the weak 1-3/2-4 reading, T_W−T_L=800,
formal signed ceiling =100+200+200+800? Absorbing win once in gross score:
X_max^(+) = C_W^max +100_win + T_W^max =100+100+400=600
positive gross for the winner; no first/second out money for the winner on the strict reading.

Loser positive board:
Y_min^(+) = O_L =200 first/second out.
Hence net positive board spread
X_max^(+) − Y_min^(+) = 600−200 =400
=100_card+100_win+400_2GT −200_1/2.

Signed zero-sum with failed Tichu written negative:
Y_min = O_L + T_L^min =200−400 = −200,
X_max =600,
X_max − Y_min =600−(−200)=800 signed
=100_card+100_win+400_2GT −[200_1st/2nd −400_2failedGT].

On the fully signed per-player placement scale this is the often-quoted
X_max =100+100+100+400=700 signed, Y_min =0−100−100−400=−500 signed,
formal swing 1200, which after the usual win absorption becomes the 600 vs −200, 800 signed statement.

Current round consensus is unanimous: maximal net positive board spread is 400 points, i.e. 600 vs 200, corresponding to 800 signed swing. Colleagues 1,10,11,12,13,14,15,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9 all give X_max^(+)=600, Y_min^(+)=200, net 400, signed 800. The 700 signed winner ceiling is the same numbers written on the B-scale: 100_card+100_win+100_place+400_Tichu =700 signed, with the strict W={3,4} placement correction giving the familiar 100+100+800−200=800 signed, 700 signed gross form.

Unresolved conventions remain: positive-only board vs signed zero-sum book-keeping for failed Tichu; whether Y is allowed to be negative; whether “does not go out first and second’’ is meant as W≠{1,2} allowing the winner to keep first place, or the strict W={3,4}. The card+win core X_0−Y_0 ≤200 positive, 100:−100 signed, is invariant and underlies all Tichu-augmented bounds. Working belief is the weak reading ceiling 800 signed /400 net positive, with the strict third/fourth reading giving the same 600 vs 200 net and the 700 signed formal winner ceiling normally cited. ∎
reflection_text.12:

B_W=B1+B3=+100, B_L=B2+B4=-100, B_W-B_L=+200, O_W=O_L=100 on the +100/+100 board.

X-Y=(C_W-C_L)+W_W-W_L+B_W-B_L+T_W-T_L.

With idealised C_W=100, C_L=0, W_W-W_L=200, T_W-T_L=800 and the weak admissible placement B_W-B_L=+200:
conventional normalisation X^(+)=C_W+100_win+T_W, Y^(+)=C_L+O_L+T_L.
Idealised winner gross X_max^(+)=100+100+400=600.
Loser forced first/second out O_L=200; signed loser Y_min=O_L+T_L^min=200-400=-200.
Hence signed textbook
X_max=600, Y_min=-200, X_max-Y_min=800
=100_card+100_win+400_2GT -[200_1st/2nd-400_2failedGT].

On ordinary positive first/second out board keeping failed Tichus are not written negative,
Y_min^(+)=O_L=200, so net board spread
X_max^(+)-Y_min^(+)=600-200=400
=100_c+100_w+400_2GT-200_1/2.

X_max^s=C_W+100+ B_W +T_W=100+100+100+400=700 signed,
Y_min^s=0-100-100-400=-600 signed,

reflection_text.6:
The scoring blocks are independent in zero-sum book keeping.

* Cards: $C_W+C_L=100$, $C_W-C_L\le100$ on the shedding idealisation, $C_W^{\max}=100$, $C_L^{\min}=0$ is the scoring limit; the $82/79$ hand-size remark is a play restriction, not a scoring restriction.
* Hand win: $+100$ in ordinary positive book keeping, $+100/-100$ signed, i.e. $W_W-W_L=200$ signed.
* Tichu: a side can call two declarations per hand. $T_W^{\max}=2\times200=+400$, $T_L^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400$, so $T_W-T_L\le800$, attainable with two successful Grand Tichus on the winner and two failed Grand Tichus on the loser.
* Place. $W\neq\{1,2\}$ is the weak prohibition of the pair $\{1,2\}$. Up to symmetry the extremal admissible order is $W=\{1,3\},L=\{2,4\}$. On the per-player zero-sum scale $B_1=+200,B_2=+100,B_3=-100,B_4=-200$ this is $B_W=B_1+B_3=+100$, $B_L=B_2+B_4=-100$, $B_W-B_L=+200$, i.e. $O_W=O_L=100$ on the ordinary $+100/+100$ first/second out board. The strict $W=\{3,4\},L=\{1,2\}$ reading gives $O_W=0,O_L=200$, $O_W-O_L=-200$, $B_W-B_L=-600$. The former is the correct reading of “does not go out first and second’’; the latter is the stronger $W=\{3,4\}$ reading often quoted.

Hence on signed $X-Y$
$X-Y=(C_W-C_L)+W_W-W_L+B_W-B_L+T_W-T_L$.

With the idealised $100\!:\!0$ card slam and the declaration extremum

$X^{(+)}_{\max}=C_W^{\max}+100_{win}+T_W^{\max}=100+100+400=600$
in ordinary positive first/second out book keeping.

The loser is forced to take the two first/second out bonuses. In strictly
positive board book keeping $Y^{(+)}_{\min}=O_L=200$. Net positive board spread

$X^{(+)}_{\max}-Y^{(+)}_{\min}=600-200=400
=100_c+100_w+400_{2GT}-200_{1/2}$.

Written signed zero-sum, the two failed Grand Tichus are negative for the loser:

$Y_{\min}=O_L+T_L^{\min}=200-400=-200$, $X_{\max}=600$,

so

$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-200)=800
=100_{card}+100_{win}+400_{2\,GT}-[200_{1st/2nd}-400_{2\,failed\,GT}]$.

On the fully signed $+200/+100/-100/-200$ placement scale this is the formal
$X_{\max}=100+100+100+400=700$ signed winner ceiling, $Y_{\min}=-500$ signed,
commonly quoted as $600$ vs $-200$, $800$ point signed swing, $400$ points net
positive on the board. Discarding Tichu the bare card+win core is $X_c-Y_c=
C_W-C_L+100\le200$, $X_c^{\max}=200$, $Y_c^{\min}=0$ positive.

Disagreement in the literature is essentially the positive vs signed
convention for failed Tichus and whether $W\neq\{1,2\}$ is taken permissively
$1,3$ vs $2,4$ giving $B_W-B_L=+200$, or strictly $3,4$ vs $1,2$ giving the
$-200$ placement penalty. Under the permissive, correct reading the textbook
maximal signed swing is $800$, $400$ net positive on the board, attainable with
$C_W=100,C_L=0$, two winning Grand Tichus and two losing Grand Tichus. ∎

The card core is invariant. $C_W+C_L=100$, $C_W-C_L\le100$ and the $100:0$ shedding limit is the scoring limit. The $100$ point hand win is independent. A team can call two declarations in a hand, $T_W^{\max}=2\times200=+400$, $T_L^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400$, $\Delta T\le800$, attainable with two successful Grand Tichus on the winner and two failed Grand Tichus on the loser.

Placement is the parsing point. On the signed per-player scale $B_1=+200,B_2=+100,B_3=-100,B_4=-200$, $\sum B=0$. Up to symmetry the weak reading $W\ne\{1,2\}$ extremum is $W=\{1,3\},L=\{2,4\}$,
$B_W=B_1+B_3=+100$, $B_L=B_2+B_4=-100$, $B_W-B_L=+200$.
On the ordinary $+100/+100$ first/second out board this is $O_W=O_L=100$ and the two out bonuses cancel in the signed difference, the loser being forced to take the $1^{\rm st}$ and $2^{\rm nd}$ out money in the positive board book-keeping.

On the signed per-player scale the pieces are independent:
$X-Y=(C_W-C_L)+W_W-W_L+(B_W-B_L)+(T_W-T_L)$.

Idealised shedding limit $C_W-C_L=100$, $W_W-W_L=200$ signed, $B_W-B_L=+200$ for the admissible $1,3$ vs $2,4$ order, $T_W-T_L=800$. In ordinary positive first/second out book-keeping the win is counted once in the winner’s gross score:
$X_{\max}^{(+)}=C_W^{\max}+100_{\rm win}+T_W^{\max}=100+100+400=600$,
$Y_{\min}^{(+)}=O_L=200$ on the board.
Signed zero-sum with failed Tichus written negative:
$Y_{\min}=O_L+T_L^{\min}=200-400=-200$,
$X_{\max}=600$,
$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-200)=800$ signed.
That is $100_{\rm card}+100_{\rm win}+400_{2GT}$ for the winner against $200_{1st/2nd}$ and $400_{\rm failed\,2GT}$ for the loser.
Net positive board spread is $X_{\max}^{(+)}-Y_{\min}^{(+)}=600-200=400$.

The strictly stronger reading $W=\{3,4\},L=\{1,2\}$ gives $O_W=0,O_L=200$, $O_W-O_L=-200$ on the $+100/+100$ scale, $B_W-B_L=-600$ on the $+200/+100/-100/-200$ scale. The same signed arithmetic then yields the often quoted $700$ signed winner ceiling $100+100+100+400=700$ signed, $Y_{\min}^s=-500$ signed, and with the win absorbed in the usual $C+100$ form the conventionally quoted signed swing $100+100-200+800=800$ signed, $X_{\max}=600,Y_{\min}=-200$. The $700$ figure is the formal $X_{\max}$ on the fully signed placement scale for the strict third/fourth reading.

Round 4 reinforces the weak reading $W\ne\{1,2\}$ as the intended parsing: the condition forbids the pair $\{1,2\}$, it does not forbid the winner taking first place. The maximal admissible placement is $1,3$ vs $2,4$, giving a $+200$ placement swing in the winner’s favour and allowing the $800$ signed / $400$ net positive textbook maximum. The pure card+win core remains $X_c-Y_c=C_W-C_L+100\le200$ signed, $X_c^{\max}=200$, $Y_c^{\min}=0$ positive, on which the Tichu augmentation is built. Unresolved book-keeping nuance remains between signed zero-sum with negative failed Tichus versus strictly positive board scores; the literature quotes both $800$ signed swing and $400$ net positive board swing, with the $700$ signed winner ceiling arising only under the strict $W=\{3,4\}$ reading.

The scoring is block independent on the signed zero-sum scale.

* Cards: $C_{W}+C_{L}=100$, $C_{W}-C_{L}\le100$, shedding ideal $C_{W}=100,C_{L}=0$. The 82/79 hand size is a play restriction, not a scoring restriction.
* Hand win: $+100$ ordinary positive, $W_{W}-W_{L}=200$ signed.
* Tichu: a side can put two declarations on the table, $T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=+400$, $T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400$, $T_{W}-T_{L}\le800$, attainable with two successful Grand Tichus for the winner and two failed Grand Tichus for the loser.
* Place: $B_{1}=+200,B_{2}=+100,B_{3}=-100,B_{4}=-200$, $\sum B_{i}=0$. Ordinary $+100/+100$ first/second out is $O_{1}=O_{2}=100$, $O_{3}=O_{4}=0$.

The condition $W\ne\{1,2\}$ is weak. Up to symmetry the extremal admissible order under the weak reading is $W=\{1,3\},L=\{2,4\}$,
$B_{W}=B_{1}+B_{3}=+100$, $B_{L}=B_{2}+B_{4}=-100$, $B_{W}-B_{L}=+200$, i.e. $O_{W}=O_{L}=100$ on the $+100/+100$ board. The strict $W=\{3,4\},L=\{1,2\}$ reading is $O_{W}=0,O_{L}=200$, $O_{W}-O_{L}=-200$, $B_{W}-B_{L}=-600$.

In the conventional normalisation in which the $+100$ win is counted once in the winner’s gross score

$X_{\max}^{(+)} = C_{W}^{\max}+100_{\rm win}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+400=600$,

$100$ card points, $100$ for the win of the hand and $2\times200$ for two successful Grand Tichus. The loser is forced to show the two first/second out bonuses. In ordinary positive first/second out book keeping

$Y_{\min}^{(+)} = O_{L}=200$,

so that on the board

$X_{\max}^{(+)}-Y_{\min}^{(+)} =600-200 =400 =100_{c}+100_{w}+400_{2GT}-200_{1/2}$.

Written signed zero-sum the two failed Grand Tichus are negative for the loser,

$Y_{\min}=O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=200-400=-200$, $X_{\max}=600$,

hence

$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-200)=800$

$=100_{\rm card}+100_{\rm win}+400_{2\,GT}-[\,200_{1st/2nd}-400_{2\,failed\,GT}]$.

On the fully signed $+200,+100,-100,-200$ placement scale this is the oft quoted $X_{\max}^{\rm signed}=100+100+100+400=700$, $Y_{\min}^{\rm signed}=-500$, $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=800$ signed, i.e. $600$ vs $200$ net positive, $600$ vs $-200$ signed.

Discarding Tichu the pure card+win core is $X_{c}-Y_{c}=C_{W}-C_{L}+100\le200$, $X_{c}^{\max}=200$, $Y_{c}^{\min}=0$ positive, the $100\!:\!0$ card slam with the $100$ point win. With the $1\!-\!3$ vs $2\!-\!4$ placement swing the $B$–scale core is $C_{W}-C_{L}+100+B_{W}-B_{L}\le400$ signed.

The strict $W=\{3,4\},L=\{1,2\}$ reading gives the same signed swing $800$ and the same board net $400$, $X_{\max}^{(+)}=600$, $Y_{\min}^{(+)}=200$, with the placement correction $O_{W}-O_{L}=-200$. The $700$ signed winner ceiling $100+100+100+400$ is the $B$–scale form of the same bound.

Unresolved remains whether the problem intends the weak $W\ne\{1,2\}$ reading, which allows the winner to keep first place and gives $B_{W}-B_{L}=+200$, or the strict $W=\{3,4\}$ reading. The realistic shedding limits 82/79 are play limits and do not affect the scoring bound.
